4.s: atha śāktamupāyamaṇḍalaṃ kathayāmaḥ paramātmasaṃvide // 1
4.d: अथ शाक्तमुपायमण्डलं कथयामः परमात्मसंविदे ॥ 1
4.m: Now we explain the realm of the Śākta means for the realization of the supreme Self.

4.s:
anantarāhnikokte'sminsvabhāve pārameśvare /
pravivikṣurvikalpasya kuryātsaṃskāramañjasā // 2
4.d:
अनन्तराह्निकोक्तेऽस्मिन्स्वभावे पारमेश्वरे ।
प्रविविक्षुर्विकल्पस्य कुर्यात्संस्कारमञ्जसा ॥ 2
4.m: Wishing to enter into this essential nature belonging to the Supreme Lord, which was explained in the immediately preceding daily lesson, / one should straightway effect the refinement of conceptual construct.

4.s:
vikalpaḥ saṃskṛtaḥ sūte vikalpaṃ svātmasaṃskṛtam /
svatulyaṃ so'pi so'pyanyaṃ so'pyanyaṃ sadṛśātmakam // 3
4.d:
विकल्पः संस्कृतः सूते विकल्पं स्वात्मसंस्कृतम् ।
स्वतुल्यं सोऽपि सोऽप्यन्यं सोऽप्यन्यं सदृशात्मकम् ॥ 3
4.m: Refined conceptual construct generates another conceptual construct refined by its own nature / equal to itself; and that one too [generates] another, and that another, identical in kind.

4.s:
caturṣveva vikalpeṣu yaḥ saṃskāraḥ kramādasau /
asphuṭaḥ sphuṭatābhāvī prasphuṭansphuṭitātmakaḥ // 4
4.d:
चतुर्ष्वेव विकल्पेषु यः संस्कारः क्रमादसौ ।
अस्फुटः स्फुटताभावी प्रस्फुटन्स्फुटितात्मकः ॥ 4
4.m: Through just four conceptual constructs, this refinement proceeds in succession: / indistinct, becoming distinct, radiant, and fully unfolded;

4.s:
tataḥ sphuṭataro yāvadante sphuṭatamo bhavet /
asphuṭādau vikalpe ca bhedo'pyastyāntarālikaḥ // 5
4.d:
ततः स्फुटतरो यावदन्ते स्फुटतमो भवेत् ।
अस्फुटादौ विकल्पे च भेदोऽप्यस्त्यान्तरालिकः ॥ 5
4.m: from there, more distinct, until in the end it becomes most distinct; / and even in the indistinct and other conceptual constructs, there are intermediate differences.

4.s:
tataḥ sphuṭatamodāratādrūpyaparivṛṃhitā /
saṃvidabhyeti vimalāmavikalpasvarūpatām // 6
4.d:
ततः स्फुटतमोदारताद्रूप्यपरिवृंहिता ।
संविदभ्येति विमलामविकल्पस्वरूपताम् ॥ 6
4.m: Then, reinforced by that most distinct, sublime identity, / consciousness attains the spotless essential nature of the non-conceptual.

4.s:
ataśca bhairavīyaṃ yattejaḥ saṃvitsvabhāvakam /
bhūyo bhūyo vimṛśatāṃ jāyate tatsphuṭātmatā // 7
4.d:
अतश्च भैरवीयं यत्तेजः संवित्स्वभावकम् ।
भूयो भूयो विमृशतां जायते तत्स्फुटात्मता ॥ 7
4.m: Therefore, this splendor belonging to Bhairava, whose essential nature is consciousness, / becomes clearly manifest to those who contemplate it again and again.

4.s:
nanu saṃvitparāmraṣṭrī parāmarśamayī svataḥ /
parāmṛśyā kathaṃ tāthārūpyasṛṣṭau tu sā jaḍā // 8
4.d:
ननु संवित्पराम्रष्ट्री परामर्शमयी स्वतः ।
परामृश्या कथं ताथारूप्यसृष्टौ तु सा जडा ॥ 8
4.m: [Objection:] Surely, consciousness is inherently the grasper and consists of reflective awareness; / how can it be grasped? If an objective identity is created for it, it would be inert!

4.s:
ucyate svātmasaṃvittiḥ svabhāvādeva nirbharā /
nāsyāmapāsyaṃ nādheyaṃ kiṃcidityuditaṃ purā // 9
4.d:
उच्यते स्वात्मसंवित्तिः स्वभावादेव निर्भरा ।
नास्यामपास्यं नाधेयं किंचिदित्युदितं पुरा ॥ 9
4.m: [Reply:] It is taught: consciousness of one's own self is completely full by its very nature; / nothing is to be removed from it and nothing added, as was said before.

4.s:
kiṃ tu durghaṭakāritvātsvācchandyānnirmalādasau /
svātmapracchādanakrīḍāpaṇḍitaḥ parameśvaraḥ // 10
4.d:
किं तु दुर्घटकारित्वात्स्वाच्छन्द्यान्निर्मलादसौ ।
स्वात्मप्रच्छादनक्रीडापण्डितः परमेश्वरः ॥ 10
4.m: Yet, because He accomplishes the impossible, and through His immaculate absolute autonomy, / the Supreme Lord is skilled in the play of concealing His own nature.

4.s:
anāvṛtte svarūpe'pi yadātmācchādanaṃ vibhoḥ /
saiva māyā yato bheda etāvānviśvavṛttikaḥ // 11
4.d:
अनावृत्ते स्वरूपेऽपि यदात्माच्छादनं विभोः ।
सैव माया यतो भेद एतावान्विश्ववृत्तिकः ॥ 11
4.m: That which is the concealment of Himself by the omnipresent Lord, even though His nature is unconcealed, / is precisely māyā, from which arises this vast differentiation operating throughout the universe.

4.s:
tathābhāsanamevāsya dvaitamuktaṃ maheśituḥ /
taddvayāpāsanenāyaṃ parāmarśo'bhidhīyate // 12
4.d:
तथाभासनमेवास्य द्वैतमुक्तं महेशितुः ।
तद्द्वयापासनेनायं परामर्शोऽभिधीयते ॥ 12
4.m: Its very manifestation in such a manner has been called the duality of the Great Lord; / by casting off that duality, this reflective awareness is described.

4.s:
durbhedapādapasyāsya mūlaṃ kṛntanti kovidāḥ /
dhārārūḍhena sattarkakuṭhāreṇeti niścayaḥ // 13
4.d:
दुर्भेदपादपस्यास्य मूलं कृन्तन्ति कोविदाः ।
धारारूढेन सत्तर्ककुठारेणेति निश्चयः ॥ 13
4.m: The wise sever the root of this tree of hard-to-cut differentiation / with the sharp axe of right reasoning; such is the conclusion.

4.s:
tāmenāṃ bhāvanāmāhuḥ sarvakāmadughāṃ budhāḥ /
sphuṭayedvastu yāpetaṃ manosthapadādapi // 14
4.d:
तामेनां भावनामाहुः सर्वकामदुघां बुधाः ।
स्फुटयेद्वस्तु यापेतं मनोस्थपदादपि ॥ 14
4.m: The wise call this very thing creative contemplation, which yields all desires, / which can make evident even an object removed from the realm of the mind.

4.s:
śrīpūrvaśāstre tatproktaṃ tarko yogāṅgamuttamam /
heyādyālocanāttasmāttatra yatnaḥ praśasyate // 15
4.d:
श्रीपूर्वशास्त्रे तत्प्रोक्तं तर्को योगाङ्गमुत्तमम् ।
हेयाद्यालोचनात्तस्मात्तत्र यत्नः प्रशस्यते ॥ 15
4.m: In the venerable Pūrvaśāstra, it is said: 'Reasoning is the supreme limb of yoga.' / Because it discriminates what is to be abandoned and the like, effort in that regard is commended.

4.s:
mārge cetaḥ sthirībhūtaṃ heye'pi viṣayecchayā /
prerya tena nayettāvadyāvatpadamanāmayam // 16
4.d:
मार्गे चेतः स्थिरीभूतं हेयेऽपि विषयेच्छया ।
प्रेर्य तेन नयेत्तावद्यावत्पदमनामयम् ॥ 16
4.m: Even if the mind is fixed on a path that ought to be abandoned out of desire for sense objects, / one should impel it with that [reasoning] and guide it until it reaches the untroubled state.

4.s:
mārgo'tra mokṣopāyaḥ sa heyaḥ śāstrāntaroditaḥ /
viṣiṇoti nibadhnāti yecchā niyatisaṃgatam // 17
4.d:
मार्गोऽत्र मोक्षोपायः स हेयः शास्त्रान्तरोदितः ।
विषिणोति निबध्नाति येच्छा नियतिसंगतम् ॥ 17
4.m: The 'path' here is the means of liberation; that [path] taught in other scriptures ought to be abandoned. / That desire which binds and enchains [the soul] conditioned by restriction

4.s:
rāgatattvaṃ tayoktaṃ yat tena tatrānurajyate /
yathā sāmrājyasaṃbhogaṃ dṛṣṭvādṛṣṭvāthabādhame // 18
4.d:
रागतत्त्वं तयोक्तं यत् तेन तत्रानुरज्यते ।
यथा साम्राज्यसंभोगं दृष्ट्वादृष्ट्वाथबाधमे ॥ 18
4.m: is termed the principle of attachment by which one is captivated there, / just as a person, having seen imperial enjoyment, or even not having seen it, in an inferior

4.s:
bhoge rajyeta durbuddhistadvanmokṣe'pi rāgataḥ /
sa evāṃśaka ityuktaḥ svabhāvākhyaḥ sa tu sphuṭam // 19
4.d:
भोगे रज्येत दुर्बुद्धिस्तद्वन्मोक्षेऽपि रागतः ।
स एवांशक इत्युक्तः स्वभावाख्यः स तु स्फुटम् ॥ 19
4.m: enjoyment might delight, if foolish—so too in [a false] liberation through attachment. / That itself has been called a limitation known as 'nature'; clearly,

4.s:
siddhyaṅgamiti mokṣāya pratyūha iti kovidāḥ /
śivaśāsanamāhātmyaṃ vidannapyata eva hi // 20
4.d:
सिद्ध्यङ्गमिति मोक्षाय प्रत्यूह इति कोविदाः ।
शिवशासनमाहात्म्यं विदन्नप्यत एव हि ॥ 20
4.m: it is an auxiliary to worldly accomplishment, but an obstacle to liberation, according to the wise. / For this very reason, even one who knows the greatness of the Śaiva teaching,

4.s:
vaiṣṇavādhyeṣu rajyeta mūḍho rāgeṇa rañjitaḥ /
yatastāvati sā tasya vāmākhyā śaktiraiśvarī // 21
4.d:
वैष्णवाध्येषु रज्येत मूढो रागेण रञ्जितः ।
यतस्तावति सा तस्य वामाख्या शक्तिरैश्वरी ॥ 21
4.m: deluded, colored by attachment, may find pleasure in Vaiṣṇava and other doctrines; / because to that extent the divine power named Vāmā

4.s:
pāñcarātrikavairiñcasaugatādervijṛmbhate /
dṛṣṭāḥ sāmrājyasaṃbhogaṃ nindantaḥ ke'pi vāliśāḥ // 22
4.d:
पाञ्चरात्रिकवैरिञ्चसौगतादेर्विजृम्भते ।
दृष्टाः साम्राज्यसंभोगं निन्दन्तः केऽपि वालिशाः ॥ 22
4.m: unfolds itself belonging to Pāñcarātrikas, Brahmins, Saugatas, and others. / Some fools are seen reviling imperial enjoyment,

4.s:
na tu saṃtoṣataḥ sveṣu bhogeṣvāśīḥpravartanāt /
evaṃcidbhairavāveśanindātatparamānasāḥ // 23
4.d:
न तु संतोषतः स्वेषु भोगेष्वाशीःप्रवर्तनात् ।
एवंचिद्भैरवावेशनिन्दातत्परमानसाः ॥ 23
4.m: not out of contentment, but because a wish arises for their own [meager] enjoyments. / Likewise, those whose minds are intent on reviling the immersion into the consciousness of Bhairava,

4.s:
bhavantyatisughorābhiḥ śaktibhiḥ pātitā yataḥ /
tena śāṃbhavamāhātmyaṃ jānanyaḥ śāsanāntare // 24
4.d:
भवन्त्यतिसुघोराभिः शक्तिभिः पातिता यतः ।
तेन शांभवमाहात्म्यं जानन्यः शासनान्तरे ॥ 24
4.m: because they have been cast down by the extremely terrifying powers, / do not cross over the great ocean of differentiation on that account,

4.s:
āśvasto nottarītavyaṃ tena bhedamahārṇavāt /
śrīkāmikāyāṃ proktaṃ ca pāśaprakaraṇe sphuṭam // 25
4.d:
आश्वस्तो नोत्तरीतव्यं तेन भेदमहार्णवात् ।
श्रीकामिकायां प्रोक्तं च पाशप्रकरणे स्फुटम् ॥ 25
4.m: even if they know the Śāmbhava greatness, resting confident in another teaching. / And in the venerable Kāmikā, it is explicitly taught in the chapter on bonds:

4.s:
vedasāṃkhyapurāṇajñāḥ pāñcarātraparāyaṇāḥ /
ye kecidṛṣayo dhīrāḥ śāstrāntaraparāyaṇāḥ // 26
4.d:
वेदसांख्यपुराणज्ञाः पाञ्चरात्रपरायणाः ।
ये केचिदृषयो धीराः शास्त्रान्तरपरायणाः ॥ 26
4.m: 'Those who know the Vedas, Sāṃkhya, and the Purāṇas, those devoted to Pāñcarātra, / whatever wise sages are devoted to other scriptures,

4.s:
bauddhārhatādyāḥ sarve te vidyārāgeṇa rañjitāḥ /
māyāpāśena baddhatvācchivadīkṣāṃ na vindate // 27
4.d:
बौद्धार्हताद्याः सर्वे ते विद्यारागेण रञ्जिताः ।
मायापाशेन बद्धत्वाच्छिवदीक्षां न विन्दते ॥ 27
4.m: Buddhists, Jainas, and all others—colored by attachment to limited knowledge, / being bound by the fetter of māyā, do not attain the Śaiva initiation.'

4.s:
rāgaśabdena ca proktaṃ rāgatattvaṃ niyāmakam /
māyīye tacca taṃ tasmiñchāstre niyamayediti // 28
4.d:
रागशब्देन च प्रोक्तं रागतत्त्वं नियामकम् ।
मायीये तच्च तं तस्मिञ्छास्त्रे नियमयेदिति ॥ 28
4.m: And by the word 'attachment', the determining principle of attachment is designated, / which belongs to māyā; and that [principle] would restrict him to that scripture.

4.s:
mokṣo'pi vaiṣṇavāderyaḥ svasaṃkalpena bhāvitaḥ /
paraprakṛtisāyujyaṃ yadvāpyānandarūpatā // 29
4.d:
मोक्षोऽपि वैष्णवादेर्यः स्वसंकल्पेन भावितः ।
परप्रकृतिसायुज्यं यद्वाप्यानन्दरूपता ॥ 29
4.m: Even the liberation of the Vaiṣṇava and others, conceived by their own imagination, / whether union with higher Prakṛti, or consisting of bliss,

4.s:
viśuddhacittamātraṃ vā dīpavatsaṃtatikṣayaḥ /
sa savedyāpavedyātmapralayākalatāmayaḥ // 30
4.d:
विशुद्धचित्तमात्रं वा दीपवत्संततिक्षयः ।
स सवेद्यापवेद्यात्मप्रलयाकलतामयः ॥ 30
4.m: or mere purified consciousness, or the extinction of the mind's continuum like a lamp, / consists in the state of a dissolutive knower, with objective consciousness or devoid of it.

4.s:
taṃ prāpyāpi ciraṃ kālaṃ tadgogābhogabhuktataḥ /
tattattvapralayānte tu tadūrdhvāṃ sṛṣṭimāgataḥ // 31
4.d:
तं प्राप्यापि चिरं कालं तद्गोगाभोगभुक्ततः ।
तत्तत्त्वप्रलयान्ते तु तदूर्ध्वां सृष्टिमागतः ॥ 31
4.m: Even having attained that, after long time, through enjoying the fullness of that enjoyment, / at the end of the dissolution of that respective principle, having entered into creation above it,

4.s:
mantratvameti saṃbodhādananteśena kalpitāt /
etaccāgre taniṣyāma ityāstāṃ tāvadatra tat // 32
4.d:
मन्त्रत्वमेति संबोधादनन्तेशेन कल्पितात् ।
एतच्चाग्रे तनिष्याम इत्यास्तां तावदत्र तत् ॥ 32
4.m: he attains the status of a mantra through the awakening fashioned by Ananteśa. / And we will elaborate this further on; so let that be for now.

4.s:
tenājñajanatāklṛptapravādairyo viḍambitaḥ /
asadgurau rūḍhacitsa māyāpāśena rañjitaḥ // 33
4.d:
तेनाज्ञजनताक्लृप्तप्रवादैर्यो विडम्बितः ।
असद्गुरौ रूढचित्स मायापाशेन रञ्जितः ॥ 33
4.m: Therefore, one who is deceived by doctrines fashioned by ignorant people, / whose mind is established in an untrue guru, is colored by the bond of māyā.

4.s:
so'pi sattarkayogena nīyate sadguruṃ prati /
sattarkaḥ śuddhavidyaiva sā cecchā parameśituḥ // 34
4.d:
सोऽपि सत्तर्कयोगेन नीयते सद्गुरुं प्रति ।
सत्तर्कः शुद्धविद्यैव सा चेच्छा परमेशितुः ॥ 34
4.m: Even he is led to a true guru by the practice of right reasoning; / right reasoning is indeed Pure Knowledge, and that is the will of the Supreme Lord.

4.s:
śrīpūrvaśāstre tenoktaṃ sa yiyāsuḥ śivecchayā /
bhuktimuktiprasiddhyarthaṃ nīyate sadguruṃ prati // 35
4.d:
श्रीपूर्वशास्त्रे तेनोक्तं स यियासुः शिवेच्छया ।
भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रसिद्ध्यर्थं नीयते सद्गुरुं प्रति ॥ 35
4.m: Therefore, in the venerable Pūrvaśāstra it is said: 'Desiring to go by the will of Śiva / for the attainment of enjoyment and liberation, he is led to a true guru.'

4.s:
śaktipātastu tatraiṣa kramikaḥ saṃpravartate /
sthitvā yo'sadgurau śāstrāntare vā satpathaṃ śritaḥ // 36
4.d:
शक्तिपातस्तु तत्रैष क्रमिकः संप्रवर्तते ।
स्थित्वा योऽसद्गुरौ शास्त्रान्तरे वा सत्पथं श्रितः ॥ 36
4.m: However, that descent of power operates gradually in this case: / having stayed with a false guru or in another scripture, he takes refuge in the true path.

4.s:
guruśāstragate sattve'sattve cātra vibhedakam /
śaktipātasya vaicitryaṃ purastātpravivicyate // 37
4.d:
गुरुशास्त्रगते सत्त्वेऽसत्त्वे चात्र विभेदकम् ।
शक्तिपातस्य वैचित्र्यं पुरस्तात्प्रविविच्यते ॥ 37
4.m: The differentiating factor here between true and false in gurus and scriptures / is the variety of the descent of power, which will be analyzed further on.

4.s:
uktaṃ svacchandaśāstre tat vaiṣṇavādyānpravādinaḥ /
sarvānbhramayate māyā sāmokṣe mokṣalipsayā // 38
4.d:
उक्तं स्वच्छन्दशास्त्रे तत् वैष्णवाद्यान्प्रवादिनः ।
सर्वान्भ्रमयते माया सामोक्षे मोक्षलिप्सया ॥ 38
4.m: It is stated in the Svacchandaśāstra: 'Māyā deludes all disputants / such as the Vaiṣṇavas, in that which is not liberation, through the desire to attain liberation.'

4.s:
yastu rūḍho'pi tatrodyatparāmarśaviśāradaḥ /
sa śuddhavidyāmāhātmyācchaktipātapavitritaḥ // 39
4.d:
यस्तु रूढोऽपि तत्रोद्यत्परामर्शविशारदः ।
स शुद्धविद्यामाहात्म्याच्छक्तिपातपवित्रितः ॥ 39
4.m: However, one who, even though established there, is skilled in emerging reflective awareness, / purified by the descent of power through the greatness of Pure Knowledge,

4.s:
ārohatyeva sanmārgaṃ pratyūhaparivarjitaḥ /
sa tāvatkasyacittarkaḥ svata eva pravartate // 40
4.d:
आरोहत्येव सन्मार्गं प्रत्यूहपरिवर्जितः ।
स तावत्कस्यचित्तर्कः स्वत एव प्रवर्तते ॥ 40
4.m: ascends to the true path, completely free from obstacles. / In some persons, that reasoning operates entirely of itself;

4.s:
sa ca sāṃsiddhikaḥ śāstre proktaḥ svapratyayātmakaḥ /
kiraṇāyāṃ yadapyuktaṃ gurutaḥ śāstrataḥ svataḥ // 41
4.d:
स च सांसिद्धिकः शास्त्रे प्रोक्तः स्वप्रत्ययात्मकः ।
किरणायां यदप्युक्तं गुरुतः शास्त्रतः स्वतः ॥ 41
4.m: and it is declared in the scripture as spontaneous, consisting of self-validating conviction. / As is also stated in the Kiraṇa: 'From the guru, from scripture, or of oneself'—

4.s:
tatrottarottaraṃ mukhyaṃ pūrvapūrva upāyakaḥ /
yasya svato'yaṃ sattarkaḥ sarvatraivādhikāravān // 42
4.d:
तत्रोत्तरोत्तरं मुख्यं पूर्वपूर्व उपायकः ।
यस्य स्वतोऽयं सत्तर्कः सर्वत्रैवाधिकारवान् ॥ 42
4.m: among these, each subsequent one is superior, while each preceding one is a means. / One in whom this right reasoning arises of itself possesses authority everywhere;

4.s:
abhiṣiktaḥ svasaṃvittidevībhirdīkṣitaśca saḥ /
sa eva sarvācāryāṇāṃ madhye mukhyaḥ prakīrtitaḥ // 43
4.d:
अभिषिक्तः स्वसंवित्तिदेवीभिर्दीक्षितश्च सः ।
स एव सर्वाचार्याणां मध्ये मुख्यः प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 43
4.m: he is consecrated and initiated by the goddesses of his own consciousness; / he alone is proclaimed the chief among all masters.

4.s:
tatsaṃnidhāne nānyeṣu kalpiteṣvadhikāritā /
sa samastaṃ ca śāstrārthaṃ sattarkādeva manyate // 44
4.d:
तत्संनिधाने नान्येषु कल्पितेष्वधिकारिता ।
स समस्तं च शास्त्रार्थं सत्तर्कादेव मन्यते ॥ 44
4.m: In his presence, other manufactured [masters] have no authority. / And he grasps the entire meaning of the scriptures through right reasoning alone.

4.s:
śuddhavidyā hi tannāsti satyaṃ yadyanna bhāsayet /
sarvaśāstrārthavettṛtvamakasmāccāsya jāyate // 45
4.d:
शुद्धविद्या हि तन्नास्ति सत्यं यद्यन्न भासयेत् ।
सर्वशास्त्रार्थवेत्तृत्वमकस्माच्चास्य जायते ॥ 45
4.m: For it is Pure Knowledge: there is nothing true that it does not illuminate; / and knowledge of the meaning of all scriptures arises in him spontaneously.

4.s:
iti śrīpūvavākye tad+akasmāditi-śabdataḥ /
lokāprasiddho yo hetuḥ so'kasmāditi kathyate // 46
4.d:
इति श्रीपूववाक्ये तद्+अकस्मादिति-शब्दतः ।
लोकाप्रसिद्धो यो हेतुः सोऽकस्मादिति कथ्यते ॥ 46
4.m: Thus, in the statement from the venerable Pūrva, by the word 'spontaneously' [akasmāt]: / that cause which is not well-known to the world is termed 'spontaneous'.

4.s:
sa caiṣa parameśānaśuddhavidyāvijṛmbhatam /
asya bhodāśca bahavo nirbhittiḥ sahabhittikaḥ // 47
4.d:
स चैष परमेशानशुद्धविद्याविजृम्भतम् ।
अस्य भोदाश्च बहवो निर्भित्तिः सहभित्तिकः ॥ 47
4.m: And this is the blossoming of the Pure Knowledge of the Supreme Lord. / And its varieties are many: without support and with support.

4.s:
sarvago'ṃśagataḥ so'pi mukhyāmukhyāṃśaniṣṭhitaḥ /
bhittiḥ paropajīvitvaṃ parā prajñātha tatkṛtiḥ // 48
4.d:
सर्वगोऽंशगतः सोऽपि मुख्यामुख्यांशनिष्ठितः ।
भित्तिः परोपजीवित्वं परा प्रज्ञाथ तत्कृतिः ॥ 48
4.m: [This pure knowledge is] all-pervading or partial; and even that [partial one] resides in a primary or secondary part. / The 'support' [consists of] depending on another, [namely] another's intellect or its product.

4.s:
adṛṣṭamaṇḍalo'pyevaṃ yaḥ kaścidvetti tattvataḥ /
sa siddhibhāgbhavennityaṃ sa yogī sa ca dīkṣitaḥ // 49
4.d:
अदृष्टमण्डलोऽप्येवं यः कश्चिद्वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ।
स सिद्धिभाग्भवेन्नित्यं स योगी स च दीक्षितः ॥ 49
4.m: Anyone who thus knows [the reality] as it is, even without having seen a maṇḍala, / shall always attain spiritual accomplishment; he is a yogin and he is initiated.

4.s:
evaṃ yo vetti tattvena tasya nirvāṇagāminī /
dīkṣā bhavediti proktaṃ tacchrītriṃśakaśāsane // 50
4.d:
एवं यो वेत्ति तत्त्वेन तस्य निर्वाणगामिनी ।
दीक्षा भवेदिति प्रोक्तं तच्छ्रीत्रिंशकशासने ॥ 50
4.m: It is stated thus in the venerated Triṃśikā-śāsana: / for one who knows [the reality] as it is, there is initiation leading to nirvāṇa.

4.s:
akalpito gururjñayaḥ sāṃsiddhika iti smṛtaḥ /
yastu tadrūpabhāgātmabhāvanātaḥ paraṃ vinā // 51
4.d:
अकल्पितो गुरुर्ज्ञयः सांसिद्धिक इति स्मृतः ।
यस्तु तद्रूपभागात्मभावनातः परं विना ॥ 51
4.m: The innate (sāṃsiddhika) guru should be known as 'unfabricated' (akalpita): / he who attains that nature through self-cultivation without an external [master].

4.s:
śāstravitsa guruḥ śāstre prokto'kalpitakalpakaḥ /
tasyāpi bhedā utkṛṣṭamadhyamandādyupāyataḥ // 52
4.d:
शास्त्रवित्स गुरुः शास्त्रे प्रोक्तोऽकल्पितकल्पकः ।
तस्यापि भेदा उत्कृष्टमध्यमन्दाद्युपायतः ॥ 52
4.m: One who knows the scripture is declared in the scripture to be an 'unfabricated fabricator' (akalpita-kalpaka) guru; / and his divisions too [arise] through superior, middling, or inferior means.

4.s:
bhāvanāto'tha vā dhyānājjapātsvapnādvratāddhuteḥ /
prāpnotyakalpitodāramabhiṣekaṃ mahāmatiḥ // 53
4.d:
भावनातोऽथ वा ध्यानाज्जपात्स्वप्नाद्व्रताद्धुतेः ।
प्राप्नोत्यकल्पितोदारमभिषेकं महामतिः ॥ 53
4.m: From creative contemplation (bhāvanā), meditation, recitation, a dream, an observance, or oblation, / the great-minded one attains an exalted, unfabricated consecration.

4.s:
śrīmadvājasanīye śrīvīre śrībrahmayāmale /
śrīsiddhāyāmidaṃ dhātrā proktamanyatra ca sphuṭam // 54
4.d:
श्रीमद्वाजसनीये श्रीवीरे श्रीब्रह्मयामले ।
श्रीसिद्धायामिदं धात्रा प्रोक्तमन्यत्र च स्फुटम् ॥ 54
4.m: This is clearly declared by the Creator in the illustrious Vājasanīya, the Vīra, the Brahmayāmala, / the Siddhā, and elsewhere.

4.s:
tasya svecchāpravṛttatvātkāraṇānantateṣyate /
kadācidbhaktiyogena karmaṇā vidyayāpi vā // 55
4.d:
तस्य स्वेच्छाप्रवृत्तत्वात्कारणानन्ततेष्यते ।
कदाचिद्भक्तियोगेन कर्मणा विद्ययापि वा ॥ 55
4.m: Because it proceeds from his own will, an endlessness of causes is accepted: / sometimes through devotion, ritual action, or even knowledge;

4.s:
jñānadharmopadeśena mantrairvā dīkṣayāpi vā /
evamādyairanekaiśca prakāraiḥ parameśvaraḥ // 56
4.d:
ज्ञानधर्मोपदेशेन मन्त्रैर्वा दीक्षयापि वा ।
एवमाद्यैरनेकैश्च प्रकारैः परमेश्वरः ॥ 56
4.m: through the teaching of gnosis and duty, through mantras, or through initiation— / by these and many such manners, the Supreme Lord,

4.s:
saṃsāriṇo'nugṛhṇāti viśvasya jagataḥ patiḥ /
mātṛmaṇḍalasaṃbodhātsaṃskārāttapasaḥ priye // 57
4.d:
संसारिणोऽनुगृह्णाति विश्वस्य जगतः पतिः ।
मातृमण्डलसंबोधात्संस्कारात्तपसः प्रिये ॥ 57
4.m: the Master of the entire universe, graces transmigrating souls: / 'O dear one, from the awakening granted by the circle of mothers, from sacramental refinement, from asceticism,

4.s:
dhyānādyogājjapājjñānānmantrārādhanāto vratāt /
saṃprāpyaṃ kulasāmānyaṃ jñānaṃ kaulikasiddhidam // 58
4.d:
ध्यानाद्योगाज्जपाज्ज्ञानान्मन्त्राराधनातो व्रतात् ।
संप्राप्यं कुलसामान्यं ज्ञानं कौलिकसिद्धिदम् ॥ 58
4.m: from meditation, yoga, recitation, knowledge, propitiation of mantras, and observances, / that knowledge common to the Kula is obtained which bestows Kaula accomplishment.'

4.s:
tattvajñānātmakaṃ sādhyaṃ yatra yatraiva dṛśyate /
sa eva hi gurustatra hetujālaṃ prakalpyatām // 59
4.d:
तत्त्वज्ञानात्मकं साध्यं यत्र यत्रैव दृश्यते ।
स एव हि गुरुस्तत्र हेतुजालं प्रकल्प्यताम् ॥ 59
4.m: Wherever the goal consisting of knowledge of reality is observed, / there he alone is the guru; let the web of causes be devised there.

4.s:
tattvajñānādṛte nānyallakṣaṇaṃ brahmayāmale /
tatraiva coktaṃ sevāyāṃ kṛtāyāmavikalpataḥ // 60
4.d:
तत्त्वज्ञानादृते नान्यल्लक्षणं ब्रह्मयामले ।
तत्रैव चोक्तं सेवायां कृतायामविकल्पतः ॥ 60
4.m: In the Brahmayāmala there is no other characteristic than knowledge of reality; / and right there it is said: when selfless service has been performed without doubt,

4.s:
sādhakasya na cetsiddhiḥ kiṃ kāryamiti codite /
ātmīyamasya saṃjñānakrameṇa svātmadīkṣaṇam // 61
4.d:
साधकस्य न चेत्सिद्धिः किं कार्यमिति चोदिते ।
आत्मीयमस्य संज्ञानक्रमेण स्वात्मदीक्षणम् ॥ 61
4.m: if the adept does not attain spiritual accomplishment, to the question 'What is to be done?': / one's own self-initiation through the sequence of his own consciousness,

4.s:
sasphuratvaprasiddhyarthaṃ tataḥ sādhyaṃ prasiddhyati /
anena svātmavijñānaṃ sasphuratvaprasādhakam // 62
4.d:
सस्फुरत्वप्रसिद्ध्यर्थं ततः साध्यं प्रसिद्ध्यति ।
अनेन स्वात्मविज्ञानं सस्फुरत्वप्रसाधकम् ॥ 62
4.m: in order to establish the state of vibrant pulsing; then the goal is accomplished. / By this, realization of one's own self establishes vibrant pulsing;

4.s:
uktaṃ mukhyatayācāryo bhavedyadi na sasphuraḥ /
tatraiva ca punaḥ śrīmadraktārādhanakarmaṇi // 63
4.d:
उक्तं मुख्यतयाचार्यो भवेद्यदि न सस्फुरः ।
तत्रैव च पुनः श्रीमद्रक्ताराधनकर्मणि ॥ 63
4.m: it is taught that he would essentially be a master (ācārya) if he possesses vibrant pulsing. / And in that very [text], concerning the rite of worship of the illustrious Raktā:

4.s:
vidhiṃ proktaṃ sadā kurvanmāsenācārya ucyate /
pakṣeṇa sādhako'rdhārdhātputrakaḥ samayī tathā // 64
4.d:
विधिं प्रोक्तं सदा कुर्वन्मासेनाचार्य उच्यते ।
पक्षेण साधकोऽर्धार्धात्पुत्रकः समयी तथा ॥ 64
4.m: Constantly performing the prescribed ritual, he is called a master in a month; / an adept in a fortnight; a spiritual son in half of half of that; and likewise an initiate into the rule.

4.s:
dīkṣayejjapayogena raktādevī kramādyataḥ /
guroralābhe proktasya vidhimetaṃ samācaret // 65
4.d:
दीक्षयेज्जपयोगेन रक्तादेवी क्रमाद्यतः ।
गुरोरलाभे प्रोक्तस्य विधिमेतं समाचरेत् ॥ 65
4.m: Since Goddess Raktā would initiate by means of recitation in due succession, / in the absence of a declared guru one should perform this ritual.

4.s:
mate ca pustakādvidyādhyayane doṣa īdṛśaḥ /
ukto yastena taddoṣābhāve'sau na niṣiddhatā // 66
4.d:
मते च पुस्तकाद्विद्याध्ययने दोष ईदृशः ।
उक्तो यस्तेन तद्दोषाभावेऽसौ न निषिद्धता ॥ 66
4.m: And the fault in studying knowledge from a book that is mentioned in the Mata / is of such a nature: therefore, when that fault is absent, this [study] is not prohibited.

4.s:
mantradravyādiguptatve phalaṃ kimiti codite /
pustakādhītavidyā ye dīkṣāsamayavarjitāḥ // 67
4.d:
मन्त्रद्रव्यादिगुप्तत्वे फलं किमिति चोदिते ।
पुस्तकाधीतविद्या ये दीक्षासमयवर्जिताः ॥ 67
4.m: To the question, 'What is the fruit when mantras, substances, and the like are kept secret?': / Those who have studied knowledge from books while devoid of initiation and observances,

4.s:
tāmasāḥ parahiṃsādi vaśyādi ca carantyalam /
na ca tattvaṃ vidustena doṣabhāja iti sphuṭam // 68
4.d:
तामसाः परहिंसादि वश्यादि च चरन्त्यलम् ।
न च तत्त्वं विदुस्तेन दोषभाज इति स्फुटम् ॥ 68
4.m: dominated by tamas, excessively perform harm to others, subjugation, and so forth, / and do not know the reality; hence they clearly incur fault.

4.s:
pūrvaṃ padayugaṃ vācyamanyonyaṃ hetuhetumat /
yastu śāstraṃ vinā naiti śuddhavidyākhyasaṃvidam // 69
4.d:
पूर्वं पदयुगं वाच्यमन्योन्यं हेतुहेतुमत् ।
यस्तु शास्त्रं विना नैति शुद्धविद्याख्यसंविदम् ॥ 69
4.m: The first pair of words must be understood as mutually related as cause and effect. / But he who does not attain the consciousness named pure knowledge without scripture,

4.s:
guroḥ sa śāstramanvicchustaduktaṃ kramamācaret /
yena kenāpyupāyena gurumārādhya bhaktitaḥ // 70
4.d:
गुरोः स शास्त्रमन्विच्छुस्तदुक्तं क्रममाचरेत् ।
येन केनाप्युपायेन गुरुमाराध्य भक्तितः ॥ 70
4.m: seeking scripture from a guru, should perform the sequence taught by him. / Having worshiped the guru through whatever means with devotion,

4.s:
taddīkṣākramayogena śāstrārthaṃ vettyasau tataḥ /
abhiṣekaṃ samāsādya yo bhavetsa tu kalpitaḥ // 71
4.d:
तद्दीक्षाक्रमयोगेन शास्त्रार्थं वेत्त्यसौ ततः ।
अभिषेकं समासाद्य यो भवेत्स तु कल्पितः ॥ 71
4.m: he knows the meaning of scripture through the method of his initiation. / Then, having received consecration, whoever emerges is 'fabricated' (kalpita).

4.s:
sannapyaśeṣapāśaughavinivartanakovidaḥ /
yo yathākramayogena kasmiṃścicchāstravastuni // 72
4.d:
सन्नप्यशेषपाशौघविनिवर्तनकोविदः ।
यो यथाक्रमयोगेन कस्मिंश्चिच्छास्त्रवस्तुनि ॥ 72
4.m: Even while being skilled in removing the entire mass of bonds, / he who, through the method of succession, with regard to some particular topic of scripture,

4.s:
ākasmikaṃ brajedbodhaṃ kalpitākalpito hi saḥ /
tasya yo'kalpito bhāgaḥ sa tu śreṣṭhamaḥ smṛtaḥ // 73
4.d:
आकस्मिकं ब्रजेद्बोधं कल्पिताकल्पितो हि सः ।
तस्य योऽकल्पितो भागः स तु श्रेष्ठमः स्मृतः ॥ 73
4.m: attains sudden awakening, is indeed 'fabricated-unfabricated' (kalpitākalpita). / The part of him that is unfabricated is considered the highest;

4.s:
utkarṣaḥ śuddhavidyāṃśatāratamyakṛto yataḥ /
yathā bhedenādisiddhācchivānmuktaśivā hyadhaḥ // 74
4.d:
उत्कर्षः शुद्धविद्यांशतारतम्यकृतो यतः ।
यथा भेदेनादिसिद्धाच्छिवान्मुक्तशिवा ह्यधः ॥ 74
4.m: for superiority is caused by the gradations of the portion of pure knowledge. / Just as liberated Śivas are indeed lower by distinction from Śiva who is eternally perfected,

4.s:
tathā sāṃsiddhikajñānādāhṛtajñānino'dhamāḥ /
tatsaṃnidhau nādhikārasteṣāṃ muktaśivātmavat // 75
4.d:
तथा सांसिद्धिकज्ञानादाहृतज्ञानिनोऽधमाः ।
तत्संनिधौ नाधिकारस्तेषां मुक्तशिवात्मवत् ॥ 75
4.m: so those whose knowledge is acquired [from without] are inferior to one with innate knowledge. / In his presence they have no authority, just like the liberated Śivas;

4.s:
kiṃ tu tūṣṇīṃ-sthitiryadvā kṛtyaṃ tadanuvartanam /
yastvakalpitarūpo'pi saṃvādadṛḍhatākṛte // 76
4.d:
किं तु तूष्णीं-स्थितिर्यद्वा कृत्यं तदनुवर्तनम् ।
यस्त्वकल्पितरूपोऽपि संवाददृढताकृते ॥ 76
4.m: rather, there should be silence, or their task is to follow him. / But he who, though unfabricated in nature, for the sake of confirming harmony,

4.s:
anyato labdhasaṃskāraḥ sa sākṣādbhairavo guruḥ /
yataḥ śāstrakramāttajjñaguruprajñānuśīlanāt // 77
4.d:
अन्यतो लब्धसंस्कारः स साक्षाद्भैरवो गुरुः ।
यतः शास्त्रक्रमात्तज्ज्ञगुरुप्रज्ञानुशीलनात् ॥ 77
4.m: has received refinement from another, is a guru who is Bhairava directly. / Because from the sequence of scripture and from constant reflection on the intellect of a guru who knows it,

4.s:
ātmapratyayitaṃ jñānaṃ pūrṇatvādbhairavāyate /
tena śrīkiraṇoktaṃ yadgurutaḥ śāstrataḥ svataḥ // 78
4.d:
आत्मप्रत्ययितं ज्ञानं पूर्णत्वाद्भैरवायते ।
तेन श्रीकिरणोक्तं यद्गुरुतः शास्त्रतः स्वतः ॥ 78
4.m: knowledge verified by oneself becomes Bhairava-like due to fullness. / Therefore, what is said in the illustrious Kiraṇa: 'From the guru, from scripture, and from oneself—

4.s:
tripratyayamidaṃ jñānamiti yacca niśāṭane /
tatsaṃghātaviparyāsavigrahairbhāsate tathā // 79
4.d:
त्रिप्रत्ययमिदं ज्ञानमिति यच्च निशाटने ।
तत्संघातविपर्यासविग्रहैर्भासते तथा ॥ 79
4.m: this knowledge has threefold verification'; and that which is in the Niśāṭana: / 'It shines thus through the aggregates, inversions, and distinct forms.'

4.s:
karaṇasya vicitratvādvicitrāmeva tāṃ chidam /
kartuṃ vāsīṃ ca ṭaṅkaṃ ca krakacaṃ cāpi gṛhṇate // 80
4.d:
करणस्य विचित्रत्वाद्विचित्रामेव तां छिदम् ।
कर्तुं वासीं च टङ्कं च क्रकचं चापि गृह्णते ॥ 80
4.m: Because of the variety of the instrument, in order to make that very cutting diverse, / people take an adze, a chisel, and a saw;

4.s:
tāvacca chedanaṃ hyekaṃ tathaivādyābhisaṃdhitaḥ /
itthameva mitau vācyaṃ karaṇasya svakaṃ vapuḥ // 81
4.d:
तावच्च छेदनं ह्येकं तथैवाद्याभिसंधितः ।
इत्थमेव मितौ वाच्यं करणस्य स्वकं वपुः ॥ 81
4.m: yet the cutting is simply one, just as intended at the outset. / In this very way must the own-form of an instrument be explained with respect to valid cognition.

4.s:
na svatantraṃ svato mānaṃ kuryādadhigamaṃ haṭhāt /
pramātrāśvāsaparyanto yato'dhigama ucyate // 82
4.d:
न स्वतन्त्रं स्वतो मानं कुर्यादधिगमं हठात् ।
प्रमात्राश्वासपर्यन्तो यतोऽधिगम उच्यते ॥ 82
4.m: A means of valid knowledge does not forcibly produce apprehension autonomously by itself, / because apprehension is said to culminate in the certitude of the knower;

4.s:
āśvāsaśca vicitro'sau śaktipātavaśāttathā /
pramite'pi pramāṇānāmavakāśo'styataḥ sphuṭaḥ // 83
4.d:
आश्वासश्च विचित्रोऽसौ शक्तिपातवशात्तथा ।
प्रमितेऽपि प्रमाणानामवकाशोऽस्त्यतः स्फुटः ॥ 83
4.m: and this certitude is diverse according to the descent of power. / Hence, there is clearly scope for means of valid knowledge even regarding what is already known.

4.s:
dṛṣṭvā dṛṣṭvā samāśliṣya ciraṃ saṃcarvya cetasā /
priyā yaiḥ parituṣyeta kiṃ brūmaḥ kila tānprati // 84
4.d:
दृष्ट्वा दृष्ट्वा समाश्लिष्य चिरं संचर्व्य चेतसा ।
प्रिया यैः परितुष्येत किं ब्रूमः किल तान्प्रति ॥ 84
4.m: Seeing again and again, embracing, and savoring for a long time in mind, / those through whom the beloved is fully pleased—what can we possibly say to them?

4.s:
itthaṃ ca mānasaṃplutyāmapi nādhigate gatiḥ /
na vyarthatā nānavasthā nānyonyāśrayatāpi ca // 85
4.d:
इत्थं च मानसंप्लुत्यामपि नाधिगते गतिः ।
न व्यर्थता नानवस्था नान्योन्याश्रयतापि च ॥ 85
4.m: And thus, even when means of valid knowledge converge, there is no [superfluous] movement toward what is already known, / no uselessness, no infinite regress, nor mutual dependence.

4.s:
evaṃ yogāṅgamiyati tarka eva na cāparam /
antarantaḥ parāmarśapāṭavātiśayāya saḥ // 86
4.d:
एवं योगाङ्गमियति तर्क एव न चापरम् ।
अन्तरन्तः परामर्शपाटवातिशयाय सः ॥ 86
4.m: Thus, among the limbs of yoga, reasoning alone [is primary], and nothing else; / it serves to heighten the dexterity of internal reflective awareness.

4.s:
ahiṃsā satyamasteyabrahmacaryāparigrahāḥ /
iti pañca yamāḥ sākṣātsaṃvittau nopayoginaḥ // 87
4.d:
अहिंसा सत्यमस्तेयब्रह्मचर्यापरिग्रहाः ।
इति पञ्च यमाः साक्षात्संवित्तौ नोपयोगिनः ॥ 87
4.m: Non-violence, truthfulness, non-stealing, celibacy, and non-possessiveness: / these five restraints are not directly useful for consciousness.

4.s:
tapaḥprabhṛtayo ye ca niyamā yattathāsanam /
prāṇāyāmāśca ye sarvametadbāhyavijṛmbhitam // 88
4.d:
तपःप्रभृतयो ये च नियमा यत्तथासनम् ।
प्राणायामाश्च ये सर्वमेतद्बाह्यविजृम्भितम् ॥ 88
4.m: And the observances such as asceticism, likewise posture, / and the breath-controls—all this is external manifestation.

4.s:
śrīmadvīrāvalau coktaṃ bodhamātre śivātmake /
cittapralayabandhena pralīne śaśibhāskare // 89
4.d:
श्रीमद्वीरावलौ चोक्तं बोधमात्रे शिवात्मके ।
चित्तप्रलयबन्धेन प्रलीने शशिभास्करे ॥ 89
4.m: And it is said in the illustrious Vīrāvalī: 'In mere consciousness consisting of Śiva, / when the moon and sun dissolve through the binding of the mind's dissolution,

4.s:
prāpte ca dvādaśe bhāge jīvāditye svabodhake /
mokṣaḥ sa eva kathitaḥ prāṇāyāmo nirarthakaḥ // 90
4.d:
प्राप्ते च द्वादशे भागे जीवादित्ये स्वबोधके ।
मोक्षः स एव कथितः प्राणायामो निरर्थकः ॥ 90
4.m: and when the twelfth portion, the sun of life which awakens itself, is reached, / that alone is declared liberation; breath-control is useless.

4.s:
prāṇāyāmo na kartavyaḥ śarīraṃ yena pīḍyate /
rahasyaṃ vetti yo yatra sa muktaḥ sa ca mocakaḥ // 91
4.d:
प्राणायामो न कर्तव्यः शरीरं येन पीड्यते ।
रहस्यं वेत्ति यो यत्र स मुक्तः स च मोचकः ॥ 91
4.m: Breath-control should not be performed by which the body is afflicted. / One who knows the secret wherever it is, he is liberated and he is a liberator.'

4.s:
pratyāhāraśca nāmāyamarthebhyo'kṣadhiyāṃ hi yaḥ /
anibaddhasya bandhasya tadantaḥ kila kīlanam // 92
4.d:
प्रत्याहारश्च नामायमर्थेभ्योऽक्षधियां हि यः ।
अनिबद्धस्य बन्धस्य तदन्तः किल कीलनम् ॥ 92
4.m: And retraction, indeed, is that drawing back of the intellect of the senses from objects; / it is truly the pegging inward of an unbonded bondage.

4.s:
cittasya viṣaye kvāpi bandhanaṃ dhāraṇātmakam /
tatsadṛgjñānasaṃtāno dhyānamastamitā param // 93
4.d:
चित्तस्य विषये क्वापि बन्धनं धारणात्मकम् ।
तत्सदृग्ज्ञानसंतानो ध्यानमस्तमिता परम् ॥ 93
4.m: The binding of the mind to any object consists of fixation (dhāraṇā); / a continuous flow of cognition similar to that is meditation (dhyāna); beyond that, [all else] disappears.

4.s:
yadā tu jñeyatādātmyameva saṃvidi jāyate /
grāhyagrahaṇatādvaitaśūnyateyaṃ samāhitiḥ // 94
4.d:
यदा तु ज्ञेयतादात्म्यमेव संविदि जायते ।
ग्राह्यग्रहणताद्वैतशून्यतेयं समाहितिः ॥ 94
4.m: When, however, identity with the knowable arises directly in consciousness, / free from the duality of the grasper and the grasped, that is samādhi.

4.s:
tadeṣā dhāraṇādhyānasamādhitritayī parām /
saṃvidaṃ prati no kaṃcidupayogaṃ samaśnute // 95
4.d:
तदेषा धारणाध्यानसमाधित्रितयी पराम् ।
संविदं प्रति नो कंचिदुपयोगं समश्नुते ॥ 95
4.m: Therefore, this triad of dhāraṇā, dhyāna, and samādhi / serves no function toward the supreme consciousness.

4.s:
yogāṅgatā yamādestu samādhyantasya varṇyate /
svapūrvapūrvopāyatvādantyatarkopayogataḥ // 96
4.d:
योगाङ्गता यमादेस्तु समाध्यन्तस्य वर्ण्यते ।
स्वपूर्वपूर्वोपायत्वादन्त्यतर्कोपयोगतः ॥ 96
4.m: Yet the nature of limbs of yoga from yama up to samādhi is described / because each serves as an expedient for the one after it, culminating in the service of liberating discernment (tarka).

4.s:
antaḥ saṃvidi rūḍhaṃ hi taddvārā prāṇadehayoḥ /
buddhau vārpyaṃ tadabhyāsānnaiṣa nyāyastu saṃvidi // 97
4.d:
अन्तः संविदि रूढं हि तद्द्वारा प्राणदेहयोः ।
बुद्धौ वार्प्यं तदभ्यासान्नैष न्यायस्तु संविदि ॥ 97
4.m: For what is rooted internally in consciousness is imparted through it / into breath and body, or into the intellect by repeated practice; but this rule does not apply to consciousness [itself].

4.s:
atha vāsmaddṛśi prāṇadhīdehāderapi sphuṭam /
sarvātmakatvāttatrastho'pyabhyāso'nyavyapohanam // 98
4.d:
अथ वास्मद्दृशि प्राणधीदेहादेरपि स्फुटम् ।
सर्वात्मकत्वात्तत्रस्थोऽप्यभ्यासोऽन्यव्यपोहनम् ॥ 98
4.m: Or rather, in our view, because even breath, intellect, body, and the rest / are clearly all-pervasive, the practice residing there too consists in the exclusion of other [constructs].

4.s:
deha utplutisaṃpātadharmojjigamiṣārasāt /
utplāvyate tadvipakṣapātāśaṅkāvyapohanāt // 99
4.d:
देह उत्प्लुतिसंपातधर्मोज्जिगमिषारसात् ।
उत्प्लाव्यते तद्विपक्षपाताशङ्काव्यपोहनात् ॥ 99
4.m: The body is made to leap out of the relish of the desire to rise, whose nature is leaping and falling, / by dispelling the suspicion of the opposite—falling down.

4.s:
guruvākyaparāmarśasadṛśe svavimarśane /
prabuddhe tadvipakṣāṇāṃ vyudāsaḥ pāṭhacintane // 100
4.d:
गुरुवाक्यपरामर्शसदृशे स्वविमर्शने ।
प्रबुद्धे तद्विपक्षाणां व्युदासः पाठचिन्तने ॥ 100
4.m: When one's own reflective awareness, resembling the contemplation of the guru's words, / is awakened, the removal of its opposites occurs through study and contemplation.

4.s:
nahyasya guruṇā śakyaṃ svaṃ jñānaṃ śabda eva vā /
dhiyi ropayituṃ tena svaprabodhakramo dhruvam // 101
4.d:
नह्यस्य गुरुणा शक्यं स्वं ज्ञानं शब्द एव वा ।
धियि रोपयितुं तेन स्वप्रबोधक्रमो ध्रुवम् ॥ 101
4.m: For the guru cannot implant his own knowledge or speech / into another's intellect; by that [instruction], a sequence of self-awakening indeed [ensues].

4.s:
ata eva svapnakāle śrute tatrāpi vastuni /
tādātmyabhāvanāyogo na phalāya na bhaṇyate // 102
4.d:
अत एव स्वप्नकाले श्रुते तत्रापि वस्तुनि ।
तादात्म्यभावनायोगो न फलाय न भण्यते ॥ 102
4.m: For this very reason, even regarding a matter heard during a dream, / the application of contemplation on identity is not said to be devoid of fruit.

4.s:
saṃketānādare śabdaniṣṭhamāmarśanaṃ paṭhiḥ /
tadādare tadarthastu cinteti paricarcyatām // 103
4.d:
संकेतानादरे शब्दनिष्ठमामर्शनं पठिः ।
तदादरे तदर्थस्तु चिन्तेति परिचर्च्यताम् ॥ 103
4.m: Recitation is reflection resting in speech without regard to convention; / but when that [convention] is respected, its meaning is contemplation—let this be investigated.

4.s:
tadadvayāyāṃ saṃvittāvabhyāso'nupayogavān /
kevalaṃ dvaitamālinyaśaṅkānirmūlanāya saḥ // 104
4.d:
तदद्वयायां संवित्तावभ्यासोऽनुपयोगवान् ।
केवलं द्वैतमालिन्यशङ्कानिर्मूलनाय सः ॥ 104
4.m: Therefore, in non-dual consciousness practice is useless; / it serves solely to eradicate the suspicion of the stain of duality.

4.s:
dvaitaśaṅkāśca tarkeṇa tarkyanta iti varṇitam /
tattarkasādhanāyāstu yamāderapyupāyatā // 105
4.d:
द्वैतशङ्काश्च तर्केण तर्क्यन्त इति वर्णितम् ।
तत्तर्कसाधनायास्तु यमादेरप्युपायता ॥ 105
4.m: And doubts regarding duality are resolved by discernment (tarka), as has been explained; / but yama and the other [limbs] serve as expedients for the attainment of that discernment.

4.s:
uktaṃ śrīpūrvaśastre ca na dvaitaṃ nāpi cādvayam /
liṅgapūjādikaṃ sarvamityupakramya śaṃbhunā // 106
4.d:
उक्तं श्रीपूर्वशस्त्रे च न द्वैतं नापि चाद्वयम् ।
लिङ्गपूजादिकं सर्वमित्युपक्रम्य शंभुना ॥ 106
4.m: And in the venerable Mālinīvijayottara, starting with the statement: / "Neither duality nor non-duality, all things such as liṅga worship, etc.,

4.s:
vihitaṃ sarvamevātra pratiṣiddhamathāpi vā /
prāṇāyāmādikairaṅgairyogāḥ syuḥ kṛttrimā yataḥ // 107
4.d:
विहितं सर्वमेवात्र प्रतिषिद्धमथापि वा ।
प्राणायामादिकैरङ्गैर्योगाः स्युः कृत्त्रिमा यतः ॥ 107
4.m: are here enjoined, or even prohibited," / Śambhu [said]: "Since yogas attained through limbs like prāṇāyāma are artificial,

4.s:
tattenākṛtakasyāsya kalāṃ nārghanti ṣoḍaśīm /
kiṃ tvetadatra deveśi niyamena vidhīyate // 108
4.d:
तत्तेनाकृतकस्यास्य कलां नार्घन्ति षोडशीम् ।
किं त्वेतदत्र देवेशि नियमेन विधीयते ॥ 108
4.m: therefore they are not worth a sixteenth part of this uncreated [yoga]. / But this, O goddess of the gods, is enjoined here as a rule:

4.s:
tattve cetaḥ sthiraṃ kāryaṃ tacca yasya yathāstviti /
evaṃ dvaitaparāmarśanāśāya parameśvaraḥ // 109
4.d:
तत्त्वे चेतः स्थिरं कार्यं तच्च यस्य यथास्त्विति ।
एवं द्वैतपरामर्शनाशाय परमेश्वरः ॥ 109
4.m: the mind must be made firm in reality, and that may be as it suits anyone." / Thus, to destroy the reflective awareness of duality, the Supreme Lord,

4.s:
kvacitsvabhāvamamalamāmṛśannaniśaṃ sthitaḥ /
yaḥ svabhāvaparāmarśa indriyārthādyupāyataḥ // 110
4.d:
क्वचित्स्वभावममलमामृशन्ननिशं स्थितः ।
यः स्वभावपरामर्श इन्द्रियार्थाद्युपायतः ॥ 110
4.m: abiding incessantly reflecting upon His own immaculate nature, / [reveals that] reflective awareness of one's nature, arising through the senses and their objects

4.s:
vinaiva tanmukho'nyo vā svātantryāttadvikalpanam /
tacca svacchasvatantrātmaratnanirbhāsini sphuṭam // 111
4.d:
विनैव तन्मुखोऽन्यो वा स्वातन्त्र्यात्तद्विकल्पनम् ।
तच्च स्वच्छस्वतन्त्रात्मरत्ननिर्भासिनि स्फुटम् ॥ 111
4.m: or even without them, or another [awareness] arising through autonomy, is its conceptual construction. / And that [conceptual construction], clearly establishing differentiation among the multitude of entities

4.s:
bhāvaughe bhedasaṃdhātṛ svātmano naiśamucyate /
tadeva tu samastārthanirbharātmaikagocaram // 112
4.d:
भावौघे भेदसंधातृ स्वात्मनो नैशमुच्यते ।
तदेव तु समस्तार्थनिर्भरात्मैकगोचरम् ॥ 112
4.m: appearing within the jewel of the pure, autonomous Self, is called the [nocturnal] night of the Self. / But that very [construct] which has for its sole domain the Self full of all things,

4.s:
śuddhavidyātmakaṃ sarvamevedamahamityalam /
idaṃ vikalpanaṃ śuddhavidyārūpaṃ sphuṭātmakam // 113
4.d:
शुद्धविद्यात्मकं सर्वमेवेदमहमित्यलम् ।
इदं विकल्पनं शुद्धविद्यारूपं स्फुटात्मकम् ॥ 113
4.m: consisting of pure knowledge (śuddhavidyā) as "All this is indeed myself"— / this conceptual construct, having the nature of pure knowledge and fully manifest,

4.s:
pratihantīha māyīyaṃ vikalpaṃ bhedabhāvakam /
śuddhavidyāparāmarśo yaḥ sa eva tvanekadhā // 114
4.d:
प्रतिहन्तीह मायीयं विकल्पं भेदभावकम् ।
शुद्धविद्यापरामर्शो यः स एव त्वनेकधा ॥ 114
4.m: completely strikes down the construct of Māyā that creates duality. / That reflective awareness of pure knowledge, however, is manifold

4.s:
snānaśuddhyarcanāhomadhyānajapyādiyogataḥ /
viśvametatsvasaṃvittirasanirbharitaṃ rasāt // 115
4.d:
स्नानशुद्ध्यर्चनाहोमध्यानजप्यादियोगतः ।
विश्वमेतत्स्वसंवित्तिरसनिर्भरितं रसात् ॥ 115
4.m: through bath, purification, worship, oblations, meditation, recitation, and the like. / Joyfully penetrating this universe, which is brimming with the nectar of one's own consciousness,

4.s:
āviśya śuddho nikhilaṃ tarpayedadhvamaṇlam /
ullāsibodhahutabhugdagdhaviśvendhanodite // 116
4.d:
आविश्य शुद्धो निखिलं तर्पयेदध्वमण्लम् ।
उल्लासिबोधहुतभुग्दग्धविश्वेन्धनोदिते ॥ 116
4.m: the purified one should gratify the entire wheel of the path. / When the fuel of the universe is burned by the flaming fire of consciousness,

4.s:
sitabhasmani dehasya majjanaṃ snānamucyate /
itthaṃ ca vihitasnānastarpitānantadevataḥ // 117
4.d:
सितभस्मनि देहस्य मज्जनं स्नानमुच्यते ।
इत्थं च विहितस्नानस्तर्पितानन्तदेवतः ॥ 117
4.m: the immersion of the body in the resulting white ash is called the bath. / Having thus performed the bath, having satisfied the infinite deities,

4.s:
tato'pi dehārambhīṇi tattvāni pariśodhayet /
śivātmakeṣvapyeteṣu buddhiryā vyatirekiṇī // 118
4.d:
ततोऽपि देहारम्भीणि तत्त्वानि परिशोधयेत् ।
शिवात्मकेष्वप्येतेषु बुद्धिर्या व्यतिरेकिणी ॥ 118
4.m: he should then thoroughly purify the principles that constitute the body. / Even though these consist of Śiva, that awareness which separates them [from Him]

4.s:
saivāśuddhiḥ parākhyātā śuddhistaddhīvimardanam /
evaṃ svadehaṃ bodhaikapātraṃ galitabhedakam // 119
4.d:
सैवाशुद्धिः पराख्याता शुद्धिस्तद्धीविमर्दनम् ।
एवं स्वदेहं बोधैकपात्रं गलितभेदकम् ॥ 119
4.m: is said to be the supreme impurity; purification is the crushing of that awareness. / Thus viewing his own body as the sole vessel of consciousness, free of differentiation,

4.s:
paśyansaṃvittimātratve svatantre tiṣṭhati prabhuḥ /
yatkiṃcinmānasāhlādi yatra kvāpīndriyasthitau // 120
4.d:
पश्यन्संवित्तिमात्रत्वे स्वतन्त्रे तिष्ठति प्रभुः ।
यत्किंचिन्मानसाह्लादि यत्र क्वापीन्द्रियस्थितौ ॥ 120
4.m: the Lord abides in autonomous pure consciousness alone. / Whatever delights the mind, wherever the senses may be situated,

4.s:
yojyate brahmasaddhāmni pūjopakaraṇaṃ hi tat /
pūjā nāma vibhinnasya bhāvaughasyāpi saṃgatiḥ // 121
4.d:
योज्यते ब्रह्मसद्धाम्नि पूजोपकरणं हि तत् ।
पूजा नाम विभिन्नस्य भावौघस्यापि संगतिः ॥ 121
4.m: is offered into the real abode of Brahman; that is indeed an implement of worship. / Worship is the union even of a differentiated stream of entities

4.s:
svatantravimalānantabhairavīyacidātmanā /
tathāhi saṃvideveyamantarbāhyobhayātmanā // 122
4.d:
स्वतन्त्रविमलानन्तभैरवीयचिदात्मना ।
तथाहि संविदेवेयमन्तर्बाह्योभयात्मना ॥ 122
4.m: with the consciousness of Bhairava, which is autonomous, immaculate, and infinite. / For this very consciousness, by virtue of its absolute autonomy,

4.s:
svātantryādvartamānaiva parāmarśasvarūpiṇī /
sa ca dvādaśadhā tatra sarvamantarbhavedyataḥ // 123
4.d:
स्वातन्त्र्याद्वर्तमानैव परामर्शस्वरूपिणी ।
स च द्वादशधा तत्र सर्वमन्तर्भवेद्यतः ॥ 123
4.m: abides consisting of reflective awareness, having an internal, external, and dual nature; / and that is twelvefold, because everything is contained within it.

4.s:
sūrya eva hi somātmā sa ca viśvamayaḥ sthitaḥ /
kalādvādaśakātmaiva tatsaṃvitparamārthataḥ // 124
4.d:
सूर्य एव हि सोमात्मा स च विश्वमयः स्थितः ।
कलाद्वादशकात्मैव तत्संवित्परमार्थतः ॥ 124
4.m: For the sun itself has the nature of the moon, and it abides consisting of the universe; / in ultimate truth, that consciousness has the nature of the twelve kalās.

4.s:
sā ca mātari vijñāne māne karaṇagocare /
meye caturvidhaṃ bhāti rūpamāśritya sarvadā // 125
4.d:
सा च मातरि विज्ञाने माने करणगोचरे ।
मेये चतुर्विधं भाति रूपमाश्रित्य सर्वदा ॥ 125
4.m: And it always shines having assumed a fourfold form: / in the knower, in cognition, in the means of knowledge situated in the sense organ, and in the knowable.

4.s:
śuddhasaṃvinmayī prācye jñāne śabdanarūpiṇī /
karaṇe grahaṇākārā yataḥ śrīyogasaṃcare // 126
4.d:
शुद्धसंविन्मयी प्राच्ये ज्ञाने शब्दनरूपिणी ।
करणे ग्रहणाकारा यतः श्रीयोगसंचरे ॥ 126
4.m: In the first it consists of pure consciousness, in cognition it consists of verbal articulation, / and in the instrument it takes the form of apprehension, as is said in the venerable Yogasaṃcara:

4.s:
ye cakṣurmaṇḍale śvete pratyakṣe parameśvari /
ṣoḍaśāraṃ dvādaśāraṃ tatrasthaṃ cakramuttamam // 127
4.d:
ये चक्षुर्मण्डले श्वेते प्रत्यक्षे परमेश्वरि ।
षोडशारं द्वादशारं तत्रस्थं चक्रमुत्तमम् ॥ 127
4.m: "The two white circles of the eyes, O supreme goddess, visible to perception— / situated there is the supreme wheel of sixteen spokes and twelve spokes;

4.s:
prativāraṇavadrakte tadbahirye taducyate /
dvitīyaṃ madhyage ye te kṛṣṇaśvete ca maṇḍale // 128
4.d:
प्रतिवारणवद्रक्ते तद्बहिर्ये तदुच्यते ।
द्वितीयं मध्यगे ये ते कृष्णश्वेते च मण्डले ॥ 128
4.m: it is said to be like a protective rim outside them, [radiating] red. / The second [pair] consists of the black and white circles in the center;

4.s:
tadantarye sthite śuddhe bhinnāñjanasamaprabhe /
caturdale tu te jñeye agnīṣomātmake priye // 129
4.d:
तदन्तर्ये स्थिते शुद्धे भिन्नाञ्जनसमप्रभे ।
चतुर्दले तु ते ज्ञेये अग्नीषोमात्मके प्रिये ॥ 129
4.m: those resting within them, pure and radiant like crushed collyrium, / are to be known as having four petals, O dear one, composed of fire and moon.

4.s:
mithunatve sthite ye ca cakre dve parameśvari /
saṃmīlanonmīlanaṃ te anyonyaṃ vidadhātake // 130
4.d:
मिथुनत्वे स्थिते ये च चक्रे द्वे परमेश्वरि ।
संमीलनोन्मीलनं ते अन्योन्यं विदधातके ॥ 130
4.m: And the two wheels that abide as a couple, O supreme goddess, / continuously close and open each other.

4.s:
yathā yoniśca liṅgaṃ ca saṃyogātsravato'mṛtam /
tathāmṛtāgnisaṃyogāddravataste na saṃśayaḥ // 131
4.d:
यथा योनिश्च लिङ्गं च संयोगात्स्रवतोऽमृतम् ।
तथामृताग्निसंयोगाद्द्रवतस्ते न संशयः ॥ 131
4.m: Just as the yoni and the liṅga emit nectar from their union, / so from the union of fire and nectar do they melt without doubt.

4.s:
taccakrapīḍanādrātrau jyotirbhātyarkasomagam /
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā paramāṃ jyotsnāṃ kālajñānaṃ pravartate // 132
4.d:
तच्चक्रपीडनाद्रात्रौ ज्योतिर्भात्यर्कसोमगम् ।
तां दृष्ट्वा परमां ज्योत्स्नां कालज्ञानं प्रवर्तते ॥ 132
4.m: From the compression of those wheels, at night the light going to sun and moon shines forth; / beholding that supreme moonlight, knowledge of time arises.

4.s:
sahasrāraṃ bhaveccakraṃ tābhyāmupari saṃsthitam /
tataścakrātsamudbhūtaṃ brahmāṇḍaṃ tadudāhṛtam // 133
4.d:
सहस्रारं भवेच्चक्रं ताभ्यामुपरि संस्थितम् ।
ततश्चक्रात्समुद्भूतं ब्रह्माण्डं तदुदाहृतम् ॥ 133
4.m: A thousand-spoked wheel exists, situated above them; / from that wheel arises the egg of Brahmā, so it is declared.

4.s:
tatrasthāṃ muñcate dhārāṃ somo hyagnipradīpitaḥ /
sṛjatītthaṃ jagatsarvamātmanyātmanyanantakam // 134
4.d:
तत्रस्थां मुञ्चते धारां सोमो ह्यग्निप्रदीपितः ।
सृजतीत्थं जगत्सर्वमात्मन्यात्मन्यनन्तकम् ॥ 134
4.m: The moon, ignited by fire, releases the stream situated therein; / in this way it creates the whole universe, infinite, in self after self.

4.s:
ṣoḍaśadvādaśārābhyāmaṣṭāreṣvatha sarvaśaḥ /
evaṃ krameṇa sarvatra cakreṣvamṛtamuttamam // 135
4.d:
षोडशद्वादशाराभ्यामष्टारेष्वथ सर्वशः ।
एवं क्रमेण सर्वत्र चक्रेष्वमृतमुत्तमम् ॥ 135
4.m: From the sixteen- and twelve-spoked wheels to the eight-spoked wheels everywhere, / in this sequence throughout all the wheels, the supreme nectar,

4.s:
somaḥ sravati yāvacca pañcānāṃ cakrapaddhatiḥ /
tatpunaḥ pibati prītyā haṃso haṃsa iti sphuran // 136
4.d:
सोमः स्रवति यावच्च पञ्चानां चक्रपद्धतिः ।
तत्पुनः पिबति प्रीत्या हंसो हंस इति स्फुरन् ॥ 136
4.m: the moon, flows as far as the path of the five wheels; / and that again the Haṃsa drinks with delight, throbbing as 'haṃsa haṃsa'.

4.s:
sakṛdyasya tu saṃśrutyā puṇyapāpairna lipyate /
pañcāre savikāro'tha bhūtvā somasrutāmṛtāt // 137
4.d:
सकृद्यस्य तु संश्रुत्या पुण्यपापैर्न लिप्यते ।
पञ्चारे सविकारोऽथ भूत्वा सोमस्रुतामृतात् ॥ 137
4.m: Hearing this but once, one is not tainted by merits or sins. / Then, undergoing transformation in the five-spoked [wheel] from the nectar flowed by the moon,

4.s:
dhāvati trirasārāṇi guhyacakrāṇyasau vibhuḥ /
yato jātaṃ jagallīnaṃ yatra ca svakalīlayā // 138
4.d:
धावति त्रिरसाराणि गुह्यचक्राण्यसौ विभुः ।
यतो जातं जगल्लीनं यत्र च स्वकलीलया ॥ 138
4.m: this all-pervading Lord rushes to the secret wheels of three and six spokes, / from which the universe is born and into which it dissolves by His own play.

4.s:
tatrānandaśca sarvasya brahmacārī ca tatparaḥ /
tatra siddhiśca muktiśca samaṃ saṃprāpyate dvayam // 139
4.d:
तत्रानन्दश्च सर्वस्य ब्रह्मचारी च तत्परः ।
तत्र सिद्धिश्च मुक्तिश्च समं संप्राप्यते द्वयम् ॥ 139
4.m: There is the bliss of everything, and the celibate is intent upon it; / there, both spiritual accomplishment and liberation are attained simultaneously."

4.s:
ata ūrdhvaṃ punaryāti yāvadbrahmātmakaṃ padam /
agnīṣomau samau tatra sṛjyete cātmanātmani // 140
4.d:
अत ऊर्ध्वं पुनर्याति यावद्ब्रह्मात्मकं पदम् ।
अग्नीषोमौ समौ तत्र सृज्येते चात्मनात्मनि ॥ 140
4.m: From here it rises further, reaching up to the state identical with Brahman; / there fire and moon are created equal by the Self within the Self.

4.s:
tatrasthastāpitaḥ somo dvedhā jaṅghe vyavasthitaḥ /
adhastaṃ pātayedagniramṛtaṃ sravati kṣaṇāt // 141
4.d:
तत्रस्थस्तापितः सोमो द्वेधा जङ्घे व्यवस्थितः ।
अधस्तं पातयेदग्निरमृतं स्रवति क्षणात् ॥ 141
4.m: Residing there and heated, the moon stationed two-fold in the shanks / is cast downwards by the fire, and nectar flows in an instant.

4.s:
gulphajānvādiṣu vyaktaṃ kuṭilārkapradīpitā /
sā śaktistāpitā bhūyaḥ pañcārādikramaṃ sṛjet // 142
4.d:
गुल्फजान्वादिषु व्यक्तं कुटिलार्कप्रदीपिता ।
सा शक्तिस्तापिता भूयः पञ्चारादिक्रमं सृजेत् ॥ 142
4.m: Clearly kindled by the coiled sun in the ankles, knees, and so forth, / that heated power generates once again the sequence beginning with the five-spoked [wheel].

4.s:
evaṃ śrotre'pi vijñeyaṃ yāvatpādāntagocaram /
pādāṅguṣṭhātsamārabhya yāvadbrahmāṇḍadarśanam // 143
4.d:
एवं श्रोत्रेऽपि विज्ञेयं यावत्पादान्तगोचरम् ।
पादाङ्गुष्ठात्समारभ्य यावद्ब्रह्माण्डदर्शनम् ॥ 143
4.m: In this way it should be understood in the ear, as far as the range ending at the feet, / starting from the big toe of the foot up to the perception of the cosmic egg.

4.s:
ityajānannaiva yogī jānanviśvaprabhurbhavet /
jvalannivāsau brahmādyairdṛśyate parameśvaraḥ // 144
4.d:
इत्यजानन्नैव योगी जानन्विश्वप्रभुर्भवेत् ।
ज्वलन्निवासौ ब्रह्माद्यैर्दृश्यते परमेश्वरः ॥ 144
4.m: Not knowing this, one is no yogin at all; knowing it, one becomes the lord of the universe. / Blazing, as it were, this Supreme Lord is beheld by Brahmā and the others.

4.s:
atra tātparyataḥ proktamakṣe kramacatuṣṭayam /
ekaikatra yatastena dvādaśātmakatoditā // 145
4.d:
अत्र तात्पर्यतः प्रोक्तमक्षे क्रमचतुष्टयम् ।
एकैकत्र यतस्तेन द्वादशात्मकतोदिता ॥ 145
4.m: Here, essentially, a quadruple succession has been declared in each sense organ; / because it is present in each one, a twelvefold nature has thereby been proclaimed.

4.s:
na vyākhyātaṃ tu nirbhajya yato'tisarahasyakam /
meye'pi devī tiṣṭhantī māsarāśyādirūpiṇī // 146
4.d:
न व्याख्यातं तु निर्भज्य यतोऽतिसरहस्यकम् ।
मेयेऽपि देवी तिष्ठन्ती मासराश्यादिरूपिणी ॥ 146
4.m: It has not been explained in full detail, however, because it is deeply esoteric. / Even in the object of knowledge the goddess abides, taking the form of the months, zodiacal signs, and so on.

4.s:
ata eṣā sthitā saṃvidantarbāhyobhayātmanā /
svayaṃ nirbhāsya tatrānyadbhāsayantīva bhāsate // 147
4.d:
अत एषा स्थिता संविदन्तर्बाह्योभयात्मना ।
स्वयं निर्भास्य तत्रान्यद्भासयन्तीव भासते ॥ 147
4.m: Therefore this consciousness abides as both internal and external: / manifesting itself, it shines as though illuminating something else within itself.

4.s:
tataśca prāgiyaṃ śuddhā tathābhāsanasotsukā /
sṛṣṭiṃ kalayate devī tannāmnāgama ucyate // 148
4.d:
ततश्च प्रागियं शुद्धा तथाभासनसोत्सुका ।
सृष्टिं कलयते देवी तन्नाम्नागम उच्यते ॥ 148
4.m: And therefore, initially pure and eager to manifest in such a manner, / the goddess projects creation; she is designated by that name in the scripture.

4.s:
tathā bhāsitavastvaṃśarañjanāṃ sā bahirmukhī /
svavṛtticakreṇa samaṃ tato'pi kalayantyalam // 149
4.d:
तथा भासितवस्त्वंशरञ्जनां सा बहिर्मुखी ।
स्ववृत्तिचक्रेण समं ततोऽपि कलयन्त्यलम् ॥ 149
4.m: Directed outward, she colors the parts of the objects thus manifested; / along with the wheel of her own faculties, she then fully projects maintenance.

4.s:
sthitireṣaiva bhāvasya tāmantarmukhatārasāt /
saṃjihīrṣuḥ sthiternāśaṃ kalayantī nirucyate // 150
4.d:
स्थितिरेषैव भावस्य तामन्तर्मुखतारसात् ।
संजिहीर्षुः स्थितेर्नाशं कलयन्ती निरुच्यते ॥ 150
4.m: This very [process] is the persistence of an entity; through the savor of inward turning, / desiring to withdraw that [entity], she is described as projecting the destruction of its persistence.

4.s:
tato'pi saṃhārarase pūrṇe vighnakarīṃ svayam /
śaṅkāṃ yamātmikāṃ bhāge sūte saṃharate'pi ca // 151
4.d:
ततोऽपि संहाररसे पूर्णे विघ्नकरीं स्वयम् ।
शङ्कां यमात्मिकां भागे सूते संहरतेऽपि च ॥ 151
4.m: Even then, when the savor of withdrawal is full, she herself produces / and also withdraws doubt in the [objective] realm—a hinderer having the nature of Yama.

4.s:
saṃhṛtya śaṅkāṃ śaṅkyārthavarjaṃ vā bhāvamaṇḍale /
saṃhṛtiṃ kalayatyeva svātmavahnau vilāpanāt // 152
4.d:
संहृत्य शङ्कां शङ्क्यार्थवर्जं वा भावमण्डले ।
संहृतिं कलयत्येव स्वात्मवह्नौ विलापनात् ॥ 152
4.m: Having withdrawn doubt, or else excluding the object of doubt, in the circle of entities / she indeed projects dissolution through liquefaction into the fire of her own self.

4.s:
vilāpanātmikāṃ tāṃ ca bhāvasaṃhṛtimātmani /
āmṛśatyeva yenaiṣā mayā grastamiti sphuret // 153
4.d:
विलापनात्मिकां तां च भावसंहृतिमात्मनि ।
आमृशत्येव येनैषा मया ग्रस्तमिति स्फुरेत् ॥ 153
4.m: And within herself she directly grasps that dissolution of entities consisting of liquefaction, / so that this vibrant awareness pulses: “It has been swallowed by me.”

4.s:
saṃhāryopādhiretasyāḥ svasvabhāvo hi saṃvidaḥ /
nirupādhini saṃśuddhe saṃvidrūpeṣastamīyate // 154
4.d:
संहार्योपाधिरेतस्याः स्वस्वभावो हि संविदः ।
निरुपाधिनि संशुद्धे संविद्रूपेषस्तमीयते ॥ 154
4.m: For the limiting condition to be dissolved belongs to the very nature of this consciousness; / it comes to an end in the pure form of consciousness devoid of limiting conditions.

4.s:
vilāpite'pi bhāvaughe kaṃcidbhāvaṃ tadaiva sā /
āśyānayedya evāste śaṅkā saṃskārarūpakaḥ // 155
4.d:
विलापितेऽपि भावौघे कंचिद्भावं तदैव सा ।
आश्यानयेद्य एवास्ते शङ्का संस्काररूपकः ॥ 155
4.m: Even when the flood of entities is dissolved, she may at that very moment / solidify some entity that remains in the form of the residual trace of doubt.

4.s:
śubhāśubhatayā so'yaṃ soṣyate phalasaṃpadam /
pūrvaṃ hi bhogātpaścādvā śaṅkeyaṃ vyavatiṣṭhate // 156
4.d:
शुभाशुभतया सोऽयं सोष्यते फलसंपदम् ।
पूर्वं हि भोगात्पश्चाद्वा शङ्केयं व्यवतिष्ठते ॥ 156
4.m: In the form of the auspicious or inauspicious, this will yield an abundance of fruit; / for either before enjoyment or after, this doubt remains.

4.s:
anyadāśyānitamapi tadaiva drāvayediyam /
prāyaścittādikarmabhyo brahmahatyādikarmavat // 157
4.d:
अन्यदाश्यानितमपि तदैव द्रावयेदियम् ।
प्रायश्चित्तादिकर्मभ्यो ब्रह्महत्यादिकर्मवत् ॥ 157
4.m: Even what has been solidified at another time she may liquefy at that very moment, / just as actions such as the murder of a brahmin [are dissolved] through actions such as expiation.

4.s:
rodhanāddrāvaṇādrūpamitthaṃ kalayate citiḥ /
tadapi drāvayedeva tadapyāśyānayedatha // 158
4.d:
रोधनाद्द्रावणाद्रूपमित्थं कलयते चितिः ।
तदपि द्रावयेदेव तदप्याश्यानयेदथ ॥ 158
4.m: Consciousness thus projects form through obstruction and liquefaction; / it may also liquefy that very [form], or it may then solidify it.

4.s:
itthaṃ bhogye'pi saṃbhukte sati tatkaraṇānyapi /
saṃharantī kalayate dvādaśaivāhamātmani // 159
4.d:
इत्थं भोग्येऽपि संभुक्ते सति तत्करणान्यपि ।
संहरन्ती कलयते द्वादशैवाहमात्मनि ॥ 159
4.m: In this way, even when the object of enjoyment has been enjoyed, / she withdraws the instruments of that [enjoyment] and projects precisely twelve [forms] in the Self of “I”.

4.s:
karmabuddhyakṣavargo hi buddhyanto dvādaśātmakaḥ /
prakāśakatvātsūryātmā bhinne vastuni jṛmbhate // 160
4.d:
कर्मबुद्ध्यक्षवर्गो हि बुद्ध्यन्तो द्वादशात्मकः ।
प्रकाशकत्वात्सूर्यात्मा भिन्ने वस्तुनि जृम्भते ॥ 160
4.m: For the group of the senses of action and intellect, ending with the intellect, consists of twelve parts; / having the nature of the sun due to its illuminating power, it expands toward differentiated objects.

4.s:
ahaṃkārastu karaṇamabhimānaikasādhanam /
avicchinnaparāmarśī līyate tena tatra saḥ // 161
4.d:
अहंकारस्तु करणमभिमानैकसाधनम् ।
अविच्छिन्नपरामर्शी लीयते तेन तत्र सः ॥ 161
4.m: The ego, however, is the instrument whose sole function is appropriation; / having continuous reflective awareness, it dissolves therein.

4.s:
yathāhi khaṅgapāśādeḥ karaṇasya vibhedinaḥ /
abhedini svahastādau layastadvadayaṃ vidhiḥ // 162
4.d:
यथाहि खङ्गपाशादेः करणस्य विभेदिनः ।
अभेदिनि स्वहस्तादौ लयस्तद्वदयं विधिः ॥ 162
4.m: For just as an instrument that produces division, such as a sword or noose, / dissolves into that which is undivided, such as one's own hand, so too is this rule.

4.s:
tenendriyaughamārtaṇḍamaṇḍalaṃ kalayetsvayam /
saṃviddevī svatantratvātkalpite'haṃkṛtātmani // 163
4.d:
तेनेन्द्रियौघमार्तण्डमण्डलं कलयेत्स्वयम् ।
संविद्देवी स्वतन्त्रत्वात्कल्पितेऽहंकृतात्मनि ॥ 163
4.m: Therefore the goddess of consciousness, by virtue of her autonomy, projects / the solar orb of the senses into the fabricated self of the ego.

4.s:
sa eva paramādityaḥ pūrṇakalpastrayodaśaḥ /
karaṇatvātprayātyeva kartari pralayaṃ sphuṭam // 164
4.d:
स एव परमादित्यः पूर्णकल्पस्त्रयोदशः ।
करणत्वात्प्रयात्येव कर्तरि प्रलयं स्फुटम् ॥ 164
4.m: He alone is the supreme sun, nearly complete, the thirteenth; / because it is an instrument, it clearly undergoes dissolution in the agent.

4.s:
kartā ca dvividhaḥ proktaḥ kalpitākalpitātmakaḥ /
kalpito dehabuddhyādivyavacchedena carcitaḥ // 165
4.d:
कर्ता च द्विविधः प्रोक्तः कल्पिताकल्पितात्मकः ।
कल्पितो देहबुद्ध्यादिव्यवच्छेदेन चर्चितः ॥ 165
4.m: And the agent is declared to be of two kinds: having a fabricated nature and an unfabricated nature. / The fabricated one is considered through delimitation by the body, intellect, and so forth.

4.s:
kālāgnirudrasaṃjñāsya śāstreṣu paribhāṣitā /
kālo vyavacchittadyukto vahnirbhoktā yataḥ smṛtaḥ // 166
4.d:
कालाग्निरुद्रसंज्ञास्य शास्त्रेषु परिभाषिता ।
कालो व्यवच्छित्तद्युक्तो वह्निर्भोक्ता यतः स्मृतः ॥ 166
4.m: His designation in the scriptures is defined as Kālāgnirudra; / for Time (kāla) is endowed with delimitation, and Fire (agni) is remembered as the enjoyer.

4.s:
saṃsārāklṛptiklṛptibhyāṃ rodhanāddrāvaṇātprabhuḥ /
anivṛttapaśūbhāvastatrāhaṃkṛtpralīyate // 167
4.d:
संसाराक्लृप्तिक्लृप्तिभ्यां रोधनाद्द्रावणात्प्रभुः ।
अनिवृत्तपशूभावस्तत्राहंकृत्प्रलीयते ॥ 167
4.m: Through the non-construction and construction of saṃsāra, through obstruction and liquefaction, the Lord / whose condition as a bound soul has not ceased dissolves the ego therein.

4.s:
so'pi kalpitavṛttitvādviśvābhedaikaśālini /
vikāsini mahākāle līyate'hamidaṃmaye // 168
4.d:
सोऽपि कल्पितवृत्तित्वाद्विश्वाभेदैकशालिनि ।
विकासिनि महाकाले लीयतेऽहमिदंमये ॥ 168
4.m: Even he, having a fabricated activity, dissolves into the blossoming Mahākāla, / who is characterized solely by non-differentiation from the universe and consists of “I” and “this”.

4.s:
etasyāṃ svātmasaṃvittāvidaṃ sarvamahaṃ vibhuḥ /
iti pravikasadrūpā saṃvittiravabhāsate // 169
4.d:
एतस्यां स्वात्मसंवित्ताविदं सर्वमहं विभुः ।
इति प्रविकसद्रूपा संवित्तिरवभासते ॥ 169
4.m: In this consciousness of one's own Self, consciousness shines forth / in an expanding form, [aware that] “All this am I, the all-pervading Lord.”

4.s:
tato'ntaḥsthitasarvātmabhāvabhogoparāgiṇī /
paripūrṇāpi saṃvittirakule dhāmni līyate // 170
4.d:
ततोऽन्तःस्थितसर्वात्मभावभोगोपरागिणी ।
परिपूर्णापि संवित्तिरकुले धाम्नि लीयते ॥ 170
4.m: Then, colored by the enjoyment of all universal states resting within, / consciousness, though completely full, dissolves in the Akula abode.

4.s:
pramātṛvargo mānaughaḥ pramāśca bahudhā sthitāḥ /
meyaugha iti yatsarvamatra cinmātrameva tat // 171
4.d:
प्रमातृवर्गो मानौघः प्रमाश्च बहुधा स्थिताः ।
मेयौघ इति यत्सर्वमत्र चिन्मात्रमेव तत् ॥ 171
4.m: The class of knowers, the flood of means of knowledge, the diverse forms of valid cognition, / and the flood of knowables—all that is here nothing but pure consciousness.

4.s:
iyatīṃ rūpavaicitrīmāśrayantyāḥ svasaṃvidaḥ /
svācchandyamanapekṣaṃ yatsā parā parameśvarī // 172
4.d:
इयतीं रूपवैचित्रीमाश्रयन्त्याः स्वसंविदः ।
स्वाच्छन्द्यमनपेक्षं यत्सा परा परमेश्वरी ॥ 172
4.m: That independent, unconditioned freedom of one's own consciousness, / which resorts to such variety of form, is the supreme Goddess.

4.s:
imāḥ prāguktakalanāstadvijṛmbhocyate yataḥ /
kṣepo jñānaṃ ca saṃkhyānaṃ gatirnāda iti kramāt // 173
4.d:
इमाः प्रागुक्तकलनास्तद्विजृम्भोच्यते यतः ।
क्षेपो ज्ञानं च संख्यानं गतिर्नाद इति क्रमात् ॥ 173
4.m: For these aforesaid projections are said to be her expansion: / casting out, knowing, counting, motion, and sound, in succession.

4.s:
svātmano bhedanaṃ kṣepo bheditasyāvikalpanam /
jñānaṃ vikalpaḥ saṃkhyānamanyato vyatibhedanāt // 174
4.d:
स्वात्मनो भेदनं क्षेपो भेदितस्याविकल्पनम् ।
ज्ञानं विकल्पः संख्यानमन्यतो व्यतिभेदनात् ॥ 174
4.m: Casting out (kṣepa) is the differentiation of oneself; knowing (jñāna) is the non-differentiation of what has been differentiated; / counting (saṃkhyāna) is conceptual thought, through distinct differentiation from another;

4.s:
gatiḥ svarūpārohitvaṃ pratibimbavadeva yat /
nādaḥ svātmaparāmarśaśeṣatā tadvilopanāt // 175
4.d:
गतिः स्वरूपारोहित्वं प्रतिबिम्बवदेव यत् ।
नादः स्वात्मपरामर्शशेषता तद्विलोपनात् ॥ 175
4.m: motion (gati) is the ascending into one's own essential nature, just like a reflection; / sound (nāda) is the remaining as reflective awareness of one's Self, through the dissolution of that [reflected image].

4.s:
iti pañcavidhāmenāṃ kalanāṃ kurvatī parā /
devī kālī tathā kālakarṣiṇī ceti kathyate // 176
4.d:
इति पञ्चविधामेनां कलनां कुर्वती परा ।
देवी काली तथा कालकर्षिणी चेति कथ्यते ॥ 176
4.m: Performing this fivefold projection, the supreme / Goddess is called Kālī as well as Kālakarṣiṇī.

4.s:
mātṛsadbhāvasaṃjñāsyāstenoktā yatpramātṛṣu /
etāvadantasaṃvittau pramātṛtvaṃ sphuṭībhavet // 177
4.d:
मातृसद्भावसंज्ञास्यास्तेनोक्ता यत्प्रमातृषु ।
एतावदन्तसंवित्तौ प्रमातृत्वं स्फुटीभवेत् ॥ 177
4.m: Her designation as “Mātṛsadbhāva” (the True Essence of the Mothers) is stated because in knowing subjects, / subjectivity becomes clear only when consciousness extends this far.

4.s:
vāmeśvarīti-śabdena proktā śrīniśisaṃcare /
itthaṃ dvādaśadhā saṃvittiṣṭhantī viśvamātṛṣu // 178
4.d:
वामेश्वरीति-शब्देन प्रोक्ता श्रीनिशिसंचरे ।
इत्थं द्वादशधा संवित्तिष्ठन्ती विश्वमातृषु ॥ 178
4.m: She is proclaimed by the word Vāmeśvarī in the venerable Niśisaṃcāra. / Abiding in this manner in twelve modes among the knowers of the universe,

4.s:
ekaiveti na ko'pyasyāḥ kramasya niyamaḥ kvacit /
kramābhāvānna yugapattadabhāvātkramo'pi na // 179
4.d:
एकैवेति न कोऽप्यस्याः क्रमस्य नियमः क्वचित् ।
क्रमाभावान्न युगपत्तदभावात्क्रमोऽपि न ॥ 179
4.m: she is only one; thus there is no fixed rule anywhere regarding her succession. / Because there is no succession, there is no simultaneity; and because that is absent, there is not even succession.

4.s:
kramākramakathātītaṃ saṃvittattvaṃ sunirmalam /
tadasyāḥ saṃvido devyā yatra kvāpi pravartanam // 180
4.d:
क्रमाक्रमकथातीतं संवित्तत्त्वं सुनिर्मलम् ।
तदस्याः संविदो देव्या यत्र क्वापि प्रवर्तनम् ॥ 180
4.m: The principle of consciousness, utterly pure, transcends talk of succession and non-succession; / therefore, wherever this goddess of consciousness operates,

4.s:
tatra tādātmyayogena pūjā pūrṇaiva vartate /
parāmarśasvabhāvatvādetasyā yaḥ svayaṃ dhvaniḥ // 181
4.d:
तत्र तादात्म्ययोगेन पूजा पूर्णैव वर्तते ।
परामर्शस्वभावत्वादेतस्या यः स्वयं ध्वनिः ॥ 181
4.m: right there worship occurs fully through identification [with her]. / The spontaneous sound that exists, because her essential nature is reflective awareness,

4.s:
sadoditaḥ sa evoktaḥ paramaṃ hṛdayaṃ mahat /
hṛdaye svavimarśo'sau drāvitāśeṣaviśvakaḥ // 182
4.d:
सदोदितः स एवोक्तः परमं हृदयं महत् ।
हृदये स्वविमर्शोऽसौ द्राविताशेषविश्वकः ॥ 182
4.m: and which is ever-risen, is declared to be the supreme, great Heart. / In the Heart, that reflective awareness of oneself, which has liquefied the entire universe,

4.s:
bhāvagrahādiparyantabhāvī sāmānyasaṃjñakaḥ /
spandaḥ sa kathyate śāstre svātmanyucchalanātmakaḥ // 183
4.d:
भावग्रहादिपर्यन्तभावी सामान्यसंज्ञकः ।
स्पन्दः स कथ्यते शास्त्रे स्वात्मन्युच्छलनात्मकः ॥ 183
4.m: and exists right up to the grasping of objects, is called the universal; / in scripture it is called spanda, which consists in surging up within oneself.

4.s:
kiṃciccalanametāvadananyasphuraṇaṃ hi yat /
ūrmireṣā vibodhābdherna saṃvidanayā vinā // 184
4.d:
किंचिच्चलनमेतावदनन्यस्फुरणं हि यत् ।
ऊर्मिरेषा विबोधाब्धेर्न संविदनया विना ॥ 184
4.m: For that subtle movement is just this: the vibrant radiance that is non-different [from consciousness]. / This is the wave of the ocean of awakening; without it there is no consciousness.

4.s:
nistaraṅgataraṅgādivṛttireva hi sindhutā /
sārametatsamastasya yaccitsāraṃ jaḍaṃ jagat // 185
4.d:
निस्तरङ्गतरङ्गादिवृत्तिरेव हि सिन्धुता ।
सारमेतत्समस्तस्य यच्चित्सारं जडं जगत् ॥ 185
4.m: For being an ocean consists precisely in the states of wavelessness, waves, and the like. / This is the essence of all: that the insentient universe has consciousness as its essence.

4.s:
tadadhīnapratiṣṭhatvāttatsāraṃ hṛdayaṃ mahat /
tathā hi sadidaṃ brahmamūlaṃ māyāṇḍasaṃjñitam // 186
4.d:
तदधीनप्रतिष्ठत्वात्तत्सारं हृदयं महत् ।
तथा हि सदिदं ब्रह्ममूलं मायाण्डसंज्ञितम् ॥ 186
4.m: Because its subsistence depends upon it, its essence is the great heart. / For this existing world, rooted in Brahman, is termed the cosmic egg of Māyā.

4.s:
icchājñānakriyārohaṃ vinā naiva saducyate /
tacchaktitritayārohādbhairavīye cidātmani // 187
4.d:
इच्छाज्ञानक्रियारोहं विना नैव सदुच्यते ।
तच्छक्तित्रितयारोहाद्भैरवीये चिदात्मनि ॥ 187
4.m: Without ascending into will, knowledge, and action, it is not spoken of as existing at all. / From ascending into this triad of powers within the conscious self belonging to Bhairava,

4.s:
visṛjyate hi tattasmādbahirvātha visṛjyate /
evaṃ sadrūpataivaiṣāṃ satāṃ śaktitrayātmatām // 188
4.d:
विसृज्यते हि तत्तस्माद्बहिर्वाथ विसृज्यते ।
एवं सद्रूपतैवैषां सतां शक्तित्रयात्मताम् ॥ 188
4.m: it is indeed emitted from it, or rather, it is emitted externally. / Thus, the very state of existence of these real entities is the nature of the triad of powers,

4.s:
visargaṃ parabodhena samākṣipyaiva vartate /
tatsadeva bahīrūpaṃ prāgbodhāgnivilāpitam // 189
4.d:
विसर्गं परबोधेन समाक्षिप्यैव वर्तते ।
तत्सदेव बहीरूपं प्राग्बोधाग्निविलापितम् ॥ 189
4.m: and abides precisely by comprehending creative emission through supreme awakening. / That very real entity, appearing externally, is first dissolved in the fire of awakening;

4.s:
antarnadatparāmarśaśeṣībhūtaṃ tato'pyalam /
khātmatvameva saṃprāptaṃ śaktitritayagocarāt // 190
4.d:
अन्तर्नदत्परामर्शशेषीभूतं ततोऽप्यलम् ।
खात्मत्वमेव संप्राप्तं शक्तित्रितयगोचरात् ॥ 190
4.m: reduced to the residue of reflective awareness sounding internally, and then thoroughly / attaining the very nature of empty space from the domain of the triad of powers,

4.s:
vedanātmakatāmetya saṃhārātmani līyate /
idaṃ saṃhārahṛdayaṃ prācyaṃ sṛṣṭau ca hṛnmatam // 191
4.d:
वेदनात्मकतामेत्य संहारात्मनि लीयते ।
इदं संहारहृदयं प्राच्यं सृष्टौ च हृन्मतम् ॥ 191
4.m: it reaches the nature of pure knowing and dissolves in the self of reabsorption. / This is considered the heart of reabsorption, and the heart previously mentioned in emission.

4.s:
etadrūpaparāmarśamakṛtrimamanābilam /
ahamityāhureṣaiva prakāśasya prakāśatā // 192
4.d:
एतद्रूपपरामर्शमकृत्रिममनाबिलम् ।
अहमित्याहुरेषैव प्रकाशस्य प्रकाशता ॥ 192
4.m: They call this genuine, unclouded reflective awareness of such a nature / 'I'; this alone is the luminosity of luminosity.

4.s:
etadvīryaṃ hi sarveṣāṃ mantrāṇāṃ hṛdayātmakam /
vinānena jaḍāste syurjīvā iva vinā hṛdā // 193
4.d:
एतद्वीर्यं हि सर्वेषां मन्त्राणां हृदयात्मकम् ।
विनानेन जडास्ते स्युर्जीवा इव विना हृदा ॥ 193
4.m: For this is the potency of all mantras, consisting of the heart. / Without it, they would be insentient, like living beings without a heart.

4.s:
akṛtrimaitaddhṛdayārūḍho yatkiṃcidācaret /
prāṇyādvā mṛśate vāpi sa sarvo'sya japo mataḥ // 194
4.d:
अकृत्रिमैतद्धृदयारूढो यत्किंचिदाचरेत् ।
प्राण्याद्वा मृशते वापि स सर्वोऽस्य जपो मतः ॥ 194
4.m: Whatever one who has mounted this genuine heart may perform, / or whether he breathes or perceives, all that is considered his repetition of mantra.

4.s:
yadeva svecchayā sṛṣṭisvābhāvyādbahirantarā /
nirmīyate tadevāsya dhyānaṃ syātpāramārthikam // 195
4.d:
यदेव स्वेच्छया सृष्टिस्वाभाव्याद्बहिरन्तरा ।
निर्मीयते तदेवास्य ध्यानं स्यात्पारमार्थिकम् ॥ 195
4.m: Whatever is created externally or internally by his own will through the inherent nature of emission, / that alone would be his ultimate meditation.

4.s:
nirākāre hi ciddhāmni viśvākṛtimaye sati /
phalārthināṃ kācideva dhyeyatvenākṛtiḥ sthitā // 196
4.d:
निराकारे हि चिद्धाम्नि विश्वाकृतिमये सति ।
फलार्थिनां काचिदेव ध्येयत्वेनाकृतिः स्थिता ॥ 196
4.m: Indeed, when the formless realm of consciousness consists of all forms, / only a particular form is established as an object of meditation for those who seek fruit.

4.s:
yathā hyabhedātpūrṇe'pi bhāve jalamupāharan /
anyākṛtyapahānena ghaṭamarthayate rasāt // 197
4.d:
यथा ह्यभेदात्पूर्णेऽपि भावे जलमुपाहरन् ।
अन्याकृत्यपहानेन घटमर्थयते रसात् ॥ 197
4.m: Just as someone fetching water, though reality is full in its non-difference, / eagerly seeks a pot, disregarding other forms,

4.s:
tathaiva parameśānaniyatipravijṛmbhaṇāt /
kācidevākṛtiḥ kāṃcit sūte phalavikalpanām // 198
4.d:
तथैव परमेशाननियतिप्रविजृम्भणात् ।
काचिदेवाकृतिः कांचित् सूते फलविकल्पनाम् ॥ 198
4.m: so, too, through the unfolding of the Supreme Lord's restriction, / a particular form generates a particular conceptualization of fruit.

4.s:
yastu saṃpūrṇahṛdayo na phalaṃ nāma vāñchati /
tasya viśvākṛtirdevī sā cāvacchedavarjanāt // 199
4.d:
यस्तु संपूर्णहृदयो न फलं नाम वाञ्छति ।
तस्य विश्वाकृतिर्देवी सा चावच्छेदवर्जनात् ॥ 199
4.m: However, for one whose heart is complete and who desires no fruit at all, / the goddess possesses every form, and that because of the absence of limitation.

4.s:
kule yogina udriktabhairavīyaparāsavāt /
ghūrṇitasya sthitirdehe mudrā yā kācideva sā // 200
4.d:
कुले योगिन उद्रिक्तभैरवीयपरासवात् ।
घूर्णितस्य स्थितिर्देहे मुद्रा या काचिदेव सा ॥ 200
4.m: Whatever position in the body of a yogi in the Kula, reeling / from the heightened, supreme liquor of Bhairava, that alone is a mudrā.

4.s:
antarindhanasaṃbhāramanapekṣyaiva nityaśaḥ /
jājvalītyakhilākṣaughaprasṛtograśikhaḥ śikhī // 201
4.d:
अन्तरिन्धनसंभारमनपेक्ष्यैव नित्यशः ।
जाज्वलीत्यखिलाक्षौघप्रसृतोग्रशिखः शिखी ॥ 201
4.m: Disregarding entirely the internal accumulation of fuel at all times, / the fire blazes forth, its fierce flames spreading through the entire host of sense organs.

4.s:
bodhāgnau tādṛśe bhāvā viśantastasya sanmahaḥ /
udrecayanto gacchanti homakarmanimittatām // 202
4.d:
बोधाग्नौ तादृशे भावा विशन्तस्तस्य सन्महः ।
उद्रेचयन्तो गच्छन्ति होमकर्मनिमित्तताम् ॥ 202
4.m: Entering into such a fire of awakening, entities, increasing / its true majesty, become the cause of the rite of oblation.

4.s:
yaṃ kaṃcitparameśānaśaktipātapavitritam /
purobhāvya svayaṃ tiṣṭheduktavaddīkṣitastu saḥ // 203
4.d:
यं कंचित्परमेशानशक्तिपातपवित्रितम् ।
पुरोभाव्य स्वयं तिष्ठेदुक्तवद्दीक्षितस्तु सः ॥ 203
4.m: Placing before oneself whomever has been purified by the descent of power of the Supreme Lord, / one should abide as described; he is indeed initiated.

4.s:
japyādau homaparyante yadyapyekaikakarmaṇi /
udeti rūḍhiḥ paramā tathāpītthaṃ nirūpitam // 204
4.d:
जप्यादौ होमपर्यन्ते यद्यप्येकैककर्मणि ।
उदेति रूढिः परमा तथापीत्थं निरूपितम् ॥ 204
4.m: Although supreme firm establishment arises in each single ritual, / from repetition of mantra up to the oblation, nevertheless it has been explained in this way:

4.s:
yathāhi tatra tatrāśvaḥ samanimnonnatādiṣu /
citre deśe vāhyamāno yātīcchāmātrakalpitām // 205
4.d:
यथाहि तत्र तत्राश्वः समनिम्नोन्नतादिषु ।
चित्रे देशे वाह्यमानो यातीच्छामात्रकल्पिताम् ॥ 205
4.m: Just as a horse, being ridden here and there over varied terrain, / even, low, or raised, goes in a manner formed merely by will,

4.s:
tathā saṃvidvicitrābhiḥ śāntaghoratarādibhiḥ /
bhaṅgībhirabhito dvaitaṃ tyājitā bhairavāyate // 206
4.d:
तथा संविद्विचित्राभिः शान्तघोरतरादिभिः ।
भङ्गीभिरभितो द्वैतं त्याजिता भैरवायते ॥ 206
4.m: so consciousness, made to abandon duality completely through varied / modes, peaceful, extremely terrible, and so forth, acts as Bhairava.

4.s:
yathā puraḥsthe mukure nijaṃ vaktraṃ vibhāvayan /
bhūyo bhūyastadekātma vaktraṃ vetti nijātmanaḥ // 207
4.d:
यथा पुरःस्थे मुकुरे निजं वक्त्रं विभावयन् ।
भूयो भूयस्तदेकात्म वक्त्रं वेत्ति निजात्मनः ॥ 207
4.m: Just as one, contemplating his own face in a mirror placed before him, / repeatedly recognizes that very face of his own self as one with it,

4.s:
tathā vikalpamukure dhyānapūjārcanātmani /
ātmānaṃ bhairavaṃ paśyannacirāttanmayībhavet // 208
4.d:
तथा विकल्पमुकुरे ध्यानपूजार्चनात्मनि ।
आत्मानं भैरवं पश्यन्नचिरात्तन्मयीभवेत् ॥ 208
4.m: so, seeing oneself as Bhairava in the mirror of conceptual construct / consisting of meditation, worship, and veneration, one soon becomes identical with that.

4.s:
tanmayībhavanaṃ nāma prāptiḥ sānuttarātmani /
pūrṇatvasya parā kāṣṭhā setyatra na phalāntaram // 209
4.d:
तन्मयीभवनं नाम प्राप्तिः सानुत्तरात्मनि ।
पूर्णत्वस्य परा काष्ठा सेत्यत्र न फलान्तरम् ॥ 209
4.m: Becoming identical with that means attainment in the unexcelled Self; / that is the supreme summit of fullness, so there is no other fruit here.

4.s:
phalaṃ sarvamapūrṇatve tatra tatra prakalpitam /
akalpite hi pūrṇatve phalamanyatkimucyatām // 210
4.d:
फलं सर्वमपूर्णत्वे तत्र तत्र प्रकल्पितम् ।
अकल्पिते हि पूर्णत्वे फलमन्यत्किमुच्यताम् ॥ 210
4.m: All fruit is imagined only in the state of incompleteness in various contexts; / when fullness is unconstructed, what other fruit could be spoken of?

4.s:
eṣa yāgavidhiḥ ko'pi kasyāpi hṛdi vartate /
yasya prasīdecciccakraṃ drāgapaścimajanmanaḥ // 211
4.d:
एष यागविधिः कोऽपि कस्यापि हृदि वर्तते ।
यस्य प्रसीदेच्चिच्चक्रं द्रागपश्चिमजन्मनः ॥ 211
4.m: This extraordinary rule of sacrifice dwells in the heart of someone / for whom the wheel of consciousness quickly becomes gracious, whose current birth is the last.

4.s:
atra yāge gato rūḍhiṃ kaivalyamadhigacchati /
lokairālokyamāno hi dehabandhavidhau sthitaḥ // 212
4.d:
अत्र यागे गतो रूढिं कैवल्यमधिगच्छति ।
लोकैरालोक्यमानो हि देहबन्धविधौ स्थितः ॥ 212
4.m: Attaining firm establishment in this sacrifice, one reaches isolation, / even while being seen by people and abiding in the condition of the bodily bond.

4.s:
atra nāthaḥ samācāraṃ paṭale'ṣṭādaśe'bhyadhāt /
nātra śuddhirna cāśuddhirna bhakṣyādivicāraṇam // 213
4.d:
अत्र नाथः समाचारं पटलेऽष्टादशेऽभ्यधात् ।
नात्र शुद्धिर्न चाशुद्धिर्न भक्ष्यादिविचारणम् ॥ 213
4.m: Here, in the eighteenth chapter, the Lord declared the traditional practice: / 'Here there is neither purity nor impurity, nor consideration of edible food and the like,

4.s:
na dvaitaṃ nāpi cādvaitaṃ liṅgapūjādikaṃ na ca /
na cāpi tatparityāgo niṣparigrahatāpi vā // 214
4.d:
न द्वैतं नापि चाद्वैतं लिङ्गपूजादिकं न च ।
न चापि तत्परित्यागो निष्परिग्रहतापि वा ॥ 214
4.m: neither duality nor non-duality, neither worship of the liṅga and the like / nor its abandonment, neither lack of possessions

4.s:
saparigrahatā vāpi jaṭābhasmādisaṃgrahaḥ /
tattyāgo na vratādīnāṃ caraṇācaraṇaṃ ca yat // 215
4.d:
सपरिग्रहता वापि जटाभस्मादिसंग्रहः ।
तत्त्यागो न व्रतादीनां चरणाचरणं च यत् ॥ 215
4.m: nor having possessions, taking up matted hair, ashes, and so forth, / nor abandoning them, neither the practice nor non-practice of observances and the like,

4.s:
kṣetrādisaṃpraveśaśca samayādiprapālanam /
parasvarūpaliṅgādi nāmagotrādikaṃ ca yat // 216
4.d:
क्षेत्रादिसंप्रवेशश्च समयादिप्रपालनम् ।
परस्वरूपलिङ्गादि नामगोत्रादिकं च यत् ॥ 216
4.m: neither entering sacred fields and such places, nor keeping the rules, / neither the insignia and so forth of another's nature, nor name, lineage, and the like.

4.s:
nāsminvidhīyate kiṃcinna cāpi pratiṣidhyate /
vihitaṃ sarvamevātra pratiṣiddhamathāpi ca // 217
4.d:
नास्मिन्विधीयते किंचिन्न चापि प्रतिषिध्यते ।
विहितं सर्वमेवात्र प्रतिषिद्धमथापि च ॥ 217
4.m: Nothing is prescribed in this, nor is anything prohibited; / everything is indeed prescribed here, and likewise prohibited.

4.s:
kiṃ tvetadatra deveśi niyamena vidhīyate /
tattve cetaḥ sthirīkāryaṃ suprasannena yoginā // 218
4.d:
किं त्वेतदत्र देवेशि नियमेन विधीयते ।
तत्त्वे चेतः स्थिरीकार्यं सुप्रसन्नेन योगिना ॥ 218
4.m: Rather, O Queen of the Gods, this is prescribed here as a rule: / the mind must be made firm in reality by the perfectly tranquil yogi.

4.s:
tacca yasya yathaiva syātsa tathaiva samācaret /
tattve niścalacittastu bhuñjāno viṣayānapi // 219
4.d:
तच्च यस्य यथैव स्यात्स तथैव समाचरेत् ।
तत्त्वे निश्चलचित्तस्तु भुञ्जानो विषयानपि ॥ 219
4.m: And in whatever way that may happen for anyone, he should act precisely in that way. / But one whose mind is motionless in reality, even while enjoying sense objects,

4.s:
na saṃspṛśyeta doṣaiḥ sa padmapatramivāmbhasā /
viṣāpahārimantrādisaṃnaddho bhakṣayannapi // 220
4.d:
न संस्पृश्येत दोषैः स पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ।
विषापहारिमन्त्रादिसंनद्धो भक्षयन्नपि ॥ 220
4.m: is not touched by faults, just as a lotus leaf is not touched by water. / Even when consuming poison, one who is protected by poison-dispelling mantras and the like

4.s:
viṣaṃ na muhyate tena tadvadyogī mahāmatiḥ /
aśuddhaṃ hi kathaṃ nāma dehādyaṃ pāñcabhautikam // 221
4.d:
विषं न मुह्यते तेन तद्वद्योगी महामतिः ।
अशुद्धं हि कथं नाम देहाद्यं पाञ्चभौतिकम् ॥ 221
4.m: is not bewildered by it; in the same way the yogi of great intellect [is unaffected]. / For how indeed could the body and the like, made of the five elements, be impure?

4.s:
prakāśatātirikte kiṃ śuddhyaśuddhī hi vastunaḥ /
aśuddhasya ca bhāvasya śuddhiḥ syāttādṛśaiva kim // 222
4.d:
प्रकाशतातिरिक्ते किं शुद्ध्यशुद्धी हि वस्तुनः ।
अशुद्धस्य च भावस्य शुद्धिः स्यात्तादृशैव किम् ॥ 222
4.m: Can purity and impurity belong to an entity beyond luminosity? / And could the purification of an impure entity be of the same nature?

4.s:
anyonyāśrayavaiyarthyānavasthā itthamatra hi /
