pṛthivī jalataḥ śuddhyejjalaṃ dharaṇitastathā // 223
4.d:
अन्योन्याश्रयवैयर्थ्यानवस्था इत्थमत्र हि ।
पृथिवी जलतः शुद्ध्येज्जलं धरणितस्तथा ॥ 223
4.m: Thus, here there would be mutual dependence, futility, and infinite regress. / Earth would be purified by water, and water in turn by earth—

4.s:
anyonyāśrayatā seyamaśuddhatve'pyayaṃ kramaḥ /
aśuddhājjalataḥ śuddhyeddhareti vyarthatā bhavet // 224
4.d:
अन्योन्याश्रयता सेयमशुद्धत्वेऽप्ययं क्रमः ।
अशुद्धाज्जलतः शुद्ध्येद्धरेति व्यर्थता भवेत् ॥ 224
4.m: this is mutual dependence; this same sequence applies also to impurity: / if earth were purified by impure water, futility would result.

4.s:
vāyuto vāriṇo vāyostejasastasya vānyataḥ /
bahurūpādikā mantrāḥ pāvanātteṣu śuddhatā // 225
4.d:
वायुतो वारिणो वायोस्तेजसस्तस्य वान्यतः ।
बहुरूपादिका मन्त्राः पावनात्तेषु शुद्धता ॥ 225
4.m: [If water is purified] by air, or air by fire, or that by another [there is infinite regress]. / [If it is argued that] mantras such as the Bahurūpa are purifying, and so purity is in them,

4.s:
mantrāḥ svabhāvataḥ śuddhā yadi te'pi na kiṃ tathā /
śivātmatā teṣu śuddhiryadi tatrāpi sā na kim // 226
4.d:
मन्त्राः स्वभावतः शुद्धा यदि तेऽपि न किं तथा ।
शिवात्मता तेषु शुद्धिर्यदि तत्रापि सा न किम् ॥ 226
4.m: [then] if mantras are pure by nature, why are those [elements] not also so? / If their purity is their being identical with Śiva, why does that not exist there too?

4.s:
śivātmatvāparijñānaṃ na mantreṣu dharādivat /
te tena śuddhā iti cettajjñaptistarhi śuddhatā // 227
4.d:
शिवात्मत्वापरिज्ञानं न मन्त्रेषु धरादिवत् ।
ते तेन शुद्धा इति चेत्तज्ज्ञप्तिस्तर्हि शुद्धता ॥ 227
4.m: If it is said: 'In mantras, unlike earth and the like, there is no non-recognition of identity with Śiva, / and through that they are pure'—then knowledge of that is purity.

4.s:
yoginaṃ prati sā cāsti bhāveṣviti viśuddhatā /
nanu codanayā śuddhyaśuddhyādikaviniścayaḥ // 228
4.d:
योगिनं प्रति सा चास्ति भावेष्विति विशुद्धता ।
ननु चोदनया शुद्ध्यशुद्ध्यादिकविनिश्चयः ॥ 228
4.m: And that [knowledge] exists for the yogi with regard to [all] entities; thus there is complete purity. / If it is objected: 'Surely purity, impurity, and the like are determined by scriptural injunction?'—

4.s:
itthamastu tathāpyeṣā codanaiva śivoditā /
kā syātsatīti cedetadanyatra pravitānitam // 229
4.d:
इत्थमस्तु तथाप्येषा चोदनैव शिवोदिता ।
का स्यात्सतीति चेदेतदन्यत्र प्रवितानितम् ॥ 229
4.m: be it so! Even then, which can be the true injunction uttered by Śiva? / If asked, this has been expounded at length elsewhere.

4.s:
vaidikyā bādhiteyaṃ cedviparītaṃ na kiṃ bhavet /
samyakcenmanyase bādho viśiṣṭaviṣayatvataḥ // 230
4.d:
वैदिक्या बाधितेयं चेद्विपरीतं न किं भवेत् ।
सम्यक्चेन्मन्यसे बाधो विशिष्टविषयत्वतः ॥ 230
4.m: If it is said that this is sublated by Vedic injunction, why should it not be the reverse? / If you consider correctly, sublation must occur because it has a specific domain.

4.s:
apavādena kartavyaḥ sāmānyavihite vidhau /
śuddhyaśuddhī ca sāmānyavihite tattvabodhini // 231
4.d:
अपवादेन कर्तव्यः सामान्यविहिते विधौ ।
शुद्ध्यशुद्धी च सामान्यविहिते तत्त्वबोधिनि ॥ 231
4.m: A specific exception must override a rule laid down in general; / and purity and impurity are laid down in general for one who is being awakened to reality.

4.s:
puṃsi te bādhite eva tathā cātreti varṇitam /
nārthavādādiśaṅkā ca vākye māheśvare bhavet // 232
4.d:
पुंसि ते बाधिते एव तथा चात्रेति वर्णितम् ।
नार्थवादादिशङ्का च वाक्ये माहेश्वरे भवेत् ॥ 232
4.m:
for a person who knows the true principle, those two are indeed sublated, and so it has been explained here.
Moreover, in a statement of the Great Lord, there can be no suspicion of its being mere commendation or the like.

4.s:
abuddhipūrvaṃ hi tathā saṃsthite satataṃ bhavet /
vyomādirūpe nigame śaṅkā mithyārthatāṃ prati // 233
4.d:
अबुद्धिपूर्वं हि तथा संस्थिते सततं भवेत् ।
व्योमादिरूपे निगमे शङ्का मिथ्यार्थतां प्रति ॥ 233
4.m:
Indeed, suspicion regarding falsehood may constantly arise
in the Vedic tradition, which is established non-intentionally like empty space and the rest;

4.s:
anavacchinnavijñānavaiśvarūpyasunirbharaḥ /
śāstrātmanā sthito devo mithyātvaṃ kvāpi nārhati // 234
4.d:
अनवच्छिन्नविज्ञानवैश्वरूप्यसुनिर्भरः ।
शास्त्रात्मना स्थितो देवो मिथ्यात्वं क्वापि नार्हति ॥ 234
4.m:
the Lord, however, established in the form of scripture,
overflowing with the universal forms of unrestricted knowledge, never admits of falsehood anywhere.

4.s:
icchāvānbhāvarūpeṇa yathā tiṣṭhāsurīśvaraḥ /
tatsvarūpābhidhānena tiṣṭhāsuḥ sa tathā sthitaḥ // 235
4.d:
इच्छावान्भावरूपेण यथा तिष्ठासुरीश्वरः ।
तत्स्वरूपाभिधानेन तिष्ठासुः स तथा स्थितः ॥ 235
4.m:
Just as the Lord, endowed with will, chooses to abide in the form of existing entities,
so he stands choosing to abide by expressing their intrinsic nature.

4.s:
arthavādo'pi yatrānyavidhyādimukhamīkṣate /
tatrāstvasatyaḥ svātantrye sa eva tu vidhāyakaḥ // 236
4.d:
अर्थवादोऽपि यत्रान्यविध्यादिमुखमीक्षते ।
तत्रास्त्वसत्यः स्वातन्त्र्ये स एव तु विधायकः ॥ 236
4.m:
Even where a commendatory passage looks to the face of an injunction or the like,
let it be untrue there; but in absolute autonomy, it is itself an injunction.

4.s:
vidhivākyāntare gacchannaṅgabhāvamathāpi vā /
na nirarthakaṃ evāyaṃ saṃnidhergajaḍādivat // 237
4.d:
विधिवाक्यान्तरे गच्छन्नङ्गभावमथापि वा ।
न निरर्थकं एवायं संनिधेर्गजडादिवत् ॥ 237
4.m:
Or even when it becomes subordinate to another injunctive statement,
it is never merely meaningless by proximity, like ‘ga, ja, ḍa’ and so on.

4.s:
svārthapratyāyanaṃ cāsya svasaṃvittyaiva bhāsate /
tadapahnavanaṃ kartuṃ śakyaṃ vidhiniṣedhayoḥ // 238
4.d:
स्वार्थप्रत्यायनं चास्य स्वसंवित्त्यैव भासते ।
तदपह्नवनं कर्तुं शक्यं विधिनिषेधयोः ॥ 238
4.m:
Its conveying of its own meaning is revealed through one’s own consciousness alone;
can that be concealed in the case of injunctions and prohibitions?

4.s:
yuktiścātrāsti vākyeṣu svasaṃviccāpyabādhitā /
yā samagrārthamāṇikyatattvaniścayakāriṇī // 239
4.d:
युक्तिश्चात्रास्ति वाक्येषु स्वसंविच्चाप्यबाधिता ।
या समग्रार्थमाणिक्यतत्त्वनिश्चयकारिणी ॥ 239
4.m:
And here, in these statements, there is reasoning as well as unsublated self-awareness,
which brings about the ascertainment of the true nature of all objects, like gems.

4.s:
mṛtadehe'tha dehotthe yā cāśuddhiḥ prakīrtitā /
anyatra neti buddhyantāmaśuddhaṃ saṃvidaścyutam // 240
4.d:
मृतदेहेऽथ देहोत्थे या चाशुद्धिः प्रकीर्तिता ।
अन्यत्र नेति बुद्ध्यन्तामशुद्धं संविदश्च्युतम् ॥ 240
4.m:
And the impurity that is proclaimed regarding a dead body or what arises from the body,
and not elsewhere—let them understand that what has fallen from consciousness is the impure.

4.s:
saṃvittādātmyamāpannaṃ sarvaṃ śuddhamataḥ sthitam /
śrīmadvīrāvalau coktaṃ śuddhyaśuddhinirūpaṇe // 241
4.d:
संवित्तादात्म्यमापन्नं सर्वं शुद्धमतः स्थितम् ।
श्रीमद्वीरावलौ चोक्तं शुद्ध्यशुद्धिनिरूपणे ॥ 241
4.m:
Everything that has attained identity with consciousness is therefore established as pure.
And it is said in the venerable Vīrāvalī, in the determination of purity and impurity:

4.s:
sarveṣāṃ vāhako jīvo nāsti kiṃcidajīvakam /
yatkiṃcijjīvarahitamaśuddhaṃ tadvijānata // 242
4.d:
सर्वेषां वाहको जीवो नास्ति किंचिदजीवकम् ।
यत्किंचिज्जीवरहितमशुद्धं तद्विजानत ॥ 242
4.m:
‘Life is the bearer of all; there is nothing devoid of life.
Whatever is devoid of life—know that to be impure.’

4.s:
tasmādyatsaṃvido nātidūre tacchudvimāvahet /
avikalpena bhāvena munayo'pi tathābhavan // 243
4.d:
तस्माद्यत्संविदो नातिदूरे तच्छुद्विमावहेत् ।
अविकल्पेन भावेन मुनयोऽपि तथाभवन् ॥ 243
4.m:
Therefore, whatever is not too far from consciousness brings purity.
By means of a non-conceptual state, the sages too became like that.

4.s:
lokasaṃrakṣaṇārthaṃ tu tattattvaṃ taiḥ pragopitam /
bahiḥ satsvapi bhāveṣu śuddhyaśuddhī na nīlavat // 244
4.d:
लोकसंरक्षणार्थं तु तत्तत्त्वं तैः प्रगोपितम् ।
बहिः सत्स्वपि भावेषु शुद्ध्यशुद्धी न नीलवत् ॥ 244
4.m:
However, for the sake of preserving the world, that true reality was hidden by them.
Even though external entities exist, purity and impurity are not like the color blue;

4.s:
pramātṛdharma evāyaṃ cidaikyānaikyavedanāt /
yadi vā vastudharmo'pi mātrapekṣānibandhanaḥ // 245
4.d:
प्रमातृधर्म एवायं चिदैक्यानैक्यवेदनात् ।
यदि वा वस्तुधर्मोऽपि मात्रपेक्षानिबन्धनः ॥ 245
4.m:
this is a property of the subject alone, arising from the experience of unity or non-unity with consciousness;
or if it is also a property of the object, it is grounded upon the relative reference to a subject.

4.s:
sautrāmaṇyāṃ surā hotuḥ śuddhānyasya viparyayaḥ /
anena codanānāṃ ca svavākyairapi bādhanam // 246
4.d:
सौत्रामण्यां सुरा होतुः शुद्धान्यस्य विपर्ययः ।
अनेन चोदनानां च स्ववाक्यैरपि बाधनम् ॥ 246
4.m:
In the Sautrāmaṇī sacrifice, liquor is pure for the hotṛ priest, but the reverse for another.
By this, the sublation of scriptural injunctions even by their own statements

4.s:
kvacitsaṃdarśitaṃ brahmahatyāvidhiniṣedhavat /
bhakṣyādividhayo'pyenaṃ nyāyamāśritya carcitāḥ // 247
4.d:
क्वचित्संदर्शितं ब्रह्महत्याविधिनिषेधवत् ।
भक्ष्यादिविधयोऽप्येनं न्यायमाश्रित्य चर्चिताः ॥ 247
4.m:
has been shown in some instances, like the injunction and prohibition concerning the killing of a brahmin.
Injunctions regarding what may be eaten and so forth have also been discussed by taking recourse to this principle.

4.s:
sarvajñānottarādau ca bhāṣate sma maheśvaraḥ /
nararṣidevadruhiṇaviṣṇurudrādyudīritam // 248
4.d:
सर्वज्ञानोत्तरादौ च भाषते स्म महेश्वरः ।
नरर्षिदेवद्रुहिणविष्णुरुद्राद्युदीरितम् ॥ 248
4.m:
And in the Sarvajñānottara and other scriptures, the Great Lord declared:
‘That which is uttered by human beings, sages, gods, Druhiṇa, Viṣṇu, Rudra, and others,

4.s:
uttarottaravaiśiṣṭyāt pūrvapūrvaprabādhakam /
na śaivaṃ vaiṣṇavairvākyairbādhanīyaṃ kadācana // 249
4.d:
उत्तरोत्तरवैशिष्ट्यात् पूर्वपूर्वप्रबाधकम् ।
न शैवं वैष्णवैर्वाक्यैर्बाधनीयं कदाचन ॥ 249
4.m:
sublates each preceding one because of the superiority of each succeeding one.
Never should a Śaiva statement be sublated by Vaiṣṇava statements.

4.s:
vaiṣṇavaṃ brahmasaṃbhūtairnetyādi paricarcayet /
bādhate yo vaiparītyātsamūḍhaḥ pāpabhāgbhavet // 250
4.d:
वैष्णवं ब्रह्मसंभूतैर्नेत्यादि परिचर्चयेत् ।
बाधते यो वैपरीत्यात्समूढः पापभाग्भवेत् ॥ 250
4.m:
A Vaiṣṇava statement should not be investigated by those born of Brahmā,’ and so on.
One who sublates in reverse becomes bewildered and incurs sin.

4.s:
tasmānmukhyatayā skanda lokadharmānna cācaret /
nānyaśāstrasamuddiṣṭaṃ srotasyuktaṃ nije caret // 251
4.d:
तस्मान्मुख्यतया स्कन्द लोकधर्मान्न चाचरेत् ।
नान्यशास्त्रसमुद्दिष्टं स्रोतस्युक्तं निजे चरेत् ॥ 251
4.m:
‘Therefore, principally, O Skanda, one should not practice worldly norms;
one should not practice what is prescribed in another scripture, but practice what is declared in one’s own current.’

4.s:
yato yadyapi devena vedādyapi nirūpitam /
tathāpi kila saṃkocabhāvābhāvavikalpataḥ // 252
4.d:
यतो यद्यपि देवेन वेदाद्यपि निरूपितम् ।
तथापि किल संकोचभावाभावविकल्पतः ॥ 252
4.m:
Because, even though the Veda and other scriptures were also set forth by the Lord,
nonetheless, owing to the conceptual construction of the presence or absence of contraction,

4.s:
saṃkocatāratamyena pāśavaṃ jñānamīritam /
vikāsatāratamyena patijñānaṃ tu bādhakam // 253
4.d:
संकोचतारतम्येन पाशवं ज्ञानमीरितम् ।
विकासतारतम्येन पतिज्ञानं तु बाधकम् ॥ 253
4.m:
knowledge of the bound soul is stated according to the gradation of contraction,
whereas the Lord’s knowledge sublates it according to the gradation of expansion.

4.s:
idaṃ dvaitamidaṃ neti parasparaniṣedhataḥ /
māyīyabhedaklṛptaṃ tatsyādakālpanike katham // 254
4.d:
इदं द्वैतमिदं नेति परस्परनिषेधतः ।
मायीयभेदक्लृप्तं तत्स्यादकाल्पनिके कथम् ॥ 254
4.m:
Because of the mutual exclusion of ‘this is duality, this is not’,
that is constructed through illusory differentiation; how could it exist in what is non-conceptual?

4.s:
uktaṃ bhargaśikhāyāṃ ca mṛtyukālakalādikam /
dvaitādvaitavikalpotthaṃ grasate kṛtadhīriti // 255
4.d:
उक्तं भर्गशिखायां च मृत्युकालकलादिकम् ।
द्वैताद्वैतविकल्पोत्थं ग्रसते कृतधीरिति ॥ 255
4.m: And it is said in the Bhargaśikhā: / ‘The wise person swallows death, time, parts, and the rest, / which arise from the conceptual construct of duality and non-duality.’

4.s:
siddhānte liṅgapūjoktā viśvādhvamayatāvide /
kulādiṣu niṣiddhāsau dehe viśvātmatāvide // 256
4.d:
सिद्धान्ते लिङ्गपूजोक्ता विश्वाध्वमयताविदे ।
कुलादिषु निषिद्धासौ देहे विश्वात्मताविदे ॥ 256
4.m:
In the Siddhānta, the worship of the liṅga is taught for the sake of knowing the identity of the entire path;
in the Kula and other traditions, it is forbidden for the sake of knowing universal identity in the body.

4.s:
iha sarvātmake kasmāttadvidhipratiṣedhane /
niyamānupraveśena tādātmyapratipattaye // 257
4.d:
इह सर्वात्मके कस्मात्तद्विधिप्रतिषेधने ।
नियमानुप्रवेशेन तादात्म्यप्रतिपत्तये ॥ 257
4.m:
Here, in that which consists of everything, why should there be injunction and prohibition of it?
For the sake of realizing identity through entering into a restrictive rule.

4.s:
jaṭādi kaule tyāgo'sya sukhopāyopadeśataḥ /
vratacaryā ca mantrārthatādātmyapratipattaye // 258
4.d:
जटादि कौले त्यागोऽस्य सुखोपायोपदेशतः ।
व्रतचर्या च मन्त्रार्थतादात्म्यप्रतिपत्तये ॥ 258
4.m:
In the Kaula, the abandonment of matted hair and the like is taught because of its being an easy means,
and the observance of ascetic vows is for realizing identity with the meaning of the mantra.

4.s:
tanniṣedhastu mantrārthasārvātmyapratipattaye /
kṣetrapīṭhopapīṭheṣu praveśo vighnaśāntaye // 259
4.d:
तन्निषेधस्तु मन्त्रार्थसार्वात्म्यप्रतिपत्तये ।
क्षेत्रपीठोपपीठेषु प्रवेशो विघ्नशान्तये ॥ 259
4.m:
Its prohibition, however, is for realizing that the meaning of the mantra is all-encompassing.
Entering sacred fields, seats, and secondary seats is taught for the pacification of obstacles

4.s:
mantrādyārādhakasyātha tallābhāyopadiśyate /
kṣetrādigamanābhāvavidhistu svātmanastathā // 260
4.d:
मन्त्राद्याराधकस्याथ तल्लाभायोपदिश्यते ।
क्षेत्रादिगमनाभावविधिस्तु स्वात्मनस्तथा ॥ 260
4.m:
of one who worships mantras and the like, or for obtaining them;
whereas the rule against going to sacred fields and the like is likewise described

4.s:
vaiśvarūpyeṇa pūrṇatvaṃ jñātumityapi varṇitam /
samayācārasadbhāvaḥ pālyatvenopadiśyate // 261
4.d:
वैश्वरूप्येण पूर्णत्वं ज्ञातुमित्यपि वर्णितम् ।
समयाचारसद्भावः पाल्यत्वेनोपदिश्यते ॥ 261
4.m:
for the sake of knowing the fullness of one’s own self through universal form.
The presence of traditional conduct is taught as something to be observed

4.s:
bhedaprāṇatayā tattattyāgāttattvaviśuddhaye /
samayādiniṣedhastu mataśāstreṣu kathyate // 262
4.d:
भेदप्राणतया तत्तत्त्यागात्तत्त्वविशुद्धये ।
समयादिनिषेधस्तु मतशास्त्रेषु कथ्यते ॥ 262
4.m:
for the purification of reality through the renunciation of various entities whose life is difference;
whereas the prohibition of traditional observances and the like is taught in the Mata scriptures

4.s:
nirmaryādaṃ svasaṃbodhaṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ buddhyatāmiti /
parakīyamidaṃ rūpaṃ dhyeyametattu me nijam // 263
4.d:
निर्मर्यादं स्वसंबोधं संपूर्णं बुद्ध्यतामिति ।
परकीयमिदं रूपं ध्येयमेतत्तु मे निजम् ॥ 263
4.m:
so that one may realize: ‘Let self-awareness be known as boundless and complete.’
‘This is an external form, to be meditated upon, but this is my own;

4.s:
jvālādiliṅgaṃ cānyasya kapālādi tu me nijam /
ādiśabdāttapaścaryāvelātithyādi kathyate // 264
4.d:
ज्वालादिलिङ्गं चान्यस्य कपालादि तु मे निजम् ।
आदिशब्दात्तपश्चर्यावेलातिथ्यादि कथ्यते ॥ 264
4.m:
the fiery liṅga and the like belong to another, but the skull and the like are my own.’
By the word ‘and the like’, ascetic practices, times, lunar days, and so forth are meant.

4.s:
nāma śaktiśivādyantametasya mama nānyathā /
gotraṃ ca gurusaṃtāno maṭhikākulaśabditaḥ // 265
4.d:
नाम शक्तिशिवाद्यन्तमेतस्य मम नान्यथा ।
गोत्रं च गुरुसंतानो मठिकाकुलशब्दितः ॥ 265
4.m:
‘His name ends with Śakti, Śiva, and the like; mine is not otherwise.’
And the lineage and the guru’s transmission are termed the hermitage-kula;

4.s:
śrīsaṃtatistryambakākhyā tadardhāmardasaṃjñitā /
itthamardhacatasro'tra maṭhikāḥ śāṃkare krame // 266
4.d:
श्रीसंततिस्त्र्यम्बकाख्या तदर्धामर्दसंज्ञिता ।
इत्थमर्धचतस्रोऽत्र मठिकाः शांकरे क्रमे ॥ 266
4.m:
the venerable transmission is called Tryambaka, its half, and Āmarda;
thus here there are three and a half hermitages in the Śāṃkara tradition.

4.s:
yugakrameṇa kūrmādyā mīnāntā siddhasaṃtatiḥ /
ādiśabdena ca gharaṃ pallī pīṭhopapīṭhakam // 267
4.d:
युगक्रमेण कूर्माद्या मीनान्ता सिद्धसंततिः ।
आदिशब्देन च घरं पल्ली पीठोपपीठकम् ॥ 267
4.m:
According to the sequence of world-ages, there is the lineage of Siddhas beginning with Kūrma and ending with Mīna.
And by the word ‘and the like’, house, village, sacred seat, and secondary seat,

4.s:
mudrā chummeti teṣāṃ ca vidhānaṃ svaparasthitam /
tādātmyapratipattyai hi svaṃ saṃtānaṃ samāśrayet // 268
4.d:
मुद्रा छुम्मेति तेषां च विधानं स्वपरस्थितम् ।
तादात्म्यप्रतिपत्त्यै हि स्वं संतानं समाश्रयेत् ॥ 268
4.m:
mudrā, and secret recognition signs—the rule of these belonging to oneself or to another is laid down.
Indeed, for the sake of realizing identity, one should resort to one’s own lineage;

4.s:
bhuñjīta pūjayeccakraṃ parasaṃtāninā nahi /
etacca mataśāstreṣu niṣiddhaṃ khaṇḍanā yataḥ // 269
4.d:
भुञ्जीत पूजयेच्चक्रं परसंतानिना नहि ।
एतच्च मतशास्त्रेषु निषिद्धं खण्डना यतः ॥ 269
4.m:
one should not eat or worship the circle with one belonging to another lineage.
And this is forbidden in the Mata scriptures, because fragmentation

4.s:
akhaṇḍe'pi pare tattve bhedenānena jāyate /
evaṃ kṣetrapraveśādi saṃtānaniyamāntataḥ // 270
4.d:
अखण्डेऽपि परे तत्त्वे भेदेनानेन जायते ।
एवं क्षेत्रप्रवेशादि संताननियमान्ततः ॥ 270
4.m:
arises through this differentiation, even in the unfragmented supreme reality.
Thus, beginning with entry into sacred fields and ending with lineage rules,

4.s:
nāsminvidhīyate taddhi sākṣānnaupayikaṃ śive /
na tasya ca niṣodho ya nna tattattvasya khaṇḍanam // 271
4.d:
नास्मिन्विधीयते तद्धि साक्षान्नौपयिकं शिवे ।
न तस्य च निषोधो य न्न तत्तत्त्वस्य खण्डनम् ॥ 271
4.m:
nothing is enjoined in this [tradition], for that is not directly conducive to Śiva;
nor is there a prohibition against it, which would fragment that reality.

4.s:
viśvātmano hi nāthasya svasminrūpe vikalpitau /
vidhirniṣedho vā śaktau na svarūpasya khaṇḍane // 272
4.d:
विश्वात्मनो हि नाथस्य स्वस्मिन्रूपे विकल्पितौ ।
विधिर्निषेधो वा शक्तौ न स्वरूपस्य खण्डने ॥ 272
4.m:
For an injunction or a prohibition, conceptually constructed within his own form
by the Lord who is universal, is not capable of fragmenting his intrinsic nature.

4.s:
paratattvapraveśe tu yameva nikaṭaṃ yadā /
upāyaṃ vetti sa grāhyastadā tyājyo'tha vā kvacit // 273
4.d:
परतत्त्वप्रवेशे तु यमेव निकटं यदा ।
उपायं वेत्ति स ग्राह्यस्तदा त्याज्योऽथ वा क्वचित् ॥ 273
4.m:
Upon entering the supreme reality, whichever means one knows as close at that time
is to be grasped then, or in some cases to be abandoned.

4.s:
na yantraṇātra kāryeti proktaṃ śrītrikaśāsane /
samatā sarvadevānāmovallīmantravarṇayoḥ // 274
4.d:
न यन्त्रणात्र कार्येति प्रोक्तं श्रीत्रिकशासने ।
समता सर्वदेवानामोवल्लीमन्त्रवर्णयोः ॥ 274
4.m:
‘No constraint should be practiced here,’ so it is taught in the venerable Trika teaching;
there is equality of all deities, ovallīs, mantras, and syllables,

4.s:
āgamanāṃ gatīnāṃ ca sarvaṃ śivamayaṃ yataḥ /
sa hyakhaṇḍitasadbhāvaṃ śivatattvaṃ prapaśyati // 275
4.d:
आगमनां गतीनां च सर्वं शिवमयं यतः ।
स ह्यखण्डितसद्भावं शिवतत्त्वं प्रपश्यति ॥ 275
4.m:
of āgamas and paths, because everything is composed of Śiva.
For he perceives the Śiva-reality whose true being is unfragmented,

4.s:
yo hyakhaṇḍitasadbhāvamātmatattvaṃ prapadyate /
ketakīkusumasaurabhe bhṛśaṃ bhṛṅga eva rasiko na makṣikā /
bhairavīyaparamādvayārcane ko'pi rajyati maheśacoditaḥ // 276
4.d:
यो ह्यखण्डितसद्भावमात्मतत्त्वं प्रपद्यते ।
केतकीकुसुमसौरभे भृशं भृङ्ग एव रसिको न मक्षिका ।
भैरवीयपरमाद्वयार्चने कोऽपि रज्यति महेशचोदितः ॥ 276
4.m:
who realizes the self-reality whose true being is unfragmented.
Only the bee is truly passionate for the fragrance of the ketakī blossom, not the fly; / impelled by the Great Lord, some rare person delights in the worship of the supreme non-duality of Bhairava.

4.s:
asmiṃśca yoge viśrāntiṃ kurvatāṃ bhavaḍambaraḥ /
himānīva mahāgrīṣme svayameva vilīyate // 277
4.d:
अस्मिंश्च योगे विश्रान्तिं कुर्वतां भवडम्बरः ।
हिमानीव महाग्रीष्मे स्वयमेव विलीयते ॥ 277
4.m: And for those who rest in this yoga, the pomp of worldly existence / dissolves spontaneously, like a mass of snow in the height of summer.

4.s:
alaṃ vātiprasaṅgena bhūyasātiprapañcite /
yogyo'bhinavagupto'sminko'pi yāgavidhau budhaḥ // 278
4.d:
अलं वातिप्रसङ्गेन भूयसातिप्रपञ्चिते ।
योग्योऽभिनवगुप्तोऽस्मिन्कोऽपि यागविधौ बुधः ॥ 278
4.m: Enough with excessive expansion on what has already been vastly elaborated! / Some wise person here, Abhinavagupta, is fit for this sacrificial rite.

4.s: ityanuttarapadapravikāse śāktamaupayikamadya viviktam // 279
4.d: इत्यनुत्तरपदप्रविकासे शाक्तमौपयिकमद्य विविक्तम् ॥ 279
4.m: Thus, regarding the unfolding of the unexcelled abode, the Śākta means has now been distinguished.

5.s: āṇavena vidhinā paradhāma prepsatāmatha nirūpyata etat // 1
5.d: आणवेन विधिना परधाम प्रेप्सतामथ निरूप्यत एतत् ॥ 1
5.m: Now, for those who desire to attain the supreme abode by the Āṇava method, this is explained:

5.s:
vikalpasyaiva saṃskāre jāte niṣpratiyogini /
abhīṣṭe vastuni prāptirniścitā bhogamokṣayoḥ // 2
5.d:
विकल्पस्यैव संस्कारे जाते निष्प्रतियोगिनि ।
अभीष्टे वस्तुनि प्राप्तिर्निश्चिता भोगमोक्षयोः ॥ 2
5.m: Once the conceptual construct alone has been purified so as to be free of any counter-entity, / the attainment of enjoyment and liberation in the desired reality is assured.

5.s:
vikalpaḥ kasyacitsvātmasvātantryādeva susthiraḥ /
upāyāntarasāpekṣyaviyogenaiva jāyate // 3
5.d:
विकल्पः कस्यचित्स्वात्मस्वातन्त्र्यादेव सुस्थिरः ।
उपायान्तरसापेक्ष्यवियोगेनैव जायते ॥ 3
5.m: For someone, the conceptual construct becomes firmly stabilized solely through the absolute autonomy of one's own Self, / arising entirely without dependence on any other means.

5.s:
kasyacittu vikalpo'sau svātmasaṃskaraṇaṃ prati /
upāyāntarasāpekṣastatroktaḥ pūrvako vidhiḥ // 4
5.d:
कस्यचित्तु विकल्पोऽसौ स्वात्मसंस्करणं प्रति ।
उपायान्तरसापेक्षस्तत्रोक्तः पूर्वको विधिः ॥ 4
5.m: For another, however, this conceptual construct depends on other means / for its own purification; with respect to that, the previous method was spoken.

5.s:
vikalpo nāma cinmātrasvabhāvo yadyapi sthitaḥ /
tathāpi niścayātmāsāvaṇoḥ svātantryayojakaḥ // 5
5.d:
विकल्पो नाम चिन्मात्रस्वभावो यद्यपि स्थितः ।
तथापि निश्चयात्मासावणोः स्वातन्त्र्ययोजकः ॥ 5
5.m: Even though a conceptual construct by nature consists of pure consciousness alone, / nevertheless, being determinative, it unites the bound soul with absolute autonomy.

5.s:
niścayo bahudhā caiṣa tatropāyāśca bhedinaḥ /
aṇuśabdena te coktā dūrāntikavibhedataḥ // 6
5.d:
निश्चयो बहुधा चैष तत्रोपायाश्च भेदिनः ।
अणुशब्देन ते चोक्ता दूरान्तिकविभेदतः ॥ 6
5.m: And this determination is manifold, and the means therein are diversified; / and they are designated by the word 'aṇu' because of distinctions of distance and proximity.

5.s:
tatra buddhau tathā prāṇe dehe cāpi pramātari /
apāramārthike'pyasmin paramārthaḥ prakāśate // 7
5.d:
तत्र बुद्धौ तथा प्राणे देहे चापि प्रमातरि ।
अपारमार्थिकेऽप्यस्मिन् परमार्थः प्रकाशते ॥ 7
5.m: There, in the intellect as well as in the vital breath, and also in the body, the knower, / though non-ultimate, the ultimate reality shines forth.

5.s:
yataḥ prakāśāccinmātrāt prāṇādyavyatirekavat /
tasyaiva tu svatantratvāddviguṇaṃ jaḍacidvapuḥ // 8
5.d:
यतः प्रकाशाच्चिन्मात्रात् प्राणाद्यव्यतिरेकवत् ।
तस्यैव तु स्वतन्त्रत्वाद्द्विगुणं जडचिद्वपुः ॥ 8
5.m: Because, from the luminosity of pure consciousness, the vital breath and so forth are not distinct; / yet owing to its very autonomy, it has a twofold form: insentient and sentient.

5.s:
uktaṃ traiśirase caitaddevyai candrārdhamaulinā /
jīvaḥ śaktiḥ śivasyaiva sarvatraiva sthitāpi sā // 9
5.d:
उक्तं त्रैशिरसे चैतद्देव्यै चन्द्रार्धमौलिना ।
जीवः शक्तिः शिवस्यैव सर्वत्रैव स्थितापि सा ॥ 9
5.m: And this was spoken to the Goddess by the moon-crested Lord in the Traiśirasa: / 'The individual soul is the power of Śiva alone; yet though it is omnipresent,

5.s:
svarūpapratyaye rūḍhā jñānasyonmīlanātparā /
tasya cidrūpatāṃ satyāṃ svātantryollāsakalpanāt // 10
5.d:
स्वरूपप्रत्यये रूढा ज्ञानस्योन्मीलनात्परा ।
तस्य चिद्रूपतां सत्यां स्वातन्त्र्योल्लासकल्पनात् ॥ 10
5.m: rooted in the awareness of its essential nature, it is supreme due to the unfolding of knowledge.' / Perceiving its nature of consciousness as real through the imaginative display of absolute autonomy,

5.s:
paśyañjaḍātmatābhāgaṃ tirodhāyādvayo bhavet /
tatra svātantryadṛṣṭyā vā darpaṇe mukhabimbavat // 11
5.d:
पश्यञ्जडात्मताभागं तिरोधायाद्वयो भवेत् ।
तत्र स्वातन्त्र्यदृष्ट्या वा दर्पणे मुखबिम्बवत् ॥ 11
5.m: and setting aside the insentient aspect, one becomes non-dual. / Or, through the vision of absolute autonomy therein, like a reflection of a face in a mirror,

5.s:
viśuddhaṃ nijacaitanyaṃ niścinotyatadātmakam /
buddhiprāṇādito bhinnaṃ caitanyaṃ niścitaṃ balāt // 12
5.d:
विशुद्धं निजचैतन्यं निश्चिनोत्यतदात्मकम् ।
बुद्धिप्राणादितो भिन्नं चैतन्यं निश्चितं बलात् ॥ 12
5.m: one ascertains one's pure consciousness to be not of that [insentient] nature. / Once consciousness is firmly ascertained as distinct from the intellect, vital breath, and so forth,

5.s:
satyatastadabhinnaṃ syāttasyānyonyavibhedataḥ /
viśvarūpāvibheditvaṃ śuddhatvādeva jāyate // 13
5.d:
सत्यतस्तदभिन्नं स्यात्तस्यान्योन्यविभेदतः ।
विश्वरूपाविभेदित्वं शुद्धत्वादेव जायते ॥ 13
5.m: in reality it is non-distinct from them, since they are distinct from one another; / its non-distinctness from the universal form arises solely from its purity.

5.s:
niṣṭhitaikasphuranmūrtermūrtyantaravirodhataḥ /
antaḥ saṃvidi satsarvaṃ yadyapyaparathā dhiyi // 14
5.d:
निष्ठितैकस्फुरन्मूर्तेर्मूर्त्यन्तरविरोधतः ।
अन्तः संविदि सत्सर्वं यद्यप्यपरथा धियि ॥ 14
5.m: Because a single established, flashing form excludes any other form, / everything exists internally in consciousness; otherwise, how could it pass over into the intellect,

5.s:
prāṇe dehe'thavā kasmātsaṃkrāmetkena vā katham /
tathāpi nirvikalpe'sminvikalpo nāsti taṃ vinā // 15
5.d:
प्राणे देहेऽथवा कस्मात्संक्रामेत्केन वा कथम् ।
तथापि निर्विकल्पेऽस्मिन्विकल्पो नास्ति तं विना ॥ 15
5.m: or into the vital breath, or into the body? By what means or how? / Nevertheless, within this non-conceptual [awareness], there is no conceptual construct without it.

5.s:
dṛṣṭe'pyadṛṣṭakalpatvaṃ vikalpena tu niścayaḥ /
buddhiprāṇaśarīreṣu pārameśvaryamañjasā // 16
5.d:
दृष्टेऽप्यदृष्टकल्पत्वं विकल्पेन तु निश्चयः ।
बुद्धिप्राणशरीरेषु पारमेश्वर्यमञ्जसा ॥ 16
5.m: Even when seen, it is as if unseen; but through a conceptual construct, determination occurs. / Sovereign divinity is readily to be conceptualized

5.s:
vikalpyaṃ śūnyarūpe na pramātari vikalpanam /
buddhirdhyānamayī tatra prāṇa uccāraṇātmakaḥ // 17
5.d:
विकल्प्यं शून्यरूपे न प्रमातरि विकल्पनम् ।
बुद्धिर्ध्यानमयी तत्र प्राण उच्चारणात्मकः ॥ 17
5.m: in the intellect, vital breath, and body; conceptualization cannot occur in the void-like knower. / There, the intellect consists of meditation; the vital breath consists of sounding forth.

5.s:
uccāraṇaṃ ca prāṇādyā vyānāntāḥ pañca vṛttayaḥ /
ādyā tu prāṇanābhikhyāparoccārātmikā bhavet // 18
5.d:
उच्चारणं च प्राणाद्या व्यानान्ताः पञ्च वृत्तयः ।
आद्या तु प्राणनाभिख्यापरोच्चारात्मिका भवेत् ॥ 18
5.m: And sounding forth consists of the five functions, beginning with prāṇa and ending with vyāna; / the first, however, called prāṇana, consists of the supreme sounding forth.

5.s:
śarīrasyākṣaviṣayaitatpiṇḍatvena saṃsthitiḥ /
tatra dhyānamayaṃ tāvadanuttaramihocyate // 19
5.d:
शरीरस्याक्षविषयैतत्पिण्डत्वेन संस्थितिः ।
तत्र ध्यानमयं तावदनुत्तरमिहोच्यते ॥ 19
5.m: The body's state consists in being an aggregate of these sense objects. / There, that which consists of meditation is spoken of here first as unexcelled.

5.s:
yaḥ prakāśaḥ svatantro'yaṃ citsvabhāvo hṛdi sthitaḥ /
sarvatattvamayaḥ proktametacca triśiromate // 20
5.d:
यः प्रकाशः स्वतन्त्रोऽयं चित्स्वभावो हृदि स्थितः ।
सर्वतत्त्वमयः प्रोक्तमेतच्च त्रिशिरोमते ॥ 20
5.m: This autonomous luminosity, whose nature is consciousness, seated in the heart, / is declared to consist of all principles of reality; and this is stated in the Triśiromata:

5.s:
kadalīsaṃpuṭākāraṃ sabāhyābhyantarāntaram /
īkṣate hṛdayāntaḥsthaṃ tatpuṣpamiva tattvavit // 21
5.d:
कदलीसंपुटाकारं सबाह्याभ्यन्तरान्तरम् ।
ईक्षते हृदयान्तःस्थं तत्पुष्पमिव तत्त्ववित् ॥ 21
5.m: The knower of reality sees that which abides within the heart / like that banana flower, shaped like a plantain calyx, with exterior and interior compartments.

5.s:
somasūryāgnisaṃghaṭṭaṃ tatra dhyāyedananyadhīḥ /
taddhyānāraṇisaṃkṣobhānmahābhairavahavyabhuk // 22
5.d:
सोमसूर्याग्निसंघट्टं तत्र ध्यायेदनन्यधीः ।
तद्ध्यानारणिसंक्षोभान्महाभैरवहव्यभुक् ॥ 22
5.m: With undistracted mind, one should meditate there on the conjunction of the moon, sun, and fire. / From the agitation of the firesticks of that meditation, the consumer of oblations, Great Bhairava,

5.s:
hṛdayākhye mahākuṇḍe jājvalan sphītatāṃ vrajet /
tasya śaktimataḥ sphītaśakterbhairavatejasaḥ // 23
5.d:
हृदयाख्ये महाकुण्डे जाज्वलन् स्फीततां व्रजेत् ।
तस्य शक्तिमतः स्फीतशक्तेर्भैरवतेजसः ॥ 23
5.m: blazing in the great sacrificial pit known as the heart, expands. / One should contemplate the abode known as the knower, means of knowledge, and object of knowledge

5.s:
mātṛmānaprameyākhyaṃ dhāmābhedena bhāvayet /
vahnyarkasomaśaktīnāṃ tadeva tritayaṃ bhavet // 24
5.d:
मातृमानप्रमेयाख्यं धामाभेदेन भावयेत् ।
वह्न्यर्कसोमशक्तीनां तदेव त्रितयं भवेत् ॥ 24
5.m: in non-differentiation from that fire of Bhairava, the possessor of power whose power is expanded; / that itself becomes the triad of the powers of fire, sun, and moon.

5.s:
parā parāparā ceyamaparā ca sadoditā /
sṛṣṭisaṃsthitisaṃhāraistāsāṃ pratyekatastridhā // 25
5.d:
परा परापरा चेयमपरा च सदोदिता ।
सृष्टिसंस्थितिसंहारैस्तासां प्रत्येकतस्त्रिधा ॥ 25
5.m: And these, Parā, Parāparā, and Aparā, are ever arisen; / each of them is threefold through emission, maintenance, and reabsorption,

5.s:
caturthaṃ cānavacchinnaṃ rūpamāsāmakalpitam /
evaṃ dvādaśa tā devyaḥ sūryabimbavadāsthitāḥ // 26
5.d:
चतुर्थं चानवच्छिन्नं रूपमासामकल्पितम् ।
एवं द्वादश ता देव्यः सूर्यबिम्बवदास्थिताः ॥ 26
5.m: and their fourth form is undivided and unconstructed. / Thus, those twelve goddesses abide like the disc of the sun.

5.s:
ekaikamāsāṃ vahnyarkasomatacchāntibhāsanam /
etadānuttaraṃ cakraṃ hṛdayāccakṣurādibhiḥ // 27
5.d:
एकैकमासां वह्न्यर्कसोमतच्छान्तिभासनम् ।
एतदानुत्तरं चक्रं हृदयाच्चक्षुरादिभिः ॥ 27
5.m: Each one of them is the illumination of fire, sun, moon, and their peace. / This unexcelled wheel issues forth from the heart through the eyes and other

5.s:
vyomabhirniḥsaratyeva tattadviṣayagocare /
taccakrabhābhistatrārthe sṛṣṭisthitilayakramāt // 28
5.d:
व्योमभिर्निःसरत्येव तत्तद्विषयगोचरे ।
तच्चक्रभाभिस्तत्रार्थे सृष्टिस्थितिलयक्रमात् ॥ 28
5.m: openings into the range of their respective objects. / By the radiances of that wheel, upon that object, through the sequence of emission, maintenance, and dissolution,

5.s:
somasūryāgnibhāsātma rūpaṃ samavatiṣṭhate /
evaṃ śabdādiviṣaye śrotrādivyomavartmanā // 29
5.d:
सोमसूर्याग्निभासात्म रूपं समवतिष्ठते ।
एवं शब्दादिविषये श्रोत्रादिव्योमवर्त्मना ॥ 29
5.m: its form, consisting of the light of the moon, sun, and fire, becomes established. / In this way, upon the objects such as sound, through the path of the void of the ear and other senses,

5.s:
cakreṇānena patatā tādātmyaṃ paribhāvayet /
anena kramayogena yatra yatra patatyadaḥ // 30
5.d:
चक्रेणानेन पतता तादात्म्यं परिभावयेत् ।
अनेन क्रमयोगेन यत्र यत्र पतत्यदः ॥ 30
5.m: one should contemplate identity with this wheel as it descends. / By this sequential practice, wherever this

5.s:
cakraṃ sarvātmakaṃ tattatsārvabhaumamahīśavat /
itthaṃ viśvādhvapaṭalamayatnenaiva līyate // 31
5.d:
चक्रं सर्वात्मकं तत्तत्सार्वभौममहीशवत् ।
इत्थं विश्वाध्वपटलमयत्नेनैव लीयते ॥ 31
5.m: all-encompassing wheel descends, like a sovereign universal monarch, / thus the veil of the entire path dissolves without any effort

5.s:
bhairavīyamahācakre saṃvittiparivārite /
tataḥ saṃskāramātreṇa viśvasyāpi parikṣaye // 32
5.d:
भैरवीयमहाचक्रे संवित्तिपरिवारिते ।
ततः संस्कारमात्रेण विश्वस्यापि परिक्षये ॥ 32
5.m: in the great wheel of Bhairava surrounded by the retinue of consciousness. / Then, when even the universe has dissolved through mere latent impression,

5.s:
svātmocchalattayā bhrāmyaccakraṃ saṃcintayenmahat /
tatastaddāhyavilayāt tatsaṃskāraparikṣayāt // 33
5.d:
स्वात्मोच्छलत्तया भ्राम्यच्चक्रं संचिन्तयेन्महत् ।
ततस्तद्दाह्यविलयात् तत्संस्कारपरिक्षयात् ॥ 33
5.m: one should contemplate the great wheel whirling through the surge of one's own Self. / Then, through the dissolution of that fuel, through the vanishing of those latent impressions,

5.s:
praśāmyadbhāvayeccakraṃ tataḥ śāntaṃ tataḥ śamam /
anena dhyānayogena viśvaṃ cakre vilīyate // 34
5.d:
प्रशाम्यद्भावयेच्चक्रं ततः शान्तं ततः शमम् ।
अनेन ध्यानयोगेन विश्वं चक्रे विलीयते ॥ 34
5.m: one should contemplate the wheel as coming to rest, then peaceful, and then as peace itself. / Through this discipline of meditation, the universe dissolves into the wheel,

5.s:
tatsaṃvidi tataḥ saṃvidvilīnārthaiva bhāsate /
citsvābhāvyāt tato bhūyaḥ sṛṣṭiryaccinmaheśvarī // 35
5.d:
तत्संविदि ततः संविद्विलीनार्थैव भासते ।
चित्स्वाभाव्यात् ततो भूयः सृष्टिर्यच्चिन्महेश्वरी ॥ 35
5.m: that dissolves into consciousness, and then consciousness shines forth with its objects dissolved; / and from the nature of consciousness, there is emission once again, since consciousness is the Great Goddess.

5.s:
evaṃ pratikṣaṇaṃ viśvaṃ svasaṃvidi vilāpayan /
visṛjaṃśca tato bhūyaḥ śaśvadbhairavatāṃ vrajet // 36
5.d:
एवं प्रतिक्षणं विश्वं स्वसंविदि विलापयन् ।
विसृजंश्च ततो भूयः शश्वद्भैरवतां व्रजेत् ॥ 36
5.m: Dissolving the universe into one's own consciousness every moment in this manner, / and emitting it again from that, one permanently attains the state of Bhairava.

5.s:
evaṃ triśūlāt prabhṛti catuṣpañcārakakramāt /
pañcāśadaraparyantaṃ cakraṃ yogī vibhāvayet // 37
5.d:
एवं त्रिशूलात् प्रभृति चतुष्पञ्चारकक्रमात् ।
पञ्चाशदरपर्यन्तं चक्रं योगी विभावयेत् ॥ 37
5.m: In this way, the yogin should contemplate the wheel starting from the trident, / in the progression of four and five spokes, up to fifty spokes,

5.s:
catuṣṣaṣṭiśatāraṃ vā sahasrāramathāpi vā /
asaṃkhyārasahasraṃ vā cakraṃ dhyāyedananyadhīḥ // 38
5.d:
चतुष्षष्टिशतारं वा सहस्रारमथापि वा ।
असंख्यारसहस्रं वा चक्रं ध्यायेदनन्यधीः ॥ 38
5.m: or with sixty-four or a hundred spokes, or even a thousand spokes; / or with an undistracted mind, one should meditate on the wheel of countless thousands of spokes.

5.s:
saṃvinnāthasya mahato devasyollāsisaṃvidaḥ /
naivāsti kācitkalanā viśvaśaktermaheśituḥ // 39
5.d:
संविन्नाथस्य महतो देवस्योल्लासिसंविदः ।
नैवास्ति काचित्कलना विश्वशक्तेर्महेशितुः ॥ 39
5.m: For the Lord of consciousness, the great god whose consciousness is surging forth, / the supreme ruler who possesses the universal power, there is no limitation whatsoever.

5.s:
śaktayo'sya jagat kṛtsnaṃ śaktimāṃstu maheśvaraḥ /
iti māṅgalaśāstre tu śrīśrīkaṇṭho nyarūpayat // 40
5.d:
शक्तयोऽस्य जगत् कृत्स्नं शक्तिमांस्तु महेश्वरः ।
इति माङ्गलशास्त्रे तु श्रीश्रीकण्ठो न्यरूपयत् ॥ 40
5.m: The entire universe is his powers, but the Great Lord is the possessor of power: / so the venerable Śrīkaṇṭha explained in the auspicious scripture.

5.s:
ityetat prathamopāyarūpaṃ dhyānaṃ nyarūpayat /
śrīśaṃbhunātho me tuṣṭastasmai śrīsumatiprabhuḥ // 41
5.d:
इत्येतत् प्रथमोपायरूपं ध्यानं न्यरूपयत् ।
श्रीशंभुनाथो मे तुष्टस्तस्मै श्रीसुमतिप्रभुः ॥ 41
5.m: Thus, the meditation that constitutes this first means was explained to me / by the revered Śambhunātha, well pleased, and to him by the venerable master Sumati.

5.s:
anayaiva diśānyāni dhyānānyapi samāśrayet /
anuttaropāyadhurāṃ yānyāyānti kramaṃ vinā // 42
5.d:
अनयैव दिशान्यानि ध्यानान्यपि समाश्रयेत् ।
अनुत्तरोपायधुरां यान्यायान्ति क्रमं विना ॥ 42
5.m: In this very manner, one should also take recourse to other meditations / that lead without gradual sequence to the summit of the unexcelled means.

5.s:
atha prāṇasya yā vṛttiḥ prāṇanādyā nirūpitā /
tadupāyatayā brūmo'nuttarapravikāsanam // 43
5.d:
अथ प्राणस्य या वृत्तिः प्राणनाद्या निरूपिता ।
तदुपायतया ब्रूमोऽनुत्तरप्रविकासनम् ॥ 43
5.m: Now, as for the function of the vital breath described as prāṇana and so forth, / we explain the unfolding of the unexcelled using that as a means.

5.s:
nijānande pramātraṃśamātre hṛdi purā sthitaḥ /
śūnyatāmātraviśrānternirānandaṃ vibhāvayet // 44
5.d:
निजानन्दे प्रमात्रंशमात्रे हृदि पुरा स्थितः ।
शून्यतामात्रविश्रान्तेर्निरानन्दं विभावयेत् ॥ 44
5.m: Having first rested in the heart, in one's own bliss, in the mere portion of the knower, / one should contemplate the absence of bliss due to resting in the void alone.

5.s:
prāṇodaye prameye tu parānandaṃ vibhāvayet /
tatrānantaprameyāṃśapūraṇāpānanirvṛtaḥ // 45
5.d:
प्राणोदये प्रमेये तु परानन्दं विभावयेत् ।
तत्रानन्तप्रमेयांशपूरणापाननिर्वृतः ॥ 45
5.m: When prāṇa arises, however, one should contemplate the supreme bliss (parānanda) in the object of knowledge; / there, filled with the boundless portions of knowables, he is delighted by apāna. // 45

5.s:
parānandagatastiṣṭhedapānaśaśiśobhitaḥ /
tato'nantasphuranmeyasaṃghaṭṭaikāntanirvṛtaḥ // 46
5.d:
परानन्दगतस्तिष्ठेदपानशशिशोभितः ।
ततोऽनन्तस्फुरन्मेयसंघट्टैकान्तनिर्वृतः ॥ 46
5.m: Having attained parānanda, he should abide adorned by the moon of apāna; / then, entirely satisfied by the collision with the infinitely vibrant knowables, // 46

5.s:
samānabhūmimāgatya brahmānandamayo bhavet /
tato'pi mānameyaughakalanāgrāsatatparaḥ // 47
5.d:
समानभूमिमागत्य ब्रह्मानन्दमयो भवेत् ।
ततोऽपि मानमेयौघकलनाग्रासतत्परः ॥ 47
5.m: and having reached the level of samāna, he becomes full of the bliss of Brahman (brahmānanda). / Then, intent upon devouring the surging movement of means of knowledge and knowables, // 47

5.s:
udānavahnau viśrānto mahānandaṃ vibhāvayat /
tatra viśrāntimabhyetya śāmyatyasminmahārciṣi // 48
5.d:
उदानवह्नौ विश्रान्तो महानन्दं विभावयत् ।
तत्र विश्रान्तिमभ्येत्य शाम्यत्यस्मिन्महार्चिषि ॥ 48
5.m: resting in the fire of udāna, he should contemplate the great bliss (mahānanda). / Having attained repose there, he is pacified in this great flame; // 48

5.s:
nirupādhirmahāvyāptirvyānākhyopādhivarjitā /
tadā khalu cidānando yo jaḍānupabṛṃhitaḥ // 49
5.d:
निरुपाधिर्महाव्याप्तिर्व्यानाख्योपाधिवर्जिता ।
तदा खलु चिदानन्दो यो जडानुपबृंहितः ॥ 49
5.m: the great pervasion, devoid of limiting adjuncts, is stripped of the conditioning called vyāna. / Then indeed occurs the bliss of consciousness (cidānanda), which is not reinforced by insentient matter; // 49

5.s:
nahyatra saṃsthitiḥ kāpi vibhaktā jaḍarūpiṇaḥ /
yatra ko'pi vyavacchedo nāsti yadviśvataḥ sphurat // 50
5.d:
नह्यत्र संस्थितिः कापि विभक्ता जडरूपिणः ।
यत्र कोऽपि व्यवच्छेदो नास्ति यद्विश्वतः स्फुरत् ॥ 50
5.m: for here there is no separate existence whatsoever of an insentient nature, / wherein there is no demarcation at all, and which pulses everywhere, // 50

5.s:
yadanāhatasaṃvitti paramāmṛtabṛṃhitam /
yatrāsti bhāvanādīnāṃ na mukhyā kāpi saṃgatiḥ // 51
5.d:
यदनाहतसंवित्ति परमामृतबृंहितम् ।
यत्रास्ति भावनादीनां न मुख्या कापि संगतिः ॥ 51
5.m: which is uninhibited consciousness, swollen with supreme nectar, / wherein contemplation and the like have no primary relevance at all. // 51

5.s:
tadeva jagadānandamasmabhyaṃ śaṃbhurūcivān /
tatra viśrāntirādheyā hṛdayoccārayogataḥ // 52
5.d:
तदेव जगदानन्दमस्मभ्यं शंभुरूचिवान् ।
तत्र विश्रान्तिराधेया हृदयोच्चारयोगतः ॥ 52
5.m: That very state Śambhu declared to us as the universal bliss (jagadānanda); / repose is to be established therein by means of the sounding of the heart (hṛdayoccāra). // 52

5.s:
yā tatra samyagviśrāntiḥ sānuttaramayī sthitiḥ /
ityetaddhṛdayādyekasvabhāve'pi svadhāmani // 53
5.d:
या तत्र सम्यग्विश्रान्तिः सानुत्तरमयी स्थितिः ।
इत्येतद्धृदयाद्येकस्वभावेऽपि स्वधामनि ॥ 53
5.m: Complete repose therein is the state consisting of the unexcelled. / Thus, although one's own abode possesses a single nature, beginning with the heart, // 53

5.s:
ṣaṭprāṇoccārajaṃ rūpamatha vyāptyā taducyate /
prāṇadaṇḍaprayogena pūrvāparasamīkṛteḥ // 54
5.d:
षट्प्राणोच्चारजं रूपमथ व्याप्त्या तदुच्यते ।
प्राणदण्डप्रयोगेन पूर्वापरसमीकृतेः ॥ 54
5.m: its form arising from the sounding of the six vital breaths is now spoken of according to its pervasion. / By employing the staff-like movement of the breath (prāṇadaṇḍa), through harmonizing the prior and subsequent, // 54

5.s:
catuṣkikāmbujālambilambikāsaudhamāśrayet /
triśūlabhūmiṃ krāntvāto nāḍitritayasaṅgatām // 55
5.d:
चतुष्किकाम्बुजालम्बिलम्बिकासौधमाश्रयेत् ।
त्रिशूलभूमिं क्रान्त्वातो नाडित्रितयसङ्गताम् ॥ 55
5.m: one should take refuge in the palace of the uvula that hangs over the lotus of the four-pillared hall. / Then, having crossed the level of the trident connected to the triad of channels, // 55

5.s:
icchājñānakriyāśaktisamatve praviśet sudhīḥ /
ekāṃ vikāsinīṃ bhūyastvasaṃkocāṃ vikasvarām // 56
5.d:
इच्छाज्ञानक्रियाशक्तिसमत्वे प्रविशेत् सुधीः ।
एकां विकासिनीं भूयस्त्वसंकोचां विकस्वराम् ॥ 56
5.m: in the equality of the powers of will, knowledge, and action, the wise person should enter. / One, expanding, further uncontracted and blossoming, // 56

5.s:
śrayedbhrūbindunādāntaśaktisopānamālikām /
tatrordhvakuṇḍalībhūmau spandanodarasundaraḥ // 57
5.d:
श्रयेद्भ्रूबिन्दुनादान्तशक्तिसोपानमालिकाम् ।
तत्रोर्ध्वकुण्डलीभूमौ स्पन्दनोदरसुन्दरः ॥ 57
5.m: he should resort to the staircase consisting of eyebrow-center, bindu, nāda, nādānta, and śakti. / There, on the level of the upper kuṇḍalinī, lovely with the interior of vibration, // 57

5.s:
visargastatra viśrāmyenmatsyodaradaśājuṣi /
rāsabhī vaḍavā yadvatsvadhāmānandamandiram // 58
5.d:
विसर्गस्तत्र विश्राम्येन्मत्स्योदरदशाजुषि ।
रासभी वडवा यद्वत्स्वधामानन्दमन्दिरम् ॥ 58
5.m: creative emission should repose in that place enjoying the condition of the fish's belly; / just as a she-ass or a mare, entering into the mansion of bliss that is her own abode, // 58

5.s:
vikāsasaṃkocamayaṃ praviśya hṛdi hṛṣyati /
tadvanmuhurlīnasṛṣṭabhāvavrātasunirbharām // 59
5.d:
विकाससंकोचमयं प्रविश्य हृदि हृष्यति ।
तद्वन्मुहुर्लीनसृष्टभावव्रातसुनिर्भराम् ॥ 59
5.m: consisting of expansion and contraction, rejoices in her heart, / so should he resort to the dyad of Bhairava rooted in expansion and contraction, // 59

5.s:
śrayedvikāsasaṃkocarūḍhabhairavayāmalām /
ekīkṛtamahāmūlaśūlavaisargike hṛdi // 60
5.d:
श्रयेद्विकाससंकोचरूढभैरवयामलाम् ।
एकीकृतमहामूलशूलवैसर्गिके हृदि ॥ 60
5.m: utterly brimming with the host of entities repeatedly dissolved and emitted / in the emissive heart, wherein the great root trident has been unified. // 60

5.s:
parasminneti viśrāntiṃ sarvāpūraṇayogataḥ /
atra tatpūrṇavṛttyaiva viśvāveśamayaṃ sthitam // 61
5.d:
परस्मिन्नेति विश्रान्तिं सर्वापूरणयोगतः ।
अत्र तत्पूर्णवृत्त्यैव विश्वावेशमयं स्थितम् ॥ 61
5.m: He reaches repose in the supreme through filling all things; / here, through its very full activity, it abides consisting of the absorption of the universe. // 61

5.s:
prakāśasyātmaviśrāntāvahamityeva dṛśyatām /
anuttaravimarśe prāgvyāpārādivivarjite // 62
5.d:
प्रकाशस्यात्मविश्रान्तावहमित्येव दृश्यताम् ।
अनुत्तरविमर्शे प्राग्व्यापारादिविवर्जिते ॥ 62
5.m: In the self-repose of luminosity, let it be seen as 'I'; / in the unexcelled reflective awareness, devoid of prior activity and the rest, // 62

5.s:
cidvimarśaparāhaṃkṛt prathamollāsinī sphuret /
tata udyogasaktena sa dvādaśakalātmanā // 63
5.d:
चिद्विमर्शपराहंकृत् प्रथमोल्लासिनी स्फुरेत् ।
तत उद्योगसक्तेन स द्वादशकलात्मना ॥ 63
5.m: the supreme 'I'-awareness of reflective consciousness, sparkling at the very beginning, shines forth. / Then, through the sun composed of twelve digits, intent upon exertion, // 63

5.s:
sūryeṇābhāsayedbhāvaṃ pūrayedatha carcayet /
athenduḥ ṣoḍaśakalo visargagrāsamantharaḥ // 64
5.d:
सूर्येणाभासयेद्भावं पूरयेदथ चर्चयेत् ।
अथेन्दुः षोडशकलो विसर्गग्रासमन्थरः ॥ 64
5.m: he illuminates reality, fills it, and then reflects upon it. / Then the sixteen-digit moon, slow in devouring creative emission, // 64

5.s:
saṃjīvanyamṛtaṃ bodhavahnau visṛjati sphuran /
icchājñānakriyāśaktisūkṣmarandhrasrugagragam // 65
5.d:
संजीवन्यमृतं बोधवह्नौ विसृजति स्फुरन् ।
इच्छाज्ञानक्रियाशक्तिसूक्ष्मरन्ध्रस्रुगग्रगम् ॥ 65
5.m: shining, emits the reviving nectar into the fire of consciousness, / reaching the tip of the ladle that is the subtle aperture of the powers of will, knowledge, and action. // 65

5.s:
tadevama[tada]mṛtaṃ divyaṃ saṃviddevīṣu tarpakam /
visargāmṛtametāvad bodhākhye hutabhojini // 66
5.d:
तदेवम[तद]मृतं दिव्यं संविद्देवीषु तर्पकम् ।
विसर्गामृतमेतावद् बोधाख्ये हुतभोजिनि ॥ 66
5.m: Thus this divine nectar, gratifying the goddesses of consciousness, / this entire nectar of creative emission, if emitted into the fire-consumer called consciousness, // 66

5.s:
visṛṣṭaṃ cedbhavetsarvaṃ hutaṃ ṣoḍhādhvamaṇḍalam /
yato'nuttaranāthasya visargaḥ kulanāyikā /
tatkṣobhaḥ kādihāntaṃ tatprasarastattvapaddhatiḥ // 67
5.d:
विसृष्टं चेद्भवेत्सर्वं हुतं षोढाध्वमण्डलम् ।
यतोऽनुत्तरनाथस्य विसर्गः कुलनायिका ।
तत्क्षोभः कादिहान्तं तत्प्रसरस्तत्त्वपद्धतिः ॥ 67
5.m: then everything, the wheel of the sixfold path, becomes offered as oblation. / For creative emission is the mistress of Kula belonging to the unexcelled Lord; / its agitation is from ka to ha; its procession is the course of the tattvas. // 67

5.s:
aṃa iti kuleśvaryā sahito hi kuleśitā /
paro visargaviśleṣastanmayaṃ viśvamucyate // 68
5.d:
अंअ इति कुलेश्वर्या सहितो हि कुलेशिता ।
परो विसर्गविश्लेषस्तन्मयं विश्वमुच्यते ॥ 68
5.m: For the master of Kula together with the mistress of Kula is 'aṃ' and 'aḥ'; / the higher separation of creative emission—of that nature the universe is said to be. // 68

5.s:
vitprāṇaguṇadehāntarbahirdravyamayīmimām /
arcayejjuhuyāddhyāyeditthaṃ saṃjīvanīṃ kalām // 69
5.d:
वित्प्राणगुणदेहान्तर्बहिर्द्रव्यमयीमिमाम् ।
अर्चयेज्जुहुयाद्ध्यायेदित्थं संजीवनीं कलाम् ॥ 69
5.m: One should worship, sacrifice with, and meditate upon this reviving digit / consisting of external and internal substance within consciousness, breath, qualities, and the body in this way. // 69

5.s:
ānandanāḍīyugalaspandanāvahitau sthitaḥ /
enāṃ visarganiḥṣyandasaudhabhūmiṃ prapadyate // 70
5.d:
आनन्दनाडीयुगलस्पन्दनावहितौ स्थितः ।
एनां विसर्गनिःष्यन्दसौधभूमिं प्रपद्यते ॥ 70
5.m: Stationed attentively in the vibration of the pair of blissful channels, / he enters this palatial realm of the outpouring of creative emission. // 70

5.s:
śākte kṣobhe kulāveśe sarvanāḍyagragocare /
vyāptau sarvātmasaṃkoce hṛdayaṃ praviśetsudhīḥ // 71
5.d:
शाक्ते क्षोभे कुलावेशे सर्वनाड्यग्रगोचरे ।
व्याप्तौ सर्वात्मसंकोचे हृदयं प्रविशेत्सुधीः ॥ 71
5.m: In the agitation of śakti, in the absorption of Kula, at the object in the tips of all channels, / in pervasion, in the contraction of all beings, the wise person should enter the heart. // 71

5.s:
somasūryakalājālaparasparanigharṣataḥ /
agnīṣomātmake dhāmni visargānanda unmiṣet // 72
5.d:
सोमसूर्यकलाजालपरस्परनिघर्षतः ।
अग्नीषोमात्मके धाम्नि विसर्गानन्द उन्मिषेत् ॥ 72
5.m: From the mutual friction of the arrays of digits of moon and sun, / in the abode consisting of fire and moon, the bliss of creative emission blossoms forth. // 72

5.s:
alaṃ rahasyakathayā guptametatsvabhāvataḥ /
yoginīhṛdayaṃ tatra viśrāntaḥ syātkṛtī budhaḥ // 73
5.d:
अलं रहस्यकथया गुप्तमेतत्स्वभावतः ।
योगिनीहृदयं तत्र विश्रान्तः स्यात्कृती बुधः ॥ 73
5.m: Enough of talking about secrets! By its very nature this is concealed, / the Heart of the Yoginīs; reposing therein, the wise person becomes accomplished. // 73

5.s:
hānādānatiraskāravṛttau rūḍhimupāgataḥ /
abhedavṛttitaḥ paśyedviśvaṃ citicamatkṛteḥ // 74
5.d:
हानादानतिरस्कारवृत्तौ रूढिमुपागतः ।
अभेदवृत्तितः पश्येद्विश्वं चितिचमत्कृतेः ॥ 74
5.m: Having attained stability in the state beyond rejecting and accepting, / through the operation of non-differentiation, out of the wonder of consciousness, he sees the universe. // 74

5.s:
arthakriyārthitādainyaṃ tyaktvā bāhyāntarātmani /
kharūpe nirvṛtiṃ prāpya phullāṃ nādadaśāṃ śrayet // 75
5.d:
अर्थक्रियार्थितादैन्यं त्यक्त्वा बाह्यान्तरात्मनि ।
खरूपे निर्वृतिं प्राप्य फुल्लां नाददशां श्रयेत् ॥ 75
5.m: Abandoning the wretched longing for pragmatic efficacy, inwardly and outwardly, / having attained bliss in the nature of space, he should resort to the blossomed state of nāda. // 75

5.s:
vaktramantastayā samyak saṃvidaḥ pravikāsayet /
saṃvidakṣamaruccakraṃ jñeyābhinnaṃ tato bhavet // 76
5.d:
वक्त्रमन्तस्तया सम्यक् संविदः प्रविकासयेत् ।
संविदक्षमरुच्चक्रं ज्ञेयाभिन्नं ततो भवेत् ॥ 76
5.m: Through it, he should fully expand the mouth of consciousness internally; / then the circle of consciousness, sense faculties, and vital breath becomes non-different from the knowable. // 76

5.s:
tajjñeyaṃ saṃvidākhyena vahninā pravilīyate /
vilīnaṃ tat trikoṇe'smiñśaktivahnau vilīyate // 77
5.d:
तज्ज्ञेयं संविदाख्येन वह्निना प्रविलीयते ।
विलीनं तत् त्रिकोणेऽस्मिञ्शक्तिवह्नौ विलीयते ॥ 77
5.m: That knowable is dissolved by the fire called consciousness; / dissolved, it is dissolved in this triangle, the fire of śakti. // 77

5.s:
tatra saṃvedanodārabindusattāsunirvṛtaḥ /
saṃhārabījaviśrānto yogī paramayo bhavet // 78
5.d:
तत्र संवेदनोदारबिन्दुसत्तासुनिर्वृतः ।
संहारबीजविश्रान्तो योगी परमयो भवेत् ॥ 78
5.m: Delighted therein by the noble existence of the bindu of consciousness, / reposing in the seed of dissolution, the yogi becomes identified with the Supreme. // 78

5.s:
antarbāhye dvaye vāpi sāmānyetarasundaraḥ /
saṃvitspandastriśaktyātmā saṃkocapravikāsavān // 79
5.d:
अन्तर्बाह्ये द्वये वापि सामान्येतरसुन्दरः ।
संवित्स्पन्दस्त्रिशक्त्यात्मा संकोचप्रविकासवान् ॥ 79
5.m: Internally, externally, or in both, beautiful in the universal and the particular, / the vibration of consciousness embodies the three powers, possessing contraction and expansion. // 79

5.s:
asaṃkocavikāso'pi tadābhāsanatastathā /
antarlakṣyo bahirdṛṣṭiḥ paramaṃ padamaśnute // 80
5.d:
असंकोचविकासोऽपि तदाभासनतस्तथा ।
अन्तर्लक्ष्यो बहिर्दृष्टिः परमं पदमश्नुते ॥ 80
5.m: Even while devoid of contraction and expansion, through manifesting them in this manner, / with inner focus and outward gaze, he attains the supreme state. // 80

5.s:
tataḥ svātantryanirmeye vicitrārthakriyākṛti /
vimarśanaṃ viśeṣākhyaḥ spanda aunmukhyasaṃjñitaḥ // 81
5.d:
ततः स्वातन्त्र्यनिर्मेये विचित्रार्थक्रियाकृति ।
विमर्शनं विशेषाख्यः स्पन्द औन्मुख्यसंज्ञितः ॥ 81
5.m: Then, in the sphere created by absolute autonomy, producing manifold pragmatic efficacy, / reflective awareness is the particular vibration, designated as 'directedness'. // 81

5.s:
tatra viśrāntimāgacchedyadvīryaṃ mantramaṇḍale /
śāntyādisiddhayastattadrūpatādātmyato yataḥ // 82
5.d:
तत्र विश्रान्तिमागच्छेद्यद्वीर्यं मन्त्रमण्डले ।
शान्त्यादिसिद्धयस्तत्तद्रूपतादात्म्यतो यतः ॥ 82
5.m: He should attain repose there, which is the potency in the circle of mantras; / for spiritual accomplishments such as pacification arise through identification with their respective forms. // 82

5.s:
divyo yaścākṣasaṃgho'yaṃ bodhasvātantryasaṃjñakaḥ /
so'nimīlita evaitat kuryātsvātmamayaṃ jagat // 83
5.d:
दिव्यो यश्चाक्षसंघोऽयं बोधस्वातन्त्र्यसंज्ञकः ।
सोऽनिमीलित एवैतत् कुर्यात्स्वात्ममयं जगत् ॥ 83
5.m: And this divine assembly of sense faculties, designated as the absolute autonomy of consciousness, / remaining unclosed, should render this world composed of its own Self. // 83

5.s:
mahāsāhasasaṃyogavilīnākhilavṛttikaḥ /
puñjībhūte svaraśmyoghe nirbharībhūya tiṣṭhati // 84
5.d:
महासाहससंयोगविलीनाखिलवृत्तिकः ।
पुञ्जीभूते स्वरश्म्योघे निर्भरीभूय तिष्ठति ॥ 84
5.m: With all operations dissolved through contact with the Great Audacity, / he abides, overflowing, in the assembled mass of his own rays. // 84

5.s:
akiciccintakastatra spaṣṭadṛgyāti saṃvidam /
yadvisphuliṅgāḥ saṃsārabhasmadāhaikahetavaḥ // 85
5.d:
अकिचिच्चिन्तकस्तत्र स्पष्टदृग्याति संविदम् ।
यद्विस्फुलिङ्गाः संसारभस्मदाहैकहेतवः ॥ 85
5.m: Thinking of nothing there, with clear vision, he enters consciousness, / whose sparks are the sole cause of burning the transmigration into ashes. // 85

5.s:
taduktaṃ parameśena triśirobhairavāgame /
śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi mantrabhūmyāṃ praveśanam // 86
5.d:
तदुक्तं परमेशेन त्रिशिरोभैरवागमे ।
शृणु देवि प्रवक्ष्यामि मन्त्रभूम्यां प्रवेशनम् ॥ 86
5.m: That was spoken by the Supreme Lord in the Triśirobhairava scripture: / 'Hear, O Goddess, I will declare entrance into the plane of mantra: // 86

5.s:
madhyanāḍyordhvagamanaṃ taddharmaprāptilakṣaṇam /
visargāntapadātītaṃ prāntakoṭinirūpitam // 87
5.d:
मध्यनाड्योर्ध्वगमनं तद्धर्मप्राप्तिलक्षणम् ।
विसर्गान्तपदातीतं प्रान्तकोटिनिरूपितम् ॥ 87
5.m: The upward movement of the central channel is defined by the attainment of its characteristics; / it transcends the state at the end of creative emission and is defined at the final tip. // 87

5.s:
adhaḥpravāhasaṃrodhādūrdhvakṣepavivarjanāt /
mahāprakāśamudayajñānavyaktipradāyakam // 88
5.d:
अधःप्रवाहसंरोधादूर्ध्वक्षेपविवर्जनात् ।
महाप्रकाशमुदयज्ञानव्यक्तिप्रदायकम् ॥ 88
5.m: By blocking the downward flow and avoiding upward expulsion, / it grants the great light and the manifestation of emergent knowledge. // 88

5.s:
anubhūya pare dhāmni mātrāvṛttyā puraṃ viśet /
nistaraṅgāvatīrṇā sā vṛttirekā śivātmikā // 89
5.d:
अनुभूय परे धाम्नि मात्रावृत्त्या पुरं विशेत् ।
निस्तरङ्गावतीर्णा सा वृत्तिरेका शिवात्मिका ॥ 89
5.m: Having experienced this in the supreme abode, through the movement of the measure, he should enter the city. / Devoid of waves, that descended single movement consists of Śiva; // 89

5.s:
catuṣṣaḍdvirdviguṇitacakraṣaṭkasamujjvalā /
tatsthaṃ [tstho] vicārayet khaṃ khaṃ khasthaṃ khasthena saṃviśet // 90
5.d:
चतुष्षड्द्विर्द्विगुणितचक्रषट्कसमुज्ज्वला ।
तत्स्थं [त्स्थो] विचारयेत् खं खं खस्थं खस्थेन संविशेत् ॥ 90
5.m: it shines brilliantly with the six chakras doubled by four, six, and two. / Standing therein, he should contemplate space: space, space, resting in space; through that which rests in space, he should enter. // 90

5.s:
khaṃ khaṃ tyaktvā khamāruhya khasthaṃ khaṃ coccarediti /
khamadhyāsyādhikāreṇa padasthāścinmarīcayaḥ // 91
5.d:
खं खं त्यक्त्वा खमारुह्य खस्थं खं चोच्चरेदिति ।
खमध्यास्याधिकारेण पदस्थाश्चिन्मरीचयः ॥ 91
5.m: Abandoning space after space, ascending to space, he should sound space resting in space.' / By authority over the center of space, the rays of consciousness are established in their places. // 91

5.s:
bhāvayedbhāvamantaḥsthaṃ bhāvastho bhāvaniḥspṛhaḥ /
bhāvābhāvagatī ruddhvā bhāvābhāvāvarodhadṛk // 92
5.d:
भावयेद्भावमन्तःस्थं भावस्थो भावनिःस्पृहः ।
भावाभावगती रुद्ध्वा भावाभावावरोधदृक् ॥ 92
5.m: Established in the state [of consciousness], free from craving for external entities, one should cultivate the inner reality, / having stopped the movement of being and non-being, beholding the cessation of being and non-being. // 92

5.s:
ātmāṇukulamūlāni śaktirbhūtiścitī ratiḥ /
śaktitrayaṃ draṣṭṛdṛśyoparaktaṃ tadvivarjitam // 93
5.d:
आत्माणुकुलमूलानि शक्तिर्भूतिश्चिती रतिः ।
शक्तित्रयं द्रष्टृदृश्योपरक्तं तद्विवर्जितम् ॥ 93
5.m: Self, soul, family, root, power, manifestation, consciousness, delight, / the triad of powers colored by perceiver and perceived, and that which is free of them: // 93

5.s:
etatkhaṃ daśadhā proktamuccāroccāralakṣaṇam /
dhāmasthaṃ dhāmamadhyasthaṃ dhāmodarapuṭīkṛtam // 94
5.d:
एतत्खं दशधा प्रोक्तमुच्चारोच्चारलक्षणम् ।
धामस्थं धाममध्यस्थं धामोदरपुटीकृतम् ॥ 94
5.m: this void is taught as tenfold, characterized by phonic enunciation upon phonic enunciation; / residing in the station, residing in the middle of the station, enclosed within the cavity of the station. // 94

5.s:
dhāmnā tu bodhayeddhāma dhāma dhāmāntagaṃ kuru /
taddhāma dhāmagatyā tu bhedyaṃ dhāmāntamāntaram // 95
5.d:
धाम्ना तु बोधयेद्धाम धाम धामान्तगं कुरु ।
तद्धाम धामगत्या तु भेद्यं धामान्तमान्तरम् ॥ 95
5.m: One should awaken station through station; bring the station to the end of the station; / that station, through movement from station to station, is to be pierced to the innermost end of the station. // 95

5.s:
bhedopabhedabhedena bhedaḥ kāryastu madhyataḥ /
iti praveśopāyo'yamāṇavaḥ parikīrtitaḥ // 96
5.d:
भेदोपभेदभेदेन भेदः कार्यस्तु मध्यतः ।
इति प्रवेशोपायोऽयमाणवः परिकीर्तितः ॥ 96
5.m: Piercing is to be effected from the middle through the division of primary and secondary divisions. / Thus this individual means of absorption has been proclaimed, // 96

5.s:
śrīmaheśvaranāthena yo hṛtsthena mamoditaḥ /
śrībrahmayāmale coktaṃ śrīmān rāvo daśātmakaḥ // 97
5.d:
श्रीमहेश्वरनाथेन यो हृत्स्थेन ममोदितः ।
श्रीब्रह्मयामले चोक्तं श्रीमान् रावो दशात्मकः ॥ 97
5.m: which was spoken to me by the venerable Maheśvaranātha dwelling in my heart. / And in the venerable Brahmayāmala it is taught: 'The glorious sound is tenfold: // 97

5.s:
sthūlaḥ sūkṣmaḥ paro hṛdyaḥ kaṇṭhyastālavya eva ca /
sarvataśca vibhuryo'sau vibhutvapadadāyakaḥ // 98
5.d:
स्थूलः सूक्ष्मः परो हृद्यः कण्ठ्यस्तालव्य एव च ।
सर्वतश्च विभुर्योऽसौ विभुत्वपददायकः ॥ 98
5.m: gross, subtle, supreme, belonging to the heart, guttural, and palatal, / and that all-pervading [sound] everywhere, which bestows the state of omnipresence. // 98

5.s:
jitarāvo mahāyogī saṃkrāmetparadehagaḥ /
parāṃ ca vindati vyāptiṃ pratyahaṃ hyabhyaseta tam // 99
5.d:
जितरावो महायोगी संक्रामेत्परदेहगः ।
परां च विन्दति व्याप्तिं प्रत्यहं ह्यभ्यसेत तम् ॥ 99
5.m: The great yogin who has mastered sound can enter into another's body, / and attains supreme pervasion; one should indeed practice it every day, // 99

5.s:
tāvadyāvadarāve sā rāvāllīyeta rāviṇī /
atra bhāvanayā dehagatopāyaiḥ pare pathi // 100
5.d:
तावद्यावदरावे सा रावाल्लीयेत राविणी ।
अत्र भावनया देहगतोपायैः परे पथि ॥ 100
5.m: so long until that sounding [power] dissolves from sound into the soundless.' / Here, through contemplation by means rooted in the body, on the supreme path, // 100

5.s:
vivikṣoḥ pūrṇatāsparśātprāgānandaḥ prajāyate /
tato'pi vidyudāpātasadṛśe dehavarjite // 101
5.d:
विविक्षोः पूर्णतास्पर्शात्प्रागानन्दः प्रजायते ।
ततोऽपि विद्युदापातसदृशे देहवर्जिते ॥ 101
5.m: for one wishing to enter, bliss arises first from the contact with fullness. / Then, from absorption even for a moment in the station free from the body, // 101

5.s:
dhāmni kṣaṇaṃ samāveśādudbhavaḥ prasphuṭaṃ plutiḥ /
jalapāṃsuvadabhyastasaṃviddehaikyahānitaḥ // 102
5.d:
धाम्नि क्षणं समावेशादुद्भवः प्रस्फुटं प्लुतिः ।
जलपांसुवदभ्यस्तसंविद्देहैक्यहानितः ॥ 102
5.m: resembling a flash of lightning, there occurs an upward surge, distinctly a leaping up. / Through the abandonment of the unity of consciousness and body, practiced like water [mixed with] dust, // 102

5.s:
svabalākramaṇāddehaśaithilyāt kampamāpnuyāt /
galite dehatādātmyaniścaye'ntarbhukhatvataḥ // 103
5.d:
स्वबलाक्रमणाद्देहशैथिल्यात् कम्पमाप्नुयात् ।
गलिते देहतादात्म्यनिश्चयेऽन्तर्भुखत्वतः ॥ 103
5.m: from the surging of one's own power and the relaxation of the body, one experiences trembling. / When the conviction of identity with the body has dissolved, because of interiorization, // 103

5.s:
nidrāyate purā yāvanna rūḍhaḥ saṃvidātmani /
tataḥ satyapade rūḍho viśvātmatvena saṃvidam // 104
5.d:
निद्रायते पुरा यावन्न रूढः संविदात्मनि ।
ततः सत्यपदे रूढो विश्वात्मत्वेन संविदम् ॥ 104
5.m: one enters sleep at first, as long as one has not taken root in the self of consciousness. / Then, having taken root in the true state, experiencing consciousness // 104

5.s:
saṃvidan ghūrṇate ghūrṇirmahāvyāptiryataḥ smṛtā /
ātmanyanātmābhimatau satyāmeva hyanātmani // 105
5.d:
संविदन् घूर्णते घूर्णिर्महाव्याप्तिर्यतः स्मृता ।
आत्मन्यनात्माभिमतौ सत्यामेव ह्यनात्मनि ॥ 105
5.m: as the universal self, one whirls; for whirling is traditionally declared to be the great pervasion. / Indeed, only when there is the notion of the non-self in the Self, does the notion of Self // 105

5.s:
ātmābhimāno dehādau bandho muktistu tallayaḥ /
ādāvanātmanyātmatve līne labdhe nijātmani // 106
5.d:
आत्माभिमानो देहादौ बन्धो मुक्तिस्तु तल्लयः ।
आदावनात्मन्यात्मत्वे लीने लब्धे निजात्मनि ॥ 106
5.m: in the non-self such as the body constitute bondage; but liberation is its dissolution. / At first, when the state of Self has dissolved in the non-self and been attained in one's own Self, // 106

5.s:
ātmanyanātmatānāśe mahāvyāptiḥ pravartate /
ānanda udbhavaḥ kampo nindrā ghūrṇiśca pañcakam // 107
5.d:
आत्मन्यनात्मतानाशे महाव्याप्तिः प्रवर्तते ।
आनन्द उद्भवः कम्पो निन्द्रा घूर्णिश्च पञ्चकम् ॥ 107
5.m: and the non-selfhood in the Self has been destroyed, the great pervasion operates. / Bliss, upward surge, trembling, sleep, and whirling: this pentad // 107

5.s:
ityuktamata eva śrīmālinīvijayottare /
pradarśite'sminnānandaprabhṛtau pañcake yadā // 108
5.d:
इत्युक्तमत एव श्रीमालिनीविजयोत्तरे ।
प्रदर्शितेऽस्मिन्नानन्दप्रभृतौ पञ्चके यदा ॥ 108
5.m: has been stated for this very reason in the venerable Mālinīvijayottara. / When a yogin enters into this pentad beginning with bliss // 108

5.s:
yogī viśettadā tattaccakreśatvaṃ haṭhādvrajet /
yathā sarveśinā bodhenākrāntāpi tanuḥ kvacit // 109
5.d:
योगी विशेत्तदा तत्तच्चक्रेशत्वं हठाद्व्रजेत् ।
यथा सर्वेशिना बोधेनाक्रान्तापि तनुः क्वचित् ॥ 109
5.m: that has been shown, he forcibly attains mastership over the respective centers. / Just as the body, although pervaded by the consciousness that governs everything, is able // 109

5.s:
kiṃcitkartuṃ prabhavati cakṣuṣā rūpasaṃvidam /
tathaiva cakre kutrāpi praveśātko'pi saṃbhavet // 110
5.d:
किंचित्कर्तुं प्रभवति चक्षुषा रूपसंविदम् ।
तथैव चक्रे कुत्रापि प्रवेशात्कोऽपि संभवेत् ॥ 110
5.m: to do something somewhere, [such as] the awareness of form through the eye, / even so, from entry into a particular center, some [particular power] arises. // 110

5.s:
ānandacakraṃ vahnyaśri kanda udbhava ucyate /
kampo hṛttālu nidrā ca ghūrṇiḥ syādūrdhvakuṇḍalī // 111
5.d:
आनन्दचक्रं वह्न्यश्रि कन्द उद्भव उच्यते ।
कम्पो हृत्तालु निद्रा च घूर्णिः स्यादूर्ध्वकुण्डली ॥ 111
5.m: The center of bliss is triangular; the upward surge is said to be the bulb; / trembling is the heart; sleep is the palate; and whirling is the upward kuṇḍalī. // 111

5.s:
etacca sphuṭamevoktaṃ śrīmantraiśirase mate /
evaṃ pradarśitoccāraviśrāntihṛdayaṃ param // 112
5.d:
एतच्च स्फुटमेवोक्तं श्रीमन्त्रैशिरसे मते ।
एवं प्रदर्शितोच्चारविश्रान्तिहृदयं परम् ॥ 112
5.m: And this has been stated clearly in the venerable doctrine of the Triśirobhairava. / Thus the supreme heart of rest in phonic enunciation has been shown. // 112

5.s:
yattadavyaktaliṅgaṃ nṛśivaśaktyavibhāgavat /
atra viśvamidaṃ līnamatrāntaḥsthaṃ ca gamyate // 113
5.d:
यत्तदव्यक्तलिङ्गं नृशिवशक्त्यविभागवत् ।
अत्र विश्वमिदं लीनमत्रान्तःस्थं च गम्यते ॥ 113
5.m: That which is the unmanifest sign, having no differentiation between man, Śiva, and power, / in this the universe is dissolved, and in this it is understood to reside within. // 113

5.s:
idaṃ tallakṣaṇaṃ pūrṇaśaktibhairavasaṃvidaḥ /
dehagādhvasamunmeṣe samāveśastu yaḥ sphuṭaḥ // 114
5.d:
इदं तल्लक्षणं पूर्णशक्तिभैरवसंविदः ।
देहगाध्वसमुन्मेषे समावेशस्तु यः स्फुटः ॥ 114
5.m: This is the characteristic mark of the consciousness of Bhairava with full power. / But when there is the flashing forth of the paths residing in the body, the evident absorption, // 114

5.s:
ahantācchāditonmeṣibhāvedaṃbhāvayuk sa ca /
vyaktāvyaktamidaṃ liṅgaṃ mantravīryaṃ parāparam // 115
5.d:
अहन्ताच्छादितोन्मेषिभावेदंभावयुक् स च ।
व्यक्ताव्यक्तमिदं लिङ्गं मन्त्रवीर्यं परापरम् ॥ 115
5.m: associated with objective entities emerging covered by I-ness— / this manifest-unmanifest sign is the supreme-and-non-supreme vitality of mantra. // 115

5.s:
naraśaktisamunmeṣi śivarūpādvibheditam /
yannyakkṛtaśivāhantāsamāveśaṃ vibhedavat // 116
5.d:
नरशक्तिसमुन्मेषि शिवरूपाद्विभेदितम् ।
यन्न्यक्कृतशिवाहन्तासमावेशं विभेदवत् ॥ 116
5.m: Flashing forth through man and power, differentiated from the nature of Śiva, / wherein absorption in Śiva's I-ness is suppressed, having differentiation, // 116

5.s:
viśeṣaspandarūpaṃ tad vyaktaṃ liṅgaṃ cidātmakam /
vyaktātsiddhiprasavo vyaktāvyaktāddvayaṃ vimokṣaśca /
avyaktādbalamādyaṃ parasya nānuttare tviyaṃ carcā // 117
5.d:
विशेषस्पन्दरूपं तद् व्यक्तं लिङ्गं चिदात्मकम् ।
व्यक्तात्सिद्धिप्रसवो व्यक्ताव्यक्ताद्द्वयं विमोक्षश्च ।
अव्यक्ताद्बलमाद्यं परस्य नानुत्तरे त्वियं चर्चा ॥ 117
5.m: consisting of particular vibration—that manifest sign is of the nature of consciousness. / From the manifest comes the arising of spiritual accomplishment; from the manifest-unmanifest comes both and liberation; / from the unmanifest comes the primal power of the Supreme; but in the unexcelled this inquiry does not apply. // 117

5.s:
ātmākhyaṃ yadvyaktaṃ naraliṅgaṃ tatra viśvamarpayataḥ /
vyaktāvyaktaṃ tasmādgalite tasmiṃstadavyaktam // 118
5.d:
आत्माख्यं यद्व्यक्तं नरलिङ्गं तत्र विश्वमर्पयतः ।
व्यक्ताव्यक्तं तस्माद्गलिते तस्मिंस्तदव्यक्तम् ॥ 118
5.m: For one who offers the universe into that manifest sign of man, called the self, / it becomes the manifest-unmanifest; when that has fallen away, it becomes the unmanifest. // 118

5.s:
tenātmaliṅgametat parame śivaśaktyaṇusvabhāvamaye /
avyakte viśrāmyati nānuttaradhāmagā tviyaṃ carcā // 119
5.d:
तेनात्मलिङ्गमेतत् परमे शिवशक्त्यणुस्वभावमये ।
अव्यक्ते विश्राम्यति नानुत्तरधामगा त्वियं चर्चा ॥ 119
5.m: Therefore this sign of the self comes to rest in the supreme unmanifest / whose nature consists of Śiva, power, and the soul; but this inquiry does not belong to the unexcelled station. // 119

5.s:
ekasya spandanasyaiṣā traidhaṃ bhedavyavasthitiḥ /
atra liṅge sadā tiṣṭhet pūjāviśrāntitatparaḥ // 120
5.d:
एकस्य स्पन्दनस्यैषा त्रैधं भेदव्यवस्थितिः ।
अत्र लिङ्गे सदा तिष्ठेत् पूजाविश्रान्तितत्परः ॥ 120
5.m: This threefold division is the arrangement of a single vibration. / One should always abide in this sign, intent upon worship and rest. // 120

5.s:
yoginīhṛdayaṃ liṅgamidamānandasundaram /
bījayonisamāpattyā sūte kāmapi saṃvidam // 121
5.d:
योगिनीहृदयं लिङ्गमिदमानन्दसुन्दरम् ।
बीजयोनिसमापत्त्या सूते कामपि संविदम् ॥ 121
5.m: This sign is the heart of the yoginī, lovely with bliss; / through the union of seed and womb, it generates an ineffable consciousness. // 121

5.s:
atra prayāsavirahātsarvo'sau devatāgaṇaḥ /
ānandapūrṇe dhāmnyāste nityoditacidātmakaḥ // 122
5.d:
अत्र प्रयासविरहात्सर्वोऽसौ देवतागणः ।
आनन्दपूर्णे धाम्न्यास्ते नित्योदितचिदात्मकः ॥ 122
5.m: Here, free from exertion, that entire host of deities / resides in the station full of bliss, of ever-risen conscious nature. // 122

5.s:
atra bhairavanāthasya sasaṃkocavikāsikā /
bhāsate durghaṭā śaktirasaṃkocavikāsinaḥ // 123
5.d:
अत्र भैरवनाथस्य ससंकोचविकासिका ।
भासते दुर्घटा शक्तिरसंकोचविकासिनः ॥ 123
5.m: Here shines the power of Lord Bhairava, which is difficult to accomplish, / unfolding with contraction, belonging to Him who unfolds without contraction. // 123

5.s:
etalliṅgasamāpattivisargānandadhārayā /
siktaṃ tadeva sadviśvaṃ śaśvannavanavāyate // 124
5.d:
एतल्लिङ्गसमापत्तिविसर्गानन्दधारया ।
सिक्तं तदेव सद्विश्वं शश्वन्नवनवायते ॥ 124
5.m: Sprinkled by the stream of the bliss of emission upon union with this sign, / this very universe continually becomes ever-new. // 124

5.s:
anuttare'bhyupāyo'tra tādrūpyādeva varṇitaḥ /
jvaliteṣvapi dīpeṣu gharmāṃśuḥ kiṃ na bhāsate // 125
5.d:
अनुत्तरेऽभ्युपायोऽत्र ताद्रूप्यादेव वर्णितः ।
ज्वलितेष्वपि दीपेषु घर्मांशुः किं न भासते ॥ 125
5.m: Here, an approach to the unexcelled has been described precisely on account of having its nature: / when lamps are lit, does the sun not shine? // 125

5.s:
artheṣu tadbhogavidhau tadutthe duḥkhe sukhe vā galitābhiśaṅkam /
anāviśanto'pi nimagnacittā jānanti vṛttikṣayasaukhyamantaḥ // 126
5.d:
अर्थेषु तद्भोगविधौ तदुत्थे दुःखे सुखे वा गलिताभिशङ्कम् ।
अनाविशन्तोऽपि निमग्नचित्ता जानन्ति वृत्तिक्षयसौख्यमन्तः ॥ 126
5.m: In the presence of objects, in the enjoyment of them, or in pleasure or pain arising from them, with doubts dispelled, / those whose minds are immersed, even without formal entry, know within the joy of the cessation of mental fluctuations. // 126

5.s:
satyevātmani citsvabhāvamahasi svānte tathopaktiyāṃ tasmai kurvati tatpracāravivaśe satyakṣavarge'pi ca /
satsvartheṣu sukhādiṣu sphuṭataraṃ yadbhedavandhyodayaṃ yogī tiṣṭhati pūrṇaraśmivibhavastattattvamācīyatām // 127
5.d:
सत्येवात्मनि चित्स्वभावमहसि स्वान्ते तथोपक्तियां तस्मै कुर्वति तत्प्रचारविवशे सत्यक्षवर्गेऽपि च ।
सत्स्वर्थेषु सुखादिषु स्फुटतरं यद्भेदवन्ध्योदयं योगी तिष्ठति पूर्णरश्मिविभवस्तत्तत्त्वमाचीयताम् ॥ 127
5.m: Even when the Self exists, a splendor whose nature is consciousness; when the internal organ renders service to it; when the senses, helpless in their functioning, exist; / and when objects, pleasure, and the rest exist—let that reality be practiced wherein the yogin abides, rich in full rays, with an arising evidently barren of division. // 127

5.s:
ityuccāravidhiḥ proktaḥ karaṇaṃ pravivicyate /
taccetthaṃ triśiraḥśāstre parameśena bhāṣitam // 128
5.d:
इत्युच्चारविधिः प्रोक्तः करणं प्रविविच्यते ।
तच्चेत्थं त्रिशिरःशास्त्रे परमेशेन भाषितम् ॥ 128
5.m: Thus the rule of phonic enunciation has been stated; the bodily posture is now thoroughly analyzed. / And it was spoken thus in the Triśirobhairava scripture by the Supreme Lord: // 128

5.s:
grāhyagrāhakacidvyāptityāgākṣepaniveśanaiḥ /
karaṇaṃ saptadhā prāhurabhyāsaṃ bodhapūrvakam // 129
5.d:
ग्राह्यग्राहकचिद्व्याप्तित्यागाक्षेपनिवेशनैः ।
करणं सप्तधा प्राहुरभ्यासं बोधपूर्वकम् ॥ 129
5.m: Through pervasion, abandonment, casting, and settling of the object, subject, and consciousness, / they teach bodily posture as sevenfold, a practice preceded by awakening. // 129

5.s:
tadvyāptipūrvamākṣepe karaṇaṃ svapratiṣṭhatā /
guruvaktrācca boddhavyaṃ karaṇaṃ yadyapi sphuṭam // 130
5.d:
तद्व्याप्तिपूर्वमाक्षेपे करणं स्वप्रतिष्ठता ।
गुरुवक्त्राच्च बोद्धव्यं करणं यद्यपि स्फुटम् ॥ 130
5.m: Bodily posture is established in itself upon casting [them] preceded by that pervasion. / Although bodily posture should be understood clearly from the mouth of the guru, // 130

5.s:
tathāpyāgamarakṣārthaṃ tadagre varṇayiṣyate /
ukto ya eṣa uccārastatra yo'sau sphuran sthitaḥ // 131
5.d:
तथाप्यागमरक्षार्थं तदग्रे वर्णयिष्यते ।
उक्तो य एष उच्चारस्तत्र योऽसौ स्फुरन् स्थितः ॥ 131
5.m: nonetheless it will be described ahead for the sake of preserving the tradition. / In that enunciation which has been stated, that vibrating sound which remains, // 131

5.s:
avyaktānukṛtiprāyo dhvanirvarṇaḥ sa kathyate /
sṛṣṭisaṃhārabījaṃ ca tasya mukhyaṃ vapurviduḥ // 132
5.d:
अव्यक्तानुकृतिप्रायो ध्वनिर्वर्णः स कथ्यते ।
सृष्टिसंहारबीजं च तस्य मुख्यं वपुर्विदुः ॥ 132
5.m: mostly imitating the unmanifest, is called a phoneme; / and they know the seed of creation and dissolution to be its principal form. // 132

5.s:
tadabhyāsavaśādyāti kramādyogī cidātmatām /
tathā hyanacke sācke vā kādau sānte punaḥpunaḥ // 133
5.d:
तदभ्यासवशाद्याति क्रमाद्योगी चिदात्मताम् ।
तथा ह्यनच्के साच्के वा कादौ सान्ते पुनःपुनः ॥ 133
5.m: Through the practice of that, the yogin gradually attains the nature of consciousness. / For thus, when [a consonant] without vowels or with vowels, beginning with ka and ending with sa, // 133

5.s:
smṛte proccārite vāpi sā sā saṃvitprasūyāte /
bāhyārthasamayāpekṣā ghaṭādyā dhvanayo'pi ye // 134
5.d:
स्मृते प्रोच्चारिते वापि सा सा संवित्प्रसूयाते ।
बाह्यार्थसमयापेक्षा घटाद्या ध्वनयोऽपि ये ॥ 134
5.m: is recollected or enunciated again and again, that particular consciousness is born. / Even those sounds such as 'pot', dependent on convention regarding external objects, // 134

5.s:
te'pyarthabhāvanāṃ kuryurmanorājyavadātmani /
taduktaṃ parameśena bhairavo vyāpako'khile // 135
5.d:
तेऽप्यर्थभावनां कुर्युर्मनोराज्यवदात्मनि ।
तदुक्तं परमेशेन भैरवो व्यापकोऽखिले ॥ 135
5.m: produce contemplation of the object in oneself, like a daydream. / That has been stated by the Supreme Lord: 'Bhairava is all-pervading in everything.' // 135

5.s:
iti bhairavaśabdasya saṃtatoccāraṇācchivaḥ /
śrīmattraiśirase'pyuktaṃ mantroddhārasya pūrvataḥ // 136
5.d:
इति भैरवशब्दस्य संततोच्चारणाच्छिवः ।
श्रीमत्त्रैशिरसेऽप्युक्तं मन्त्रोद्धारस्य पूर्वतः ॥ 136
5.m: "Thus, through the uninterrupted utterance of the word Bhairava, one becomes Śiva." / It is also stated in the venerable Traiśirasa prior to the extraction of mantras:

5.s:
smṛtiśca smaraṇaṃ pūrvaṃ sarvabhāveṣu vastutaḥ /
mantrasvarūpaṃ tadbhāvyasvarūpāpattiyojakam // 137
5.d:
स्मृतिश्च स्मरणं पूर्वं सर्वभावेषु वस्तुतः ।
मन्त्रस्वरूपं तद्भाव्यस्वरूपापत्तियोजकम् ॥ 137
5.m: "And memory is prior recollection in all existing entities, in truth; / it is the intrinsic nature of the mantra, bringing about absorption into the intrinsic nature of what is to be contemplated.

5.s:
smṛtiḥ svarūpajanikā sarvabhāveṣu rañjikā /
anekākārarūpeṇa sarvatrāvasthitena tu // 138
5.d:
स्मृतिः स्वरूपजनिका सर्वभावेषु रञ्जिका ।
अनेकाकाररूपेण सर्वत्रावस्थितेन तु ॥ 138
5.m: Memory brings forth intrinsic nature, providing delight in all existing entities; / but, residing everywhere through manifold forms,

5.s:
svasvabhāvasya saṃprāptiḥ saṃvittiḥ paramārthataḥ /
vyaktiniṣṭhā tato viddhi sattā sā kīrtitā parā // 139
5.d:
स्वस्वभावस्य संप्राप्तिः संवित्तिः परमार्थतः ।
व्यक्तिनिष्ठा ततो विद्धि सत्ता सा कीर्तिता परा ॥ 139
5.m: the attainment of one's own nature is, in the highest sense, consciousness; / know that from this it culminates in individual manifestation, and is celebrated as supreme existence."

5.s:
kiṃ punaḥ samayāpekṣāṃ vinā ye bījapiṇḍakāḥ /
saṃvidaṃ spandapantyete neyuḥ saṃvidupāyatām // 140
5.d:
किं पुनः समयापेक्षां विना ये बीजपिण्डकाः ।
संविदं स्पन्दपन्त्येते नेयुः संविदुपायताम् ॥ 140
5.m: How much more, then, do these seed-syllables and cluster-syllables—which cause consciousness to vibrate / without dependence on conventional signification—lead to the state of being a means to consciousness!

5.s:
vācyābhāvādudāsīnasaṃvitspandātsvadhāmataḥ /
prāṇollāsanirodhābhyāṃ bījapiṇḍeṣu pūrṇatā // 141
5.d:
वाच्याभावादुदासीनसंवित्स्पन्दात्स्वधामतः ।
प्राणोल्लासनिरोधाभ्यां बीजपिण्डेषु पूर्णता ॥ 141
5.m: From the vibration of consciousness indifferent to objects because there is no designated object, from its own abode, / fullness in seed-syllables and cluster-syllables arises through the expansion and restraint of the vital breath.

5.s:
sukhasītkārasatsamyaksāmyaprathamasaṃvidaḥ /
saṃvedanaṃ hi prathamaṃ sparśo'nuttarasaṃvidaḥ // 142
5.d:
सुखसीत्कारसत्सम्यक्साम्यप्रथमसंविदः ।
संवेदनं हि प्रथमं स्पर्शोऽनुत्तरसंविदः ॥ 142
5.m: The initial awareness of the true, perfect equanimity of the blissful sound "sīt" / is indeed the first touch of unexcelled consciousness.

5.s:
hṛtkaṇṭhyoṣṭhyatridhāmāntarnitarāṃ pravikāsini /
caturdaśaḥ praveśo ya ekīkṛtatadātmakaḥ // 143
5.d:
हृत्कण्ठ्योष्ठ्यत्रिधामान्तर्नितरां प्रविकासिनि ।
चतुर्दशः प्रवेशो य एकीकृततदात्मकः ॥ 143
5.m: When within the three abodes of the heart, throat, and lips it expands completely, / that which is the fourteenth penetration, having become unified with its nature,

5.s:
tato visargoccārāṃśe dvādaśāntapathāvubhau /
hṛdayena sahaikadhyaṃ nayate japatatparaḥ // 144
5.d:
ततो विसर्गोच्चारांशे द्वादशान्तपथावुभौ ।
हृदयेन सहैकध्यं नयते जपतत्परः ॥ 144
5.m: then, in the portion of the utterance of the creative emission, one intent on recitation / unites the two paths of the dvādaśānta together with the heart.

5.s:
kandahṛtkaṇṭhatālvagrakauṇḍilīprakriyāntataḥ /
ānandamadhyanāḍyantaḥ spandanaṃ bījamāvahet // 145
5.d:
कन्दहृत्कण्ठताल्वग्रकौण्डिलीप्रक्रियान्ततः ।
आनन्दमध्यनाड्यन्तः स्पन्दनं बीजमावहेत् ॥ 145
5.m: Through the culmination of the process of the bulb, heart, throat, tip of the palate, and Kuṇḍalinī, / vibration within the central channel of bliss brings about the seed.

5.s:
saṃhārabījaṃ khaṃ hṛtsthamoṣṭhyaṃ phullaṃ svamūrdhani /
tejastryaśraṃ tālukaṇṭhe bindurūrdhvapade sthitaḥ // 146
5.d:
संहारबीजं खं हृत्स्थमोष्ठ्यं फुल्लं स्वमूर्धनि ।
तेजस्त्र्यश्रं तालुकण्ठे बिन्दुरूर्ध्वपदे स्थितः ॥ 146
5.m: The seed of dissolution is empty space, located in the heart; labial, blossomed on one's own head; / fire is triangular, in the palate and throat; the bindu resides in the upper plane.

5.s:
ityenayā budho yuktyā varṇajapyaparāyaṇaḥ /
anuttaraṃ paraṃ dhāma praviśedacirāt sudhīḥ // 147
5.d:
इत्येनया बुधो युक्त्या वर्णजप्यपरायणः ।
अनुत्तरं परं धाम प्रविशेदचिरात् सुधीः ॥ 147
5.m: By this method, the wise practitioner intent on the recitation of phonemes, / of keen intellect, will soon enter the supreme, unexcelled abode.

5.s:
varṇaśabdena nīlādi yadvā dīkṣottare yathā /
saṃhāranragnimaruto rudrabinduyutānsmaret // 148
5.d:
वर्णशब्देन नीलादि यद्वा दीक्षोत्तरे यथा ।
संहारन्रग्निमरुतो रुद्रबिन्दुयुतान्स्मरेत् ॥ 148
5.m: Or, by the word "phoneme," [are meant] blue and so forth, as in the Dīkṣottara: / "One should remember the winds of dissolution, man, and fire, joined with Rudra and the bindu.

5.s:
hṛdaye tanmayo lakṣyaṃ paśyetsaptadinādatha /
visphuliṅgāgnivannīlapītaraktādicitritam // 149
5.d:
हृदये तन्मयो लक्ष्यं पश्येत्सप्तदिनादथ ।
विस्फुलिङ्गाग्निवन्नीलपीतरक्तादिचित्रितम् ॥ 149
5.m: Identified with that, in the heart one sees the focus of contemplation after seven days, / variegated with blue, yellow, red, and other colors like sparks of fire.

5.s:
jājvalīti hṛdambhoje bījadīpaprabodhitam /
dīpavajjvalito bindurbhāsate vighanārkavat // 150
5.d:
जाज्वलीति हृदम्भोजे बीजदीपप्रबोधितम् ।
दीपवज्ज्वलितो बिन्दुर्भासते विघनार्कवत् ॥ 150
5.m: It blazes intensely in the lotus of the heart, awakened by the lamp of the seed; / the bindu, blazing like a lamp, shines forth like a cloudless sun.

5.s:
svayaṃbhāsātmanānena tādātmyaṃ yātyananyadhīḥ /
śivena hematāṃ yadvattāmraṃ sūtena vedhitam // 151
5.d:
स्वयंभासात्मनानेन तादात्म्यं यात्यनन्यधीः ।
शिवेन हेमतां यद्वत्ताम्रं सूतेन वेधितम् ॥ 151
5.m: With an undivided mind, one attains identity with this self-luminous self, / just as copper pierced by mercury attains the state of gold [by the grace of] Śiva."

5.s:
upalakṣaṇametacca sarvamantreṣu lakṣayet /
yadyatsaṃkalpasaṃbhūtaṃ varṇajālaṃ hi bhautikam // 152
5.d:
उपलक्षणमेतच्च सर्वमन्त्रेषु लक्षयेत् ।
यद्यत्संकल्पसंभूतं वर्णजालं हि भौतिकम् ॥ 152
5.m: And this should be recognized as an illustrative indication in all mantras. / For whatever network of phonemes arises from mental construction is indeed material;

5.s:
tat saṃvidādhikyavaśādabhautikamiva sthitam /
atastathāvidhe rūpe rūḍho rohati saṃvidi // 153
5.d:
तत् संविदाधिक्यवशादभौतिकमिव स्थितम् ।
अतस्तथाविधे रूपे रूढो रोहति संविदि ॥ 153
5.m: yet, by the primacy of consciousness, it stands as if immaterial. / Therefore, grounded in such a form, one ascends to consciousness.

5.s:
anācchāditarūpāyāmanupādhau prasannadhīḥ /
nīle pīte sukhe duḥkhe saṃvidrūpamakhaṇḍitam // 154
5.d:
अनाच्छादितरूपायामनुपाधौ प्रसन्नधीः ।
नीले पीते सुखे दुःखे संविद्रूपमखण्डितम् ॥ 154
5.m: One of clear mind [perceives] undivided consciousness in its unconditioned, / uncovered nature, [whether] in blue, yellow, pleasure, or pain.

5.s:
gurubhirbhāṣitaṃ tasmādupāyeṣu vicitratā /
uccārakaraṇadhyānavarṇairebhiḥ pradarśitaḥ // 155
5.d:
गुरुभिर्भाषितं तस्मादुपायेषु विचित्रता ।
उच्चारकरणध्यानवर्णैरेभिः प्रदर्शितः ॥ 155
5.m: Therefore, diversity among the means was declared by the gurus; / this has been demonstrated through utterance, bodily posture, meditation, and phonemes.

5.s:
anuttarapadaprāptāvabhyupāyavidhikramaḥ /
akiṃciccintanaṃ vīryaṃ bhāvanāyāṃ ca sā punaḥ // 156
5.d:
अनुत्तरपदप्राप्तावभ्युपायविधिक्रमः ।
अकिंचिच्चिन्तनं वीर्यं भावनायां च सा पुनः ॥ 156
5.m: In the attainment of the unexcelled plane, the sequence of the injunction of means [is as follows]: / the contemplation of nothingness is the potency within creative contemplation; and that, in turn,

5.s:
dhyāne tadapi coccāre karaṇe so'pi taddhvanau /
sa sthānakalpane bāhyamiti kramamupāśrayet // 157
5.d:
ध्याने तदपि चोच्चारे करणे सोऽपि तद्ध्वनौ ।
स स्थानकल्पने बाह्यमिति क्रममुपाश्रयेत् ॥ 157
