5.m: [is present] in meditation; and that also in utterance; that too in bodily posture; and that in sound; / that in the projection of places; one should resort to this sequence [as] external.

5.s:
laṅghanena paro yogī mandabuddhiḥ krameṇa tu /
vīryaṃ vinā yathā ṣaṇṭhastasyāpyastyatha vā balam /
mṛtadeha iveyaṃ syādbāhyāntaḥparikalpanā // 158
5.d:
लङ्घनेन परो योगी मन्दबुद्धिः क्रमेण तु ।
वीर्यं विना यथा षण्ठस्तस्याप्यस्त्यथ वा बलम् ।
मृतदेह इवेयं स्याद्बाह्यान्तःपरिकल्पना ॥ 158
5.m: The supreme yogin [attains it] by a leap, but one of dull intellect by degrees. / For just as a eunuch is without potency, yet may have strength, / so this external and internal projection would be as in a dead body [if devoid of that potency].

5.s: ityāṇave'nuttaratābhyupāyaḥ prokto nayaḥ spaṣṭapathena bāhyaḥ // 159
5.d: इत्याणवेऽनुत्तरताभ्युपायः प्रोक्तो नयः स्पष्टपथेन बाह्यः ॥ 159
5.m: Thus, in the realm of the individual means, the external method that is a means to unexcelled reality has been declared on a clear path.

6.s: sthānaprakalpākhyatayā sphuṭastu bāhyo'bhyupāyaḥ pravivicyate'tha // 1
6.d: स्थानप्रकल्पाख्यतया स्फुटस्तु बाह्योऽभ्युपायः प्रविविच्यतेऽथ ॥ 1
6.m: Now, the external means, known distinctly by the designation of the projection of places, is investigated.

6.s:
sthānabhedastridhā proktaḥ prāṇe dehe bahistathā /
prāṇaśca pañcadhā dehe dvidhā bāhyāntaratvataḥ // 2
6.d:
स्थानभेदस्त्रिधा प्रोक्तः प्राणे देहे बहिस्तथा ।
प्राणश्च पञ्चधा देहे द्विधा बाह्यान्तरत्वतः ॥ 2
6.m: The division of places is declared to be threefold: in the vital breath, in the body, and likewise externally. / The vital breath is fivefold; in the body it is twofold, by way of being external and internal.

6.s:
maṇḍalaṃ sthaṇḍilaṃ pātramakṣasūtraṃ sapustakam /
liṅgaṃ tūraṃ paṭaḥ pustaṃ pratimā mūrtireva ca // 3
6.d:
मण्डलं स्थण्डिलं पात्रमक्षसूत्रं सपुस्तकम् ।
लिङ्गं तूरं पटः पुस्तं प्रतिमा मूर्तिरेव च ॥ 3
6.m: A maṇḍala, an altar-ground, a vessel, a rosary together with a book, / a liṅga, an instrument, a cloth, a manuscript, an image, and a sculpture—

6.s:
ityekādaśadhā bāhyaṃ punastadbahudhā bhavet /
tatra prāṇāśrayaṃ tāvadvidhānamupadiśyate // 4
6.d:
इत्येकादशधा बाह्यं पुनस्तद्बहुधा भवेत् ।
तत्र प्राणाश्रयं तावद्विधानमुपदिश्यते ॥ 4
6.m: thus the external is elevenfold; further, it becomes manifold. / Therein, first the method resting upon the vital breath is taught.

6.s:
adhvā samasta evāyaṃ ṣaḍvidho'pyativistṛtaḥ /
yo vakṣyate sa ekatra prāṇe tāvatpratiṣṭhitaḥ // 5
6.d:
अध्वा समस्त एवायं षड्विधोऽप्यतिविस्तृतः ।
यो वक्ष्यते स एकत्र प्राणे तावत्प्रतिष्ठितः ॥ 5
6.m: This entire path, though sixfold and exceedingly extensive, / which will be described, is first established in the vital breath as one.

6.s:
adhvanaḥ kalanaṃ yattatkramākramatayā sthitam /
kramākramau hi citraikakalanā bhāvagocare // 6
6.d:
अध्वनः कलनं यत्तत्क्रमाक्रमतया स्थितम् ।
क्रमाक्रमौ हि चित्रैककलना भावगोचरे ॥ 6
6.m: That reckoning of the path which exists by way of succession and non-succession— / for succession and non-succession are a single manifold reckoning in the domain of entities—

6.s:
kramākramātmā kālaśca paraḥ saṃvidi vartate /
kālī nāma parā śaktiḥ saiva devasya gīyate // 7
6.d:
क्रमाक्रमात्मा कालश्च परः संविदि वर्तते ।
काली नाम परा शक्तिः सैव देवस्य गीयते ॥ 7
6.m: and time, consisting of succession and non-succession, exists in supreme consciousness; / she is sung as the supreme power named Kālī of the divine Lord.

6.s:
saiva saṃvidbahiḥ svātmagarbhībhūtau kramākramau /
sphuṭayantī prarohaṇa prāṇavṛttiriti sthitā // 8
6.d:
सैव संविद्बहिः स्वात्मगर्भीभूतौ क्रमाक्रमौ ।
स्फुटयन्ती प्ररोहण प्राणवृत्तिरिति स्थिता ॥ 8
6.m: That very consciousness, clearly manifesting externally through growth / succession and non-succession which are held within its own nature, exists as the movement of the vital breath.

6.s:
saṃvinmātraṃ hi yacchuddhaṃ prakāśaparamārthakam /
tanmeyamātmanaḥ projjhya viviktaṃ bhāsate nabhaḥ // 9
6.d:
संविन्मात्रं हि यच्छुद्धं प्रकाशपरमार्थकम् ।
तन्मेयमात्मनः प्रोज्झ्य विविक्तं भासते नभः ॥ 9
6.m: For pure consciousness alone, whose ultimate reality is luminosity, / shines as empty space distinct [from everything], casting aside knowable objects from itself.

6.s:
tadeva śūnyarūpatvaṃ saṃvidaḥ parigīyate /
neti neti vimarśena yogināṃ sā parā daśā // 10
6.d:
तदेव शून्यरूपत्वं संविदः परिगीयते ।
नेति नेति विमर्शेन योगिनां सा परा दशा ॥ 10
6.m: That very voidness of consciousness is celebrated; / it is the supreme state of the yogins by means of the reflective awareness "not this, not this."

6.s:
sa eva khātmā meye'sminbhedite svīkriyonmukhaḥ /
patansamucchalattvena prāṇaspandormisaṃjñitaḥ // 11
6.d:
स एव खात्मा मेयेऽस्मिन्भेदिते स्वीक्रियोन्मुखः ।
पतन्समुच्छलत्त्वेन प्राणस्पन्दोर्मिसंज्ञितः ॥ 11
6.m: That very space-like self, oriented toward appropriation when this knowable object is differentiated, / descending in the form of a surge, is termed the wave of the vibration of the vital breath.

6.s:
tenāhuḥ kila saṃvitprākprāṇe pariṇatā tathā /
antaḥkaraṇatattvasya vāyurāśrayatāṃ gataḥ // 12
6.d:
तेनाहुः किल संवित्प्राक्प्राणे परिणता तथा ।
अन्तःकरणतत्त्वस्य वायुराश्रयतां गतः ॥ 12
6.m: Therefore they say: consciousness indeed was first transformed into the vital breath, / and so the wind became the locus of the psychic apparatus.

6.s:
iyaṃ sā prāṇanāśaktirāntarodyogadohadā /
spandaḥ sphurattā viśrāntirjīvo hṛtpratibhā matā // 13
6.d:
इयं सा प्राणनाशक्तिरान्तरोद्योगदोहदा ।
स्पन्दः स्फुरत्ता विश्रान्तिर्जीवो हृत्प्रतिभा मता ॥ 13
6.m: This is that power of life, yielding the inner striving; / it is considered vibration, vibrant radiance, repose, the individual living soul, the heart, and intuitive flash.

6.s:
sā prāṇavṛttiḥ prāṇādyai rūpaiḥ pañcabhirātmasāt /
dehaṃ yatkurute saṃvitpūrṇastenaiṣa bhāsate // 14
6.d:
सा प्राणवृत्तिः प्राणाद्यै रूपैः पञ्चभिरात्मसात् ।
देहं यत्कुरुते संवित्पूर्णस्तेनैष भासते ॥ 14
6.m: Because consciousness appropriates the body by that movement of the vital breath / through the five forms such as prāṇa, the body shines forth filled with consciousness.

6.s:
prāṇanāvṛttitādātmyasaṃvitkhacitadehajām /
ceṣṭāṃ paśyantyato mugdhā nāstyanyaditi manvate // 15
6.d:
प्राणनावृत्तितादात्म्यसंवित्खचितदेहजाम् ।
चेष्टां पश्यन्त्यतो मुग्धा नास्त्यन्यदिति मन्वते ॥ 15
6.m: Seeing bodily activity arising from the body intertwined with consciousness through identity with the movement of life, / the bewildered therefore think: "There is nothing else."

6.s:
tāmeva bālamūrkhastrīprāyaveditṛsaṃśritām /
matiṃ pramāṇīkurvantaścārvākāstattvadarśinaḥ // 16
6.d:
तामेव बालमूर्खस्त्रीप्रायवेदितृसंश्रिताम् ।
मतिं प्रमाणीकुर्वन्तश्चार्वाकास्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥ 16
6.m: Taking as authoritative that very notion, / which relies on knowers who are mostly children, fools, and women, the Cārvākas consider themselves knowers of reality.

6.s:
teṣāṃ tathā bhāvanā caddārḍhyameti nirantaram /
taddehabhaṅge suptāḥ syurātādṛgvāsanākṣayāt // 17
6.d:
तेषां तथा भावना चद्दार्ढ्यमेति निरन्तरम् ।
तद्देहभङ्गे सुप्ताः स्युरातादृग्वासनाक्षयात् ॥ 17
6.m: And if their conviction becomes firm and continuous in that way, / at the destruction of their body they would remain asleep until the destruction of that mental impression.

6.s:
tadvāsanākṣaye tveṣāmakṣīṇaṃ vāsanāntaram /
buddhaṃ kutaścitsaṃsūte vicitrāṃ phalasampadam // 18
6.d:
तद्वासनाक्षये त्वेषामक्षीणं वासनान्तरम् ।
बुद्धं कुतश्चित्संसूते विचित्रां फलसम्पदम् ॥ 18
6.m: When that mental impression is destroyed, another undestroyed impression / awakened by something produces a manifold store of fruit for them.

6.s:
adārḍhyaśaṅkanātprācyavāsanātādavasthyataḥ /
anyakartavyaśaithilyātsaṃbhāvyānuśayatvataḥ // 19
6.d:
अदार्ढ्यशङ्कनात्प्राच्यवासनातादवस्थ्यतः ।
अन्यकर्तव्यशैथिल्यात्संभाव्यानुशयत्वतः ॥ 19
6.m: Because of the fear of instability, because of the persistence of previous mental impressions, / because of the slackening of other duties, and because of probable remorse,

6.s:
atadrūḍhānyajanatākartavyaparilopanāt /
nāstikyavāsanāmāhuḥ pāpātpāpīyasīmimām // 20
6.d:
अतद्रूढान्यजनताकर्तव्यपरिलोपनात् ।
नास्तिक्यवासनामाहुः पापात्पापीयसीमिमाम् ॥ 20
6.m: and because it destroys the duties of other people not established in that [view], / they declare this impression of materialism to be more evil than evil.

6.s:
alamaprastutenātha prakṛtaṃ pravivicyate /
yāvānsamasta evāyamadhvā prāṇe pratiṣṭhitaḥ // 21
6.d:
अलमप्रस्तुतेनाथ प्रकृतं प्रविविच्यते ।
यावान्समस्त एवायमध्वा प्राणे प्रतिष्ठितः ॥ 21
6.m: Enough of what is irrelevant! Now the matter at hand is investigated: / the extent to which this entire path is established in the vital breath.

6.s:
dvidhā ca so'dhvā kriyayā mūrtyā ca pravibhajyate /
prāṇa eva śikhā śrīmattriśirasyuditā hi sā // 22
6.d:
द्विधा च सोऽध्वा क्रियया मूर्त्या च प्रविभज्यते ।
प्राण एव शिखा श्रीमत्त्रिशिरस्युदिता हि सा ॥ 22
6.m: And that path is divided into two: by action and by form. / The vital breath itself is the tuft, for it is declared in the venerable Triśiras.

6.s:
baddhā yāgādikāle tuṃ niṣkalatvācchivātmikā /
yato'horātramadhye'syāścaturviṃśatidhā gatiḥ // 23
6.d:
बद्धा यागादिकाले तुं निष्कलत्वाच्छिवात्मिका ।
यतोऽहोरात्रमध्येऽस्याश्चतुर्विंशतिधा गतिः ॥ 23
6.m: When bound at the time of sacrifice and other rites, however, it is identical with Śiva because of its divisionless nature, / since during a day and night its movement occurs twenty-fourfold. // 23

6.s:
prāṇavikṣeparandhrākhyaśataiścitraphalapradā /
kṣapā śaśī tathāpāno nāda ekatra tiṣṭhati // 24
6.d:
प्राणविक्षेपरन्ध्राख्यशतैश्चित्रफलप्रदा ।
क्षपा शशी तथापानो नाद एकत्र तिष्ठति ॥ 24
6.m: Bestowing diverse fruits by hundreds of what are called holes of breath emission: / night, moon, as well as apāna, and resonance remain in one place; // 24

6.s:
jīvādityo na codgacchettuṭyardhaṃ sāndhyamīdṛśam /
ūrdhvavaktro raviścandro'dhomukho vahnirantare // 25
6.d:
जीवादित्यो न चोद्गच्छेत्तुट्यर्धं सान्ध्यमीदृशम् ।
ऊर्ध्ववक्त्रो रविश्चन्द्रोऽधोमुखो वह्निरन्तरे ॥ 25
6.m: and the sun of the living breath does not rise—such is the twilight lasting half a tuṭi. / The sun has its face turned upward, the moon downward, with fire in between. // 25

6.s:
mādhyāhnikī mokṣadā syādvyomamadhyasthito raviḥ /
anastamitasāro hi jantucakraprabodhakaḥ // 26
6.d:
माध्याह्निकी मोक्षदा स्याद्व्योममध्यस्थितो रविः ।
अनस्तमितसारो हि जन्तुचक्रप्रबोधकः ॥ 26
6.m: The noon [junction] would bestow liberation, with the sun situated in the middle of space; / for its essence is unsetting, awakening the host of creatures. // 26

6.s:
binduḥ prāṇo hyahaścaiva ravirekatra tiṣṭhati /
mahāsandhyā tṛtīyā tu supraśāntātmikā sthitā // 27
6.d:
बिन्दुः प्राणो ह्यहश्चैव रविरेकत्र तिष्ठति ।
महासन्ध्या तृतीया तु सुप्रशान्तात्मिका स्थिता ॥ 27
6.m: The point of light, the prāṇa, the day, and the sun indeed abide together. / But the third great junction is established as having a supremely pacified nature. // 27

6.s:
evaṃ baddhā śikhā yatra tattatphalaniyojikā /
ataḥ saṃvidi sarvo'yamadhvā viśramya tiṣṭhati // 28
6.d:
एवं बद्धा शिखा यत्र तत्तत्फलनियोजिका ।
अतः संविदि सर्वोऽयमध्वा विश्रम्य तिष्ठति ॥ 28
6.m: Thus the topknot is tied where it directs toward specific fruits. / Therefore, this whole path rests and remains in consciousness. // 28

6.s:
amūrtāyāḥ sarvagatvānniṣkriyāyāśca saṃvidaḥ /
mūrtikriyābhāsanaṃ yatsa evādhvā maheśituḥ // 29
6.d:
अमूर्तायाः सर्वगत्वान्निष्क्रियायाश्च संविदः ।
मूर्तिक्रियाभासनं यत्स एवाध्वा महेशितुः ॥ 29
6.m: For formless consciousness, being all-pervading and inactive, / the appearance of form and action is itself the Great Lord's path. // 29

6.s:
adhvā krameṇa yātavye pade saṃprāptikāraṇam /
dvaitināṃ bhogyabhāvāttu prabuddhānāṃ yato'dyate // 30
6.d:
अध्वा क्रमेण यातव्ये पदे संप्राप्तिकारणम् ।
द्वैतिनां भोग्यभावात्तु प्रबुद्धानां यतोऽद्यते ॥ 30
6.m: The path is the cause of attainment when the state to be reached is traversed by succession; / for dualists it arises as what is to be enjoyed, but for the awakened [it is otherwise]. // 30

6.s:
iha sarvatra śabdānāmanvarthaṃ carcayedyataḥ /
uktaṃ śrīmanniśācāre saṃjñātra trividhā matā // 31
6.d:
इह सर्वत्र शब्दानामन्वर्थं चर्चयेद्यतः ।
उक्तं श्रीमन्निशाचारे संज्ञात्र त्रिविधा मता ॥ 31
6.m: Here, in all cases, one should examine the etymological meaning of words; since / it is stated in the venerable Niśācāra: 'In this context, naming is considered threefold: // 31

6.s:
naimittikī prasiddhā ca tathānyā pāribhāṣikī /
pūrvatve vā pradhānaṃ syāttatrāntarbhāvayettataḥ // 32
6.d:
नैमित्तिकी प्रसिद्धा च तथान्या पारिभाषिकी ।
पूर्वत्वे वा प्रधानं स्यात्तत्रान्तर्भावयेत्ततः ॥ 32
6.m: causal, conventional, and another which is technical.' / Or, in its original state it may be primary; therefore one should subsume [the others] into that. // 32

6.s:
ato'dhvaśabdasyokteyaṃ niruktirnoditāpi cet /
kvacitsvabuddhyā sāpyūhyā kiyallekhyaṃ hi pustake // 33
6.d:
अतोऽध्वशब्दस्योक्तेयं निरुक्तिर्नोदितापि चेत् ।
क्वचित्स्वबुद्ध्या साप्यूह्या कियल्लेख्यं हि पुस्तके ॥ 33
6.m: Therefore this etymology of the word 'path' has been stated. Even if it is not stated / somewhere, it is to be inferred by one's own intellect; for how much can be written in a book? // 33

6.s:
tatra kriyābhāsanaṃ yatso'dhvā kālāhva ucyate /
varṇamantrapadābhikhyamatrāste'dhvatrayaṃ sphuṭam // 34
6.d:
तत्र क्रियाभासनं यत्सोऽध्वा कालाह्व उच्यते ।
वर्णमन्त्रपदाभिख्यमत्रास्तेऽध्वत्रयं स्फुटम् ॥ 34
6.m: Therein, the manifestation of action is called the path of time; / the triad of paths consisting of phoneme, mantra, and word clearly resides here. // 34

6.s:
yastu mūrtyavabhāsāṃśaḥ sa deśādhvā nigadyate /
kalātattvapurābhikhyamantarbhūtamiha trayam // 35
6.d:
यस्तु मूर्त्यवभासांशः स देशाध्वा निगद्यते ।
कलातत्त्वपुराभिख्यमन्तर्भूतमिह त्रयम् ॥ 35
6.m: That portion, however, which is the manifestation of form is called the path of space; / the triad known as kalā, tattva, and world is subsumed here. // 35

6.s:
trikadvaye'tra pratyekaṃ sthūlaṃ sūkṣmaṃ paraṃ vapuḥ /
yato'sti tena sarvo'yamadhvā ṣaḍvidha ucyate // 36
6.d:
त्रिकद्वयेऽत्र प्रत्येकं स्थूलं सूक्ष्मं परं वपुः ।
यतोऽस्ति तेन सर्वोऽयमध्वा षड्विध उच्यते ॥ 36
6.m: In each of these two triads there is a gross, a subtle, and a supreme form; / because this exists, this entire path is said to be sixfold. // 36

6.s:
ṣaḍvidhādadhvanaḥ prācyaṃ yadetattritayaṃ punaḥ /
eṣa eva sa kālādhvā prāṇe spaṣṭaṃ pratiṣṭhitaḥ // 37
6.d:
षड्विधादध्वनः प्राच्यं यदेतत्त्रितयं पुनः ।
एष एव स कालाध्वा प्राणे स्पष्टं प्रतिष्ठितः ॥ 37
6.m: Further, that former triad out of the sixfold path / is this very path of time, clearly established in the breath. // 37

6.s:
tattavamadhyasthitātkālādanyo'yaṃ kāla ucyate /
eṣa kālo hi devasya viśvābhāsanakāriṇī // 38
6.d:
तत्तवमध्यस्थितात्कालादन्योऽयं काल उच्यते ।
एष कालो हि देवस्य विश्वाभासनकारिणी ॥ 38
6.m: This is said to be a time different from the time that stands among the principles of existence; / for this time is the divine action power of the Lord // 38

6.s:
kriyāśaktiḥ samastānāṃ tattvānāṃ ca paraṃ vapuḥ /
etadīśvaratattvaṃ tacchivasya vapurucyate // 39
6.d:
क्रियाशक्तिः समस्तानां तत्त्वानां च परं वपुः ।
एतदीश्वरतत्त्वं तच्छिवस्य वपुरुच्यते ॥ 39
6.m: which brings about the manifestation of the universe, and the supreme body of all principles of existence. / This is the principle of Īśvara, and is called the body of Śiva, // 39

6.s:
udriktābhogakāryātmaviśvaikātmyamidaṃ yataḥ /
etadīśvararūpatvaṃ paramātmani yatkila // 40
6.d:
उद्रिक्ताभोगकार्यात्मविश्वैकात्म्यमिदं यतः ।
एतदीश्वररूपत्वं परमात्मनि यत्किल ॥ 40
6.m: since it is the identity with the universe consisting of effects in their full expanse. / That very state of being Īśvara, which belongs indeed to the supreme Self, // 40

6.s:
tatpramātari māyīye kālatattvaṃ nigadyate /
śivādiśuddhavidyāntaṃ yacchivasya svakaṃ vapuḥ // 41
6.d:
तत्प्रमातरि मायीये कालतत्त्वं निगद्यते ।
शिवादिशुद्धविद्यान्तं यच्छिवस्य स्वकं वपुः ॥ 41
6.m: is declared to be the principle of time in the subject subject to māyā. / What is Śiva's own body, ending with pure vidyā and beginning with Śiva, // 41

6.s:
tadeva puṃso māyādirāgāntaṃ kañcukībhavet /
anāśritaṃ yato māyā kalāvidye sadāśivaḥ // 42
6.d:
तदेव पुंसो मायादिरागान्तं कञ्चुकीभवेत् ।
अनाश्रितं यतो माया कलाविद्ये सदाशिवः ॥ 42
6.m: that very [body] becomes the cuirasses of the person, ending with attachment and beginning with māyā. / For Anāśrita is māyā, Sadāśiva is kalā and vidyā, // 42

6.s:
īśvaraḥ kālaniyatī sadvidyā rāga ucyate /
anāśritaḥ śūnyamātā buddhimātā sadāśivaḥ // 43
6.d:
ईश्वरः कालनियती सद्विद्या राग उच्यते ।
अनाश्रितः शून्यमाता बुद्धिमाता सदाशिवः ॥ 43
6.m: Īśvara is time and necessity, and Sadvidyā is said to be attachment. / Anāśrita is the knower of the void, Sadāśiva is the knower of the intellect, // 43

6.s:
īśvaraḥ prāṇamātā ca vidyā dehapramātṛtā /
anāśrayo hi śūnyatvaṃ jñānameva hi buddhitā // 44
6.d:
ईश्वरः प्राणमाता च विद्या देहप्रमातृता ।
अनाश्रयो हि शून्यत्वं ज्ञानमेव हि बुद्धिता ॥ 44
6.m: Īśvara is the knower of breath, and vidyā is the state of being a knower identified with the body. / For the void is indeed being without support, and the intellect is knowledge itself; // 44

6.s:
viśvātmatā ca prāṇatvaṃ dehe vedyaikatānatā /
tena prāṇapathe viśvākalaneyaṃ virājate // 45
6.d:
विश्वात्मता च प्राणत्वं देहे वेद्यैकतानता ।
तेन प्राणपथे विश्वाकलनेयं विराजते ॥ 45
6.m: breath is being the soul of the universe, and in the body there is absorption exclusively in the object of knowledge. / Therefore, this reckonable manifold of the universe shines forth in the movement of breath. // 45

6.s:
yena rūpeṇa tadvacmaḥ sadbhistadavadhīyatām /
dvādaśāntāvadhāvasmindehe yadyapi sarvataḥ // 46
6.d:
येन रूपेण तद्वच्मः सद्भिस्तदवधीयताम् ।
द्वादशान्तावधावस्मिन्देहे यद्यपि सर्वतः ॥ 46
6.m: We describe the manner in which this occurs; let it be carefully observed by the wise. / Although in this body, up to the limit of the dvādaśānta, everywhere // 46

6.s:
otaprotātmakaḥ prāṇastathāpītthaṃ na susphuṭaḥ /
yatno jīvanamātrātmā tatparaśca dvidhā mataḥ // 47
6.d:
ओतप्रोतात्मकः प्राणस्तथापीत्थं न सुस्फुटः ।
यत्नो जीवनमात्रात्मा तत्परश्च द्विधा मतः ॥ 47
6.m: breath is warp and woof, it is nonetheless not completely distinct in this way. / Effort is considered twofold: that which consists of mere living, and that which is beyond it. // 47

6.s:
saṃvedyaścāpyasaṃvedyo dvidhetthaṃ bhidyate punaḥ /
sphuṭāsphuṭatvāddvaividhyaṃ pratyekaṃ paribhāvayet // 48
6.d:
संवेद्यश्चाप्यसंवेद्यो द्विधेत्थं भिद्यते पुनः ।
स्फुटास्फुटत्वाद्द्वैविध्यं प्रत्येकं परिभावयेत् ॥ 48
6.m: It is divided again twofold into what can be experienced and what cannot be experienced; / one should consider each as two on account of being distinct or indistinct. // 48

6.s:
saṃvedyajīvanābhikhyaprayatnaspandasundaraḥ /
prāṇaḥ kandātprabhṛtyeva tathāpyatra na susphuṭaḥ // 49
6.d:
संवेद्यजीवनाभिख्यप्रयत्नस्पन्दसुन्दरः ।
प्राणः कन्दात्प्रभृत्येव तथाप्यत्र न सुस्फुटः ॥ 49
6.m: Breath, delightful through the vibration of effort known as perceptible life, / moves starting from the bulb itself; nevertheless, it is not completely distinct here. // 28

6.s:
kandādhārātprabhṛtyeva vyavasthā tena kathyate /
svacchandaśāstre nāḍīnāṃ vāyvādhāratayā sphuṭam // 50
6.d:
कन्दाधारात्प्रभृत्येव व्यवस्था तेन कथ्यते ।
स्वच्छन्दशास्त्रे नाडीनां वाय्वाधारतया स्फुटम् ॥ 50
6.m: For that reason, the arrangement of the channels is clearly explained / in the Svacchandatantra beginning from the support of the bulb, since they are supports for the wind. // 50

6.s:
tatrāpi tu prayatno'sau na saṃvedyatayā sthitaḥ /
vedyayatnāttu hṛdayātprāṇacāro vibhajyate // 51
6.d:
तत्रापि तु प्रयत्नोऽसौ न संवेद्यतया स्थितः ।
वेद्ययत्नात्तु हृदयात्प्राणचारो विभज्यते ॥ 51
6.m: Even there, however, that effort does not remain in an experienced state. / But from the heart, where effort is experienced, the course of the breath is differentiated. // 51

6.s:
prabhoḥ śivasya yā śaktirvāmā jyeṣṭhā ca raudrikā /
satadanyatamāvātmaprāṇau yatnavidhāyinau // 52
6.d:
प्रभोः शिवस्य या शक्तिर्वामा ज्येष्ठा च रौद्रिका ।
सतदन्यतमावात्मप्राणौ यत्नविधायिनौ ॥ 52
6.m: The powers of the sovereign Lord Śiva which are Vāmā, Jyeṣṭhā, and Raudrī / are those very powers which perform the effort, or other ones, as self and breath. // 52

6.s:
prabhuśaktiḥ kvacinmukhyā yathāṅgamarudīraṇe /
ātmaśaktiḥ kvacitkandasaṃkocaspandane yathā // 53
6.d:
प्रभुशक्तिः क्वचिन्मुख्या यथाङ्गमरुदीरणे ।
आत्मशक्तिः क्वचित्कन्दसंकोचस्पन्दने यथा ॥ 53
6.m: The sovereign power is primary in some contexts, as in the impelling of the bodily winds; / the self-power is primary in some, as in the pulsating contraction of the bulb; // 53

6.s:
prāṇaśaktiḥ kvacitprāṇacāre hārde yathā sphuṭam /
trayaṃ dvayaṃ vā mukhyaṃ syādyogināmavadhāninām // 54
6.d:
प्राणशक्तिः क्वचित्प्राणचारे हार्दे यथा स्फुटम् ।
त्रयं द्वयं वा मुख्यं स्याद्योगिनामवधानिनाम् ॥ 54
6.m: and the breath-power is primary in some, as clearly in the cardiac movement of the breath. / For attentive yogins, three or two might be primary. // 54

6.s:
avadhānādadṛṣṭāṃśādbalavattvādatheraṇāt /
viparyayo'pi prāṇātmaśaktīnāṃ mukhyatāṃ prati // 55
6.d:
अवधानाददृष्टांशाद्बलवत्त्वादथेरणात् ।
विपर्ययोऽपि प्राणात्मशक्तीनां मुख्यतां प्रति ॥ 55
6.m: On account of attention, of the unperceived portion, of strength, or again of impulsion, / there is also an inversion regarding the primacy of the powers of breath and self. // 55

6.s:
vāmā saṃsāriṇāmīśā prabhuśaktirvidhāyinī /
jyeṣṭhā tu suprabuddhānāṃ bubhutsūnāṃ ca raudrikā // 56
6.d:
वामा संसारिणामीशा प्रभुशक्तिर्विधायिनी ।
ज्येष्ठा तु सुप्रबुद्धानां बुभुत्सूनां च रौद्रिका ॥ 56
6.m: Vāmā is the sovereign, impelling power of transmigrating souls, / whereas Jyeṣṭhā belongs to the fully awakened, and Raudrī to those who desire to know. // 56

6.s:
vāmā saṃsāravamanā jyeṣṭhā śivamayī yataḥ /
drāvayitrī rujāṃ raudrī roddhrī cākhilakarmaṇām // 57
6.d:
वामा संसारवमना ज्येष्ठा शिवमयी यतः ।
द्रावयित्री रुजां रौद्री रोद्ध्री चाखिलकर्मणाम् ॥ 57
6.m: For Vāmā vomits forth worldly existence, Jyeṣṭhā is composed of Śiva, / and Raudrī melts away afflictions and obstructs all actions. // 57

6.s:
sṛṣṭyāditattvamajñātvā na mukto nāpi mocayet /
uktaṃ ca śrīyogacāre mokṣaḥ sarvaprakāśanāt // 58
6.d:
सृष्ट्यादितत्त्वमज्ञात्वा न मुक्तो नापि मोचयेत् ।
उक्तं च श्रीयोगचारे मोक्षः सर्वप्रकाशनात् ॥ 58
6.m: Without knowing the reality of emanation and the rest, one is not liberated, nor can one liberate others. / And it is said in the venerable Yogacāra: 'Liberation comes from illuminating all things.' // 58

6.s:
utpattisthitisaṃhārān ye na jānanti yoginaḥ /
na muktāste tadajñānabandhanaikādhivāsitāḥ // 59
6.d:
उत्पत्तिस्थितिसंहारान् ये न जानन्ति योगिनः ।
न मुक्तास्ते तदज्ञानबन्धनैकाधिवासिताः ॥ 59
6.m: Yogins who do not understand emanation, stasis, and reabsorption / are not liberated; they are steeped solely in the bondage of ignorance concerning that. // 59

6.s:
sṛṣṭyādayaśca te sarve kālādhīnā na saṃśayaḥ /
sa ca prāṇātmakastasmāduccāraḥ kathyate sphuṭaḥ // 60
6.d:
सृष्ट्यादयश्च ते सर्वे कालाधीना न संशयः ।
स च प्राणात्मकस्तस्मादुच्चारः कथ्यते स्फुटः ॥ 60
6.m: And all those—emanation and the rest—undoubtedly depend on time; / and that [time] consists of breath; therefore its distinct articulation is taught. // 60

6.s:
hṛdayātprāṇacāraśca nāsikyadvādaśāntataḥ /
ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgulo jantoḥ sarvasya svāṅgulakramāt // 61
6.d:
हृदयात्प्राणचारश्च नासिक्यद्वादशान्ततः ।
षट्त्रिंशदङ्गुलो जन्तोः सर्वस्य स्वाङ्गुलक्रमात् ॥ 61
6.m: And the course of the breath from the heart up to the nasal dvādaśānta / measures thirty-six finger-breadths for every living being, by the standard of their own finger-breadth. // 61

6.s:
kṣodiṣṭhe vā mahiṣṭhe vā dehe tādṛśa eva hi /
vīryamojo balaṃ spandaḥ prāṇacāraḥ samaṃ tataḥ // 62
6.d:
क्षोदिष्ठे वा महिष्ठे वा देहे तादृश एव हि ।
वीर्यमोजो बलं स्पन्दः प्राणचारः समं ततः ॥ 62
6.m: In a body smallest or largest it is just the same; / hence virility, vigor, strength, vibration, and the course of the breath are equal. // 62

6.s:
ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgule cāre yadgamāgamayugmakam /
nālikātithimāsābdatatsaṅghro'tra sphuṭaṃ sthitaḥ // 63
6.d:
षट्त्रिंशदङ्गुले चारे यद्गमागमयुग्मकम् ।
नालिकातिथिमासाब्दतत्सङ्घ्रोऽत्र स्फुटं स्थितः ॥ 63
6.m: In the movement across thirty-six finger-breadths, which constitutes the pair of going out and coming in, / the collection of hours, lunar days, months, and years clearly resides here. // 63

6.s:
tuṭiḥ sapādāṅgulayukprāṇastāḥ ṣoḍaśocchvasan /
niḥśvasaṃścātra caṣakaḥ sapañcāṃśe'ṅgule'ṅgule // 64
6.d:
तुटिः सपादाङ्गुलयुक्प्राणस्ताः षोडशोच्छ्वसन् ।
निःश्वसंश्चात्र चषकः सपञ्चांशेऽङ्गुलेऽङ्गुले ॥ 64
6.m: A tuṭi is a breath measuring one and a quarter finger-breadths; inhaling and / exhaling sixteen of them, a measure of time called caṣaka occurs here at every finger-breadth and a fifth. // 64

6.s:
śvāsapraśvāsayornālī proktāhorātra ucyate /
navāṅgulāmbudhituṭau praharāste'bdhayo dinam // 65
6.d:
श्वासप्रश्वासयोर्नाली प्रोक्ताहोरात्र उच्यते ।
नवाङ्गुलाम्बुधितुटौ प्रहरास्तेऽब्धयो दिनम् ॥ 65
6.m: The nālī of an inhalation and exhalation is taught, and the day and night is declared: / in nine finger-breadths, an ocean of tuṭis [four], there are the watches; four of them make a day. // 65

6.s:
nirgame'ntarniśenendū tayoḥ saṃdhye tuṭerdale /
ketuḥ sūrye vidhau rāhurbhaumādervārabhāginaḥ // 66
6.d:
निर्गमेऽन्तर्निशेनेन्दू तयोः संध्ये तुटेर्दले ।
केतुः सूर्ये विधौ राहुर्भौमादेर्वारभागिनः ॥ 66
6.m: In the outgoing and inward [breath] are the sun and moon; the two junctions are in half a tuṭi; / Ketu is in the sun, Rāhu in the moon; the shares of the weekdays of Mars and the others // 66

6.s:
praharadvayamanyeṣāṃ grahāṇāmudayo'ntarā /
siddhirdavīyasī mokṣo'bhicāraḥ pāralaukikī // 67
6.d:
प्रहरद्वयमन्येषां ग्रहाणामुदयोऽन्तरा ।
सिद्धिर्दवीयसी मोक्षोऽभिचारः पारलौकिकी ॥ 67
6.m: last two watches, and the rising of other planets is in between. / Spiritual accomplishment that is distant, liberation, sorcery, fruits pertaining to the other world, // 67

6.s:
aihikī dūranaikaṭyātiśayā praharāṣṭake /
madhyāhnamadhyaniśayorabhijinmokṣabhogadā // 68
6.d:
ऐहिकी दूरनैकट्यातिशया प्रहराष्टके ।
मध्याह्नमध्यनिशयोरभिजिन्मोक्षभोगदा ॥ 68
6.m: or mundane fruits characterized by extreme distance or proximity, occur in the eight watches; / at noon and midnight, Abhijit bestows liberation and enjoyment. // 68

6.s:
nakṣatrāṇāṃ tadanyeṣāmudayo madhyataḥ kramāt /
nāgā lokeśamūrtīśā gaṇeśā jalatattvataḥ // 69
6.d:
नक्षत्राणां तदन्येषामुदयो मध्यतः क्रमात् ।
नागा लोकेशमूर्तीशा गणेशा जलतत्त्वतः ॥ 69
6.m: The rising of the lunar mansions (nakṣatras) and the others occurs sequentially from the center: / the serpents, the lords of the worlds, the lords of the forms, the lords of the retinues, from the water principle onward, 69

6.s:
pradhānāntaṃ nāyakāśca vidyātattvādhināyakāḥ /
sakalādyāśca kaṇṭhyoṣṭhyaparyantā bhairavāstathā // 70
6.d:
प्रधानान्तं नायकाश्च विद्यातत्त्वाधिनायकाः ।
सकलाद्याश्च कण्ठ्योष्ठ्यपर्यन्ता भैरवास्तथा ॥ 70
6.m: and the lords up to the Pradhāna, the overlords of the Vidyā-principle, / and the Bhairavas beginning with Sakala and extending from the guttural to the labial sounds, 70

6.s:
śaktayaḥ pārameśvaryo vāmaśā vīranāyakāḥ /
aṣṭāvaṣṭau ye ya itthaṃ vyāpyavyāpakatājuṣaḥ // 71
6.d:
शक्तयः पारमेश्वर्यो वामशा वीरनायकाः ।
अष्टावष्टौ ये य इत्थं व्याप्यव्यापकताजुषः ॥ 71
6.m: and the sovereign powers of the Supreme Lord, the Vāmaśās, the hero-leaders— / each of these groups of eight, possessing pervaded-and-pervader relationship in this way, 71

6.s:
sthūlasūkṣmāḥ kramātteṣāmudayaḥ praharāṣṭake /
dine krūrāṇi saumyāni rātrau karmāṇyasaṃśayam // 72
6.d:
स्थूलसूक्ष्माः क्रमात्तेषामुदयः प्रहराष्टके ।
दिने क्रूराणि सौम्यानि रात्रौ कर्माण्यसंशयम् ॥ 72
6.m: gross and subtle sequentially, have their rising in the eight watches. / In the daytime, [one should perform] fierce acts, and at night, gentle ones without doubt. 72

6.s:
krūratā saumyatā vābhisandherapi nirūpitā /
dinarātrikṣaye muktiḥ sā vyāptidhyānayogataḥ // 73
6.d:
क्रूरता सौम्यता वाभिसन्धेरपि निरूपिता ।
दिनरात्रिक्षये मुक्तिः सा व्याप्तिध्यानयोगतः ॥ 73
6.m: Fierceness or gentleness is determined also by intention. / Liberation occurs at the dissolution of day and night through the yoga of meditative absorption in pervasion. 73

6.s:
te coktāḥ parameśena śrīmadvīrāvalīkule /
sitāsitau dīrghahrasvau dharmādharmau dinakṣape // 74
6.d:
ते चोक्ताः परमेशेन श्रीमद्वीरावलीकुले ।
सितासितौ दीर्घह्रस्वौ धर्माधर्मौ दिनक्षपे ॥ 74
6.m: And these are declared by the Supreme Lord in the glorious Vīrāvalīkula: / 'White and black, long and short, virtue and vice, day and night— 74

6.s:
kṣīyete yadi taddīkṣā vyāptyā dhyānena yogataḥ /
ahorātraḥ prāṇacāre kathito māsa ucyate // 75
6.d:
क्षीयेते यदि तद्दीक्षा व्याप्त्या ध्यानेन योगतः ।
अहोरात्रः प्राणचारे कथितो मास उच्यते ॥ 75
6.m: if both are dissolved, that is initiation through pervasion, meditation, and yoga.' / The day-and-night has been explained in the movement of the breath; [now] the month is described. 75

6.s:
dinaṃ kṛṣṇo niśā śuklaḥ pakṣau karmasu pūrvavat /
yāḥ ṣoḍaśoktāstithayastāsu ye pūrvapaścime // 76
6.d:
दिनं कृष्णो निशा शुक्लः पक्षौ कर्मसु पूर्ववत् ।
याः षोडशोक्तास्तिथयस्तासु ये पूर्वपश्चिमे ॥ 76
6.m: Day is the dark fortnight, night is the light fortnight, regarding rites as before. / Among the sixteen lunar days (tithis) that are spoken of, the two that are the first and the last— 76

6.s:
tayostu viśramo'rdhe'rdhe tithyaḥ pañcadaśetarāḥ /
sapāde dvyaṅgule tithyā ahorātro vibhajyate // 77
6.d:
तयोस्तु विश्रमोऽर्धेऽर्धे तिथ्यः पञ्चदशेतराः ।
सपादे द्व्यङ्गुले तिथ्या अहोरात्रो विभज्यते ॥ 77
6.m: the rest of these two is in each half; the other lunar days are fifteen. / By a lunar day of two fingers and a quarter, the day-and-night is divided. 77

6.s:
prakāśaviśramavaśāttāveva hi dinakṣape /
saṃvitpratikṣaṇaṃ yasmātprakāśānandayoginī // 78
6.d:
प्रकाशविश्रमवशात्तावेव हि दिनक्षपे ।
संवित्प्रतिक्षणं यस्मात्प्रकाशानन्दयोगिनी ॥ 78
6.m: By force of luminosity and rest, they are indeed day and night, / since consciousness at every moment is endowed with luminosity and bliss. 78

6.s:
tau klṛptau yāvati tayā tāvatyeva dinakṣape /
yāvatyeva hi saṃvittiruditoditasusphuṭā // 79
6.d:
तौ क्लृप्तौ यावति तया तावत्येव दिनक्षपे ।
यावत्येव हि संवित्तिरुदितोदितसुस्फुटा ॥ 79
6.m: In as much as they are arranged by it, for that long indeed are day and night. / For as long as consciousness has arisen and shines fully evident, 79

6.s:
tāvāneva kṣaṇaḥ kalpo nimeṣo vā tadastvapi /
yāvānevodayo vittervedyaikagrahatatparaḥ // 80
6.d:
तावानेव क्षणः कल्पो निमेषो वा तदस्त्वपि ।
यावानेवोदयो वित्तेर्वेद्यैकग्रहतत्परः ॥ 80
6.m: so long is an instant, a cosmic cycle, or a twinkling of an eye—let it be whatever. / As long as the rising of awareness is intent upon grasping only the knowable, 80

6.s:
tāvadevāstamayanaṃ veditṛsvātmacarvaṇam /
vedye ca bahirantarvā dvaye vātha dvayojjhite // 81
6.d:
तावदेवास्तमयनं वेदितृस्वात्मचर्वणम् ।
वेद्ये च बहिरन्तर्वा द्वये वाथ द्वयोज्झिते ॥ 81
6.m: so long is setting, the relish of the knower's own self. / And in the knowable, whether external or internal, or in the duality, or in that devoid of duality, 81

6.s:
sarvathā tanmayībhūtirdinaṃ vettṛsthatā niśā /
veditā vedyaviśrānto vettā tvantarmukhasthitiḥ // 82
6.d:
सर्वथा तन्मयीभूतिर्दिनं वेत्तृस्थता निशा ।
वेदिता वेद्यविश्रान्तो वेत्ता त्वन्तर्मुखस्थितिः ॥ 82
6.m: becoming identified with it in every way is day; remaining in the knower is night. / The knower [as subject-experiencer] rests in the knowable, but the true knower remains facing inward. 82

6.s:
purā vicārayanpaścātsattāmātrasvarūpakaḥ /
jāgradveditṛtā svapno vettṛbhāvaḥ purātanaḥ // 83
6.d:
पुरा विचारयन्पश्चात्सत्तामात्रस्वरूपकः ।
जाग्रद्वेदितृता स्वप्नो वेत्तृभावः पुरातनः ॥ 83
6.m: At first deliberating, afterward having the essential nature of pure existence: / waking is the state of the experiencer; dreaming is the former state of the knower; 83

6.s:
paraḥ suptaṃ kṣaye rātridinayosturyamadvayam /
kadācidvastuviśrāntisāmyenātmani carvaṇam // 84
6.d:
परः सुप्तं क्षये रात्रिदिनयोस्तुर्यमद्वयम् ।
कदाचिद्वस्तुविश्रान्तिसाम्येनात्मनि चर्वणम् ॥ 84
6.m: the higher is deep sleep; upon the dissolution of night and day, there is the fourth state free of duality. / Sometimes there is relishing in the self with equal resting in the object— 84

6.s:
vedyavedakasāmyaṃ tat sā rātridinatulyatā /
vedye viśrāntiradhikā dinadairghyāya tatra tu // 85
6.d:
वेद्यवेदकसाम्यं तत् सा रात्रिदिनतुल्यता ।
वेद्ये विश्रान्तिरधिका दिनदैर्घ्याय तत्र तु ॥ 85
6.m: that is the equality of known and knower; that is the equivalence of night and day. / But when rest in the knowable is greater, that makes for the length of the day; 85

6.s:
nyūnā syātsvātmaviśrāntirviparīte viparyayaḥ /
svātmautsukye prabuddhe hi vedyaviśrāntiralpikā // 86
6.d:
न्यूना स्यात्स्वात्मविश्रान्तिर्विपरीते विपर्ययः ।
स्वात्मौत्सुक्ये प्रबुद्धे हि वेद्यविश्रान्तिरल्पिका ॥ 86
6.m: rest in one's own self would then be lesser; when reversed, the opposite occurs. / For when eagerness for one's own self is awakened, rest in the knowable is meager. 86

6.s:
itthameva divārātrinyūnādhikyakramaṃ vadet /
yathā deheṣvahorātranyūnādhikyādi no samam // 87
6.d:
इत्थमेव दिवारात्रिन्यूनाधिक्यक्रमं वदेत् ।
यथा देहेष्वहोरात्रन्यूनाधिक्यादि नो समम् ॥ 87
6.m: In this very manner one should state the sequence of deficiency and excess of day and night. / Just as in bodies the deficiency and excess of day and night is not uniform, 87

6.s:
tathā pureṣvapītyevaṃ tadviśeṣeṇa noditam /
śrītraiyambakasantānavitatāmbarabhāskaraḥ // 88
6.d:
तथा पुरेष्वपीत्येवं तद्विशेषेण नोदितम् ।
श्रीत्रैयम्बकसन्तानवितताम्बरभास्करः ॥ 88
6.m: so also in cities; thus it has not been declared with particularity. / The sun in the vast sky of the glorious Traiyambaka lineage, 88

6.s:
dinarātrikramaṃ me śrīśaṃbhuritthamapaprathat /
śrīsantānagurustvāha sthānaṃ buddhāprabuddhayoḥ // 89
6.d:
दिनरात्रिक्रमं मे श्रीशंभुरित्थमपप्रथत् ।
श्रीसन्तानगुरुस्त्वाह स्थानं बुद्धाप्रबुद्धयोः ॥ 89
6.m: the illustrious Sambhunātha, explained to me this sequence of day and night. / But the guru of the illustrious lineage taught the locus of the awakened and unawakened: 89

6.s:
hṛda ārabhya yattena rātrindivavibhājanam /
tadasatsitapakṣe'ntaḥ praveśollāsabhāgini // 90
6.d:
हृद आरभ्य यत्तेन रात्रिन्दिवविभाजनम् ।
तदसत्सितपक्षेऽन्तः प्रवेशोल्लासभागिनि ॥ 90
6.m: because the division of night and day begins from the heart, / that is incorrect, for in the bright fortnight, which partakes of inner entry and emergence, 90

6.s:
abuddhasthānamevaitaddinatvena kathaṃ bhavet /
alaṃ vānena nedaṃ vā mama prāṅmatamatsaraḥ // 91
6.d:
अबुद्धस्थानमेवैतद्दिनत्वेन कथं भवेत् ।
अलं वानेन नेदं वा मम प्राङ्मतमत्सरः ॥ 91
6.m: how could this place of the unawakened be the day? / But enough of this; it is not that I harbor malice toward an earlier doctrine, 91

6.s:
heye tu darśite śiṣyāḥ satpathaikāntadarśinaḥ /
vyākhyātaḥ kṛṣṇapakṣo ya statra prāṇagataḥ śaśī // 92
6.d:
हेये तु दर्शिते शिष्याः सत्पथैकान्तदर्शिनः ।
व्याख्यातः कृष्णपक्षो य स्तत्र प्राणगतः शशी ॥ 92
6.m: but when what is to be discarded is pointed out, disciples see solely the true path. / The dark fortnight that has been explained—there, the moon located in the outgoing breath 92

6.s:
āpyāyanātmanaikaikāṃ kalāṃ pratitithi tyajet /
dvādaśāntasamīpe tu yāsau pañcadaśī tuṭiḥ // 93
6.d:
आप्यायनात्मनैकैकां कलां प्रतितिथि त्यजेत् ।
द्वादशान्तसमीपे तु यासौ पञ्चदशी तुटिः ॥ 93
6.m: leaves, on every lunar day, one digital division (kalā) that consists of nourishing nectar. / Now, near the twelve-finger limit, there is that fifteenth tuṭi: 93

6.s:
sāmāvasyātra sa kṣīṇaścandraḥ prāṇārkamāviśet /
uktaṃ śrīkāmikāyāṃ ca nordhve'dhaḥ prakṛtiḥ parā /
ardhārdhe kramate māyā dvikhaṇḍā śivarūpiṇī // 94
6.d:
सामावस्यात्र स क्षीणश्चन्द्रः प्राणार्कमाविशेत् ।
उक्तं श्रीकामिकायां च नोर्ध्वेऽधः प्रकृतिः परा ।
अर्धार्धे क्रमते माया द्विखण्डा शिवरूपिणी ॥ 94
6.m: that is the new moon; here, that depleted moon enters the breath-sun. / And it is said in the venerable Kāmikā: 'Not above, not below is the supreme Prakṛti; / in each half Māyā moves, divided in two, having the form of Śiva. 94

6.s:
candrasūryātmanā dehaṃ pūrayetpravilāpayet /
amṛtaṃ candrarūpeṇa dvidhā ṣoḍaśadhā punaḥ // 95
6.d:
चन्द्रसूर्यात्मना देहं पूरयेत्प्रविलापयेत् ।
अमृतं चन्द्ररूपेण द्विधा षोडशधा पुनः ॥ 95
6.m: One should fill and dissolve the body by means of the moon and the sun. / The nectar is twofold in the form of the moon, and again sixteenfold. 95

6.s:
pivanti ca surāḥ sarve daśapañca parāḥ kalāḥ /
amā śeṣaguhāntaḥsthāmāvāsyā viśvatarpiṇī // 96
6.d:
पिवन्ति च सुराः सर्वे दशपञ्च पराः कलाः ।
अमा शेषगुहान्तःस्थामावास्या विश्वतर्पिणी ॥ 96
6.m: And all the gods drink fifteen supreme digits; / the new-moon digit (amā), residing inside the cave of the remainder, is the new moon that satisfies the universe.' 96

6.s:
evaṃ kalāḥ pañcadaśa kṣīyante śaśinaḥ kramāt /
āpyāyinyamṛtābrūpatādātmyātṣoḍaśī na tu // 97
6.d:
एवं कलाः पञ्चदश क्षीयन्ते शशिनः क्रमात् ।
आप्यायिन्यमृताब्रूपतादात्म्यात्षोडशी न तु ॥ 97
6.m: In this way, the fifteen digits of the moon diminish gradually, / but not the sixteenth, because of its identity with the nourishing immortal waters. 97

6.s:
tatra pañcadaśī yāsau tuṭiḥ prakṣīṇacandramāḥ /
tadūrdhvagaṃ yattuṭyardhaṃ pakṣasaṃdhiḥ sa kīrtitaḥ // 98
6.d:
तत्र पञ्चदशी यासौ तुटिः प्रक्षीणचन्द्रमाः ।
तदूर्ध्वगं यत्तुट्यर्धं पक्षसंधिः स कीर्तितः ॥ 98
6.m: There, that fifteenth tuṭi in which the moon has waned— / the half-tuṭi that goes beyond it is called the junction of the fortnights. 98

6.s:
tasmādviśramatuṭyardhādāmāvasyaṃ purādalam /
paraṃ prātipadaṃ cārdhamiti saṃdhiḥ sa kalpyate // 99
6.d:
तस्माद्विश्रमतुट्यर्धादामावस्यं पुरादलम् ।
परं प्रातिपदं चार्धमिति संधिः स कल्प्यते ॥ 99
6.m: From that resting half-tuṭi, the first half belongs to the new moon / and the second half to the first lunar day; thus that junction is conceived. 99

6.s:
tatra prātipade tasmiṃstuṭyardhārdhe purādalam /
āmāvasyaṃ tithicchedātkuryātsūryagrahaṃ viśat // 100
6.d:
तत्र प्रातिपदे तस्मिंस्तुट्यर्धार्धे पुरादलम् ।
आमावस्यं तिथिच्छेदात्कुर्यात्सूर्यग्रहं विशत् ॥ 100
6.m: There, in that first lunar day, in the first half of that half-tuṭi, / the new moon, entering, causes a solar eclipse because of the intersection of lunar days. 100

6.s:
tatrārkamaṇḍale līnaḥ śaśī sravati yanmadhu /
taptatvāttatpibedindusahabhūḥ siṃhikāsutaḥ // 101
6.d:
तत्रार्कमण्डले लीनः शशी स्रवति यन्मधु ।
तप्तत्वात्तत्पिबेदिन्दुसहभूः सिंहिकासुतः ॥ 101
6.m: There, dissolved into the orb of the sun, the nectar that the moon pours out, / the son of Siṃhikā [Rāhu], co-arising with the moon, drinks because it is heated. 101

6.s:
arkaḥ pramāṇaṃ somastu meyaṃ jñānakriyātmakau /
rāhurmāyāpramātā syāttadācchādanakovidaḥ // 102
6.d:
अर्कः प्रमाणं सोमस्तु मेयं ज्ञानक्रियात्मकौ ।
राहुर्मायाप्रमाता स्यात्तदाच्छादनकोविदः ॥ 102
6.m: The sun is the means of knowledge (pramāṇa), and the moon is the object of knowledge (meya), consisting of knowledge and action. / Rāhu is the limited knower (māyāpramātṛ), skilled in concealing them. 102

6.s:
tata eva tamorūpo vilāpayitumakṣamaḥ /
tatsaṃghaṭṭādvayollāso mukhyo mātā vilāpakaḥ // 103
6.d:
तत एव तमोरूपो विलापयितुमक्षमः ।
तत्संघट्टाद्वयोल्लासो मुख्यो माता विलापकः ॥ 103
6.m: Therefore, having the nature of darkness, he is unable to dissolve them; / the flashing forth of the non-dual from their collision is the principal knower, the dissolver. 103

6.s:
arkendurāhusaṃghaṭṭāt pramāṇaṃ vedyavedakau /
advayena tatastena puṇya eṣa mahāgrahaḥ // 104
6.d:
अर्केन्दुराहुसंघट्टात् प्रमाणं वेद्यवेदकौ ।
अद्वयेन ततस्तेन पुण्य एष महाग्रहः ॥ 104
6.m: From the conjunction of sun, moon, and Rāhu, the means of knowledge and the known and knower / are therefore unified through non-duality; this is an auspicious great eclipse. 104

6.s:
amāvasyāṃ vināpyeṣa saṃghaṭṭaścenmahāgrahaḥ /
yathārke meṣage rāhāvaśvinīsthe'śvinīdine // 105
6.d:
अमावस्यां विनाप्येष संघट्टश्चेन्महाग्रहः ।
यथार्के मेषगे राहावश्विनीस्थेऽश्विनीदिने ॥ 105
6.m: Even without the new moon, if this conjunction takes place, it is a great eclipse, / as when the sun is in Aries, Rāhu is in Aśvinī, on the day of Aśvinī. 105

6.s:
āmāvāsyaṃ yadā tvardhaṃ līnaṃ prātipade dale /
pratipacca viśuddhā syāttanmokṣo dūrage vidhau // 106
6.d:
आमावास्यं यदा त्वर्धं लीनं प्रातिपदे दले ।
प्रतिपच्च विशुद्धा स्यात्तन्मोक्षो दूरगे विधौ ॥ 106
6.m: When, however, the new-moon half is merged into the first lunar day's segment, / and the first lunar day is purified, then there is release when the moon is far away. 106

6.s:
grāsamokṣāntare snānadhyānahomajapādikam /
laukikālaukikaṃ bhūyaḥphalaṃ syātpāralaukikam // 107
6.d:
ग्रासमोक्षान्तरे स्नानध्यानहोमजपादिकम् ।
लौकिकालौकिकं भूयःफलं स्यात्पारलौकिकम् ॥ 107
6.m: Between the seizure and release, bathing, meditation, fire sacrifice, recitation, and so forth / yield abundant fruit, mundane, extra-mundane, and related to the next world. 107

6.s:
grāsyagrāsakatākṣobhaprakṣaye kṣaṇamāviśan /
mokṣabhāgdhyānapūjādi kurvaṃścandrārkayorgrahe // 108
6.d:
ग्रास्यग्रासकताक्षोभप्रक्षये क्षणमाविशन् ।
मोक्षभाग्ध्यानपूजादि कुर्वंश्चन्द्रार्कयोर्ग्रहे ॥ 108
6.m: Entering for a moment into the cessation of the agitation between seized and seizer, / one attains liberation while performing meditation, worship, and so on during the eclipse of the moon and sun. 108

6.s:
tithiccheda ṛṇaṃ kāso vṛddhirniḥśvasanaṃ dhanam /
ayatnajaṃ yatnajaṃ tu recanādatha rodhanāt // 109
6.d:
तिथिच्छेद ऋणं कासो वृद्धिर्निःश्वसनं धनम् ।
अयत्नजं यत्नजं तु रेचनादथ रोधनात् ॥ 109
6.m: The cutting of a lunar day is a debt, a cough; its increase is an expiration, a wealth; / [this is] effortless, but that produced by effort arises from exhalation and retention. 109

6.s:
evaṃ prāṇe viśati citsūrya induṃ sudhāmayam /
ekaikadhyena bodhāṃśu kalayā paripūrayet // 110
6.d:
एवं प्राणे विशति चित्सूर्य इन्दुं सुधामयम् ।
एकैकध्येन बोधांशु कलया परिपूरयेत् ॥ 110
6.m: In this way, when the breath enters, the sun of consciousness / fills the nectar-filled moon by means of a single ray of awareness, digit by digit. 110

6.s:
kramasaṃpūraṇāśāliśaśāṅkāmṛtasundarāḥ /
tuṭyaḥ pañcadaśaitāḥ syustithayaḥ sitapakṣagāḥ // 111
6.d:
क्रमसंपूरणाशालिशशाङ्कामृतसुन्दराः ।
तुट्यः पञ्चदशैताः स्युस्तिथयः सितपक्षगाः ॥ 111
6.m: Resplendent with the moon's nectar that is full of gradual replenishment, / these fifteen tuṭis are the lunar days belonging to the bright fortnight. 111

6.s:
antyāyāṃ pūrṇamastuṭyāṃ pūrvavatpakṣasandhitā /
indugrahaśca pratipatsandhau pūrvapraveśataḥ // 112
6.d:
अन्त्यायां पूर्णमस्तुट्यां पूर्ववत्पक्षसन्धिता ।
इन्दुग्रहश्च प्रतिपत्सन्धौ पूर्वप्रवेशतः ॥ 112
6.m: In the final tuṭi of the full moon, as before, there is the junction of the fortnights, / and a lunar eclipse occurs at the junction of the first lunar day due to the prior entry. 112

6.s:
aihikaṃ grahaṇe cātra sādhakānāṃ mahāphalam /
prāgvadanyadayaṃ māsaḥ prāṇacāre'bda ucyate // 113
6.d:
ऐहिकं ग्रहणे चात्र साधकानां महाफलम् ।
प्राग्वदन्यदयं मासः प्राणचारेऽब्द उच्यते ॥ 113
6.m: And during this eclipse, there is great mundane fruit for adepts; / the rest is as before. This month is described in the movement of breath; [now] the year [is explained]. 113

6.s:
ṣaṭsu ṣaṭsvaṅguleṣvarko hṛdayānmakarādiṣu /
tiṣṭhanmāghāḍhikaṃ ṣaṭkaṃ kuryāttaccottarāyaṇam // 114
6.d:
षट्सु षट्स्वङ्गुलेष्वर्को हृदयान्मकरादिषु ।
तिष्ठन्माघाढिकं षट्कं कुर्यात्तच्चोत्तरायणम् ॥ 114
6.m: At intervals of six fingers from the heart, the sun, staying in Capricorn and the rest, / makes the six months beginning with Māgha; and that is the northern solstice. 114

6.s:
saṃkrāntitritaye vṛtte bhukte cāṣṭādaśāṅgule /
meṣaṃ prāpte ravau puṇyaṃ viṣuvatpāralaukikam // 115
6.d:
संक्रान्तित्रितये वृत्ते भुक्ते चाष्टादशाङ्गुले ।
मेषं प्राप्ते रवौ पुण्यं विषुवत्पारलौकिकम् ॥ 115
6.m: When three transitions have elapsed and eighteen digits are traversed, / the sun reaches Aries; that meritorious equinox pertains to the hereafter.

6.s:
praveśe tu tulāsthe'rke tadeva viṣuvadbhavet /
iha siddhipradaṃ caitaddakṣiṇāyanagaṃ tataḥ // 116
6.d:
प्रवेशे तु तुलास्थेऽर्के तदेव विषुवद्भवेत् ।
इह सिद्धिप्रदं चैतद्दक्षिणायनगं ततः ॥ 116
6.m: On the incoming breath, however, when the sun is in Libra, that very [junction] is the equinox; / it grants spiritual accomplishment here in this world, and is henceforth in the southern course.

6.s:
garbhatā prodbubhūṣiṣyadbhāvaścāthodbubhūṣutā /
udbhaviṣyattvamudbhūtiprārambho'pyudbhavasthitiḥ // 117
6.d:
गर्भता प्रोद्बुभूषिष्यद्भावश्चाथोद्बुभूषुता ।
उद्भविष्यत्त्वमुद्भूतिप्रारम्भोऽप्युद्भवस्थितिः ॥ 117
6.m: State of being a womb, condition of having the will to emerge, and then eagerness to emerge; / futurity of emergence, commencement of emergence, and stability of emergence;

6.s:
janma sattā pariṇatirvṛddhirhrāsaḥ kṣayaḥ kramāt /
makarādīni tenātra kriyā sūte sadṛkphalam // 118
6.d:
जन्म सत्ता परिणतिर्वृद्धिर्ह्रासः क्षयः क्रमात् ।
मकरादीनि तेनात्र क्रिया सूते सदृक्फलम् ॥ 118
6.m: birth, existence, transformation, growth, decay, and destruction in succession: / these correspond to Capricorn and the subsequent [signs], and therefore action here yields a matching fruit.

6.s:
āmutrike jhaṣaḥ kumbho mantrādeḥ pūrvasevane /
catuṣkaṃ kila mīnādyamantikaṃ cottarottaram // 119
6.d:
आमुत्रिके झषः कुम्भो मन्त्रादेः पूर्वसेवने ।
चतुष्कं किल मीनाद्यमन्तिकं चोत्तरोत्तरम् ॥ 119
6.m: For otherworldly results, Capricorn and Aquarius [serve] for the preparatory practice of mantra and the like; / the tetrad beginning with Pisces is indeed close at hand and increasingly superior.

6.s:
praveśe khalu tatraiva śāntipuṣṭyādisundaram /
karma syādaihikaṃ tacca dūradūraphalaṃ kramāt // 120
6.d:
प्रवेशे खलु तत्रैव शान्तिपुष्ट्यादिसुन्दरम् ।
कर्म स्यादैहिकं तच्च दूरदूरफलं क्रमात् ॥ 120
6.m: During the incoming breath precisely there, action that is beneficial through pacification, nourishment, and so forth, / will pertain to this world, its fruit being increasingly distant in succession.

6.s:
nirgame dinavṛddhiḥ syādviparīte viparyayaḥ /
varṣe'smiṃstithayaḥ pañca pratyaṅgulamiti kramaḥ // 121
6.d:
निर्गमे दिनवृद्धिः स्याद्विपरीते विपर्ययः ।
वर्षेऽस्मिंस्तिथयः पञ्च प्रत्यङ्गुलमिति क्रमः ॥ 121
6.m: During the outgoing breath, there is the increase of the day; on the reverse, the opposite [occurs]. / In this year, there are five lunar days per digit: such is the order.

6.s:
tatrāpyahorātravidhiriti sarvaṃ hi pūrvavat /
prāṇīye varṣa etasminkārtikādiṣu dakṣataḥ // 122
6.d:
तत्राप्यहोरात्रविधिरिति सर्वं हि पूर्ववत् ।
प्राणीये वर्ष एतस्मिन्कार्तिकादिषु दक्षतः ॥ 122
6.m: There too, the rule of day and night applies; thus everything is just as before. / In this vital-breath year, beginning with Kārttika on the right,

6.s:
pitāmahāntaṃ rudrāḥ syurdvādaśāgre'tra bhāvinaḥ /
prāṇe varṣodayaḥ prokto dvādaśābdodayo'dhunā // 123
6.d:
पितामहान्तं रुद्राः स्युर्द्वादशाग्रेऽत्र भाविनः ।
प्राणे वर्षोदयः प्रोक्तो द्वादशाब्दोदयोऽधुना ॥ 123
6.m: there are the Rudras ending with Pitāmaha, who are to appear here at the end of twelve digits. / The rising of the year in the vital breath has been described; now that of twelve years is explained.

6.s:
kharasāstithya ekasminnekasminnaṅgule kramāt /
dvādaśābdodaye te ca caitrādyā dvādaśoditāḥ // 124
6.d:
खरसास्तिथ्य एकस्मिन्नेकस्मिन्नङ्गुले क्रमात् ।
द्वादशाब्दोदये ते च चैत्राद्या द्वादशोदिताः ॥ 124
6.m: There are sixty lunar days in each single digit in succession / in the rising of twelve years, and they are declared as the twelve beginning with Caitra.

6.s:
caitre mantroditiḥ so'pi tālunyukto'dhunā punaḥ /
hṛdi caitroditistena tatra mantrodayo'pi hi // 125
6.d:
चैत्रे मन्त्रोदितिः सोऽपि तालुन्युक्तोऽधुना पुनः ।
हृदि चैत्रोदितिस्तेन तत्र मन्त्रोदयोऽपि हि ॥ 125
6.m: The rising of the mantra takes place in Caitra, and that too was stated at the palate; now again, / the rising of Caitra is in the heart, and thus the rising of the mantra is also there.

6.s:
pratyaṅgulaṃ tithīnāṃ tu triśate parikalpite /
sapañcāṃśāṅgule'bdaḥ syātprāṇe ṣaṣṭyabdatā punaḥ // 126
6.d:
प्रत्यङ्गुलं तिथीनां तु त्रिशते परिकल्पिते ।
सपञ्चांशाङ्गुलेऽब्दः स्यात्प्राणे षष्ट्यब्दता पुनः ॥ 126
6.m: When three hundred [and sixty] lunar days are assigned to each digit, / a year occurs in a digit and one-fifth; then again, sixty years in the vital breath [are reckoned].

6.s:
śatāni ṣaṭ sahasrāṇi caikaviṃśatirityayam /
vibhāgaḥ prāṇagaḥ ṣaṣṭivarṣāhorātra ucyate // 127
6.d:
शतानि षट् सहस्राणि चैकविंशतिरित्ययम् ।
विभागः प्राणगः षष्टिवर्षाहोरात्र उच्यते ॥ 127
6.m: Twenty-one thousand and six hundred: / this division located in the vital breath is spoken of as a day and night of sixty years.

6.s:
praharāharniśāmāsaṛtvabdaraviṣaṣṭigaḥ /
yaśchedastatra yaḥ sandhiḥ sa puṇyo dhyānapūjane // 128
6.d:
प्रहराहर्निशामासऋत्वब्दरविषष्टिगः ।
यश्छेदस्तत्र यः सन्धिः स पुण्यो ध्यानपूजने ॥ 128
6.m: Any division occurring in watches, days, nights, months, seasons, years, and solar sixty-year cycles— / whatever junction is there, that is meritorious for meditation and worship.

6.s:
iti prāṇodaye yo'yaṃ kālaḥ śaktyekavigrahaḥ /
viśvātmāntaḥsthitastasya bāhye rūpaṃ nirūpyate // 129
6.d:
इति प्राणोदये योऽयं कालः शक्त्येकविग्रहः ।
विश्वात्मान्तःस्थितस्तस्य बाह्ये रूपं निरूप्यते ॥ 129
6.m: Thus, this time which consists solely of the power in the rising of the vital breath, / abiding internally as the universal self, its external form is now set forth.

6.s:
ṣaṭ prāṇāścaṣakasteṣāṃ ṣaṣṭirnālī ca tāstathā /
tithistattriṃśatā māsaste dvādaśa tu vatsaraḥ // 130
6.d:
षट् प्राणाश्चषकस्तेषां षष्टिर्नाली च तास्तथा ।
तिथिस्तत्त्रिंशता मासस्ते द्वादश तु वत्सरः ॥ 130
6.m: Six breaths make a caṣaka; sixty of them make a nālī; / thirty of those make a lunar day, thirty of those a month, and twelve of those a year.

6.s:
abdaṃ pitryastvahorātra udagdakṣiṇato'yanāt /
pitṝṇāṃ yatsvamānena varṣaṃ taddivyamucyate // 131
6.d:
अब्दं पित्र्यस्त्वहोरात्र उदग्दक्षिणतोऽयनात् ।
पितॄणां यत्स्वमानेन वर्षं तद्दिव्यमुच्यते ॥ 131
6.m: A year is a day and night of the ancestors, through the northern and southern solstices. / What is a year by the ancestors' own measure is spoken of as divine.

6.s:
ṣaṣṭyadhikaṃ ca triśataṃ varṣāṇāmatra mānuṣam /
tacca dvādaśabhirhatvā māsasaṃkhyātra labhyate // 132
6.d:
षष्ट्यधिकं च त्रिशतं वर्षाणामत्र मानुषम् ।
तच्च द्वादशभिर्हत्वा माससंख्यात्र लभ्यते ॥ 132
6.m: Three hundred and sixty human years here, / multiplied by twelve, yield the number of months.

6.s:
tāṃ punastriṃśatā hatvāhorātrakalpanā vadet /
hatvā tāṃ caikaviṃśatyā sahasraiḥ ṣaṭśatena ca // 133
6.d:
तां पुनस्त्रिंशता हत्वाहोरात्रकल्पना वदेत् ।
हत्वा तां चैकविंशत्या सहस्रैः षट्शतेन च ॥ 133
6.m: Multiplying that again by thirty, one may state the computation of days and nights; / and multiplying that by twenty-one thousand six hundred,

6.s:
prāṇasaṃkhyāṃ vadettatra ṣaṣṭyādyabdodayaṃ punaḥ /
uktaṃ ca gurubhiḥ śrīmadrauravādisvavṛttiṣu // 134
6.d:
प्राणसंख्यां वदेत्तत्र षष्ट्याद्यब्दोदयं पुनः ।
उक्तं च गुरुभिः श्रीमद्रौरवादिस्ववृत्तिषु ॥ 134
6.m: one may state the number of vital breaths. The rising of sixty and other years there / has also been spoken by the gurus in their commentaries on the venerable Raurava and other works:

6.s:
devānāṃ yadahorātraṃ mānuṣāṇāṃ sa hāyanaḥ /
śatatrayeṇa ṣaṣṭyā ca nṝṇāṃ vibudhavatsaraḥ // 135
6.d:
देवानां यदहोरात्रं मानुषाणां स हायनः ।
शतत्रयेण षष्ट्या च नॄणां विबुधवत्सरः ॥ 135
6.m: “What is a day and night of the gods is a year of human beings; / by three hundred and sixty [human years] there is a year of the gods.”

6.s:
śrīmatsvacchandaśāstre ca tadeva matamīkṣyate /
pitṝṇāṃ tadahorātramityupakramya pṛṣṭhataḥ // 136
6.d:
श्रीमत्स्वच्छन्दशास्त्रे च तदेव मतमीक्ष्यते ।
पितॄणां तदहोरात्रमित्युपक्रम्य पृष्ठतः ॥ 136
6.m: In the venerable Svacchandaśāstra too, that very view is seen: / having commenced with “that day and night of the ancestors,” subsequently,

6.s:
evaṃ daivastvahorātra iti hyaikyopasaṃhṛtiḥ /
tena ye guravaḥ śrīmatsvacchandoktidvayāditaḥ // 137
6.d:
एवं दैवस्त्वहोरात्र इति ह्यैक्योपसंहृतिः ।
तेन ये गुरवः श्रीमत्स्वच्छन्दोक्तिद्वयादितः ॥ 137
6.m: there is the concluding integration: “such indeed is a divine day and night.” / Therefore, those gurus who, on the basis of two passages of the venerable Svacchanda and the like,

6.s:
pitryaṃ varṣaṃ divyadinamūcurbhrāntā hi te mudhā /
divyārkābdasahasrāṇi yugeṣu caturāditaḥ // 138
6.d:
पित्र्यं वर्षं दिव्यदिनमूचुर्भ्रान्ता हि ते मुधा ।
दिव्यार्काब्दसहस्राणि युगेषु चतुरादितः ॥ 138
6.m: claimed that an ancestral year is a divine day, were indeed wandering in error in vain. / Divine solar years in thousands in the four yugas, beginning with four,

6.s:
ekaikahānyā tāvadbhiḥ śataisteṣvaṣṭa saṃdhayaḥ /
caturyugaikasaptatyā manvantaste caturdaśa // 139
6.d:
एकैकहान्या तावद्भिः शतैस्तेष्वष्ट संधयः ।
चतुर्युगैकसप्तत्या मन्वन्तस्ते चतुर्दश ॥ 139
6.m: diminishing by one each, along with that many hundreds, have eight twilight junctions in them. / By seventy-one four-yuga cycles there is a period of a Manu; of these there are fourteen.

6.s:
brahmaṇo'hastatra cendrāḥ kramādyānti caturdaśa /
brahmāho'nte kālavahnerjvālā yojanalakṣiṇī // 140
6.d:
ब्रह्मणोऽहस्तत्र चेन्द्राः क्रमाद्यान्ति चतुर्दश ।
ब्रह्माहोऽन्ते कालवह्नेर्ज्वाला योजनलक्षिणी ॥ 140
6.m: That is a day of Brahmā, and therein fourteen Indras pass away in succession. / At the end of Brahmā's day, the flame of the fire of time, measuring a hundred thousand leagues,

6.s:
dagdhvā lokatrayaṃ dhūmāttvanyatprasvāpayettrayam /
nirayebhyaḥ purā kālavahnervyaktiryatastataḥ // 141
6.d:
दग्ध्वा लोकत्रयं धूमात्त्वन्यत्प्रस्वापयेत्त्रयम् ।
निरयेभ्यः पुरा कालवह्नेर्व्यक्तिर्यतस्ततः ॥ 141
6.m: burns the three worlds and causes another triad to fall asleep through smoke. / Because the appearance of the fire of time occurs previously from the hells,

6.s:
vibhuradhaḥsthito'pīśa iti śrīrauravaṃ matam /
brahmaniḥśvāsanirdhūte bhasmani svedavāriṇā // 142
6.d:
विभुरधःस्थितोऽपीश इति श्रीरौरवं मतम् ।
ब्रह्मनिःश्वासनिर्धूते भस्मनि स्वेदवारिणा ॥ 142
6.m: the all-pervading Lord is the master even though situated below: such is the view of the venerable Raurava. / In the ashes blown away by Brahmā's expiration, the universe,

6.s:
tadīyenāplutaṃ viśvaṃ tiṣṭhettāvanniśāgame /
tasminniśāvadhau sarve pudgalāḥ sūkṣmadehagāḥ // 143
6.d:
तदीयेनाप्लुतं विश्वं तिष्ठेत्तावन्निशागमे ।
तस्मिन्निशावधौ सर्वे पुद्गलाः सूक्ष्मदेहगाः ॥ 143
6.m: inundated by his own water of sweat, remains for that long at the advent of night. / At that boundary of night, all embodied souls residing in the subtle body,

6.s:
agnivegeritā loke jane syurlayakevalāḥ /
kūṣmāṇḍahāṭakādyāstu krīḍanti mahadālaye // 144
6.d:
अग्निवेगेरिता लोके जने स्युर्लयकेवलाः ।
कूष्माण्डहाटकाद्यास्तु क्रीडन्ति महदालये ॥ 144
6.m: impelled by the force of fire, become dissolved solitaries in the Jana world; / whereas Kūṣmāṇḍa, Hāṭaka, and others sport in the realm of the Mahat.

6.s:
niśākṣaye punaḥ sṛṣṭiṃ kurute tāmasāditaḥ /
svakavarṣaśatānte'sya kṣayastadvaiṣṇavaṃ dinam // 145
6.d:
निशाक्षये पुनः सृष्टिं कुरुते तामसादितः ।
स्वकवर्षशतान्तेऽस्य क्षयस्तद्वैष्णवं दिनम् ॥ 145
6.m: At the expiration of the night, he performs creation again, beginning from the darkness. / At the end of his own hundred years comes his dissolution; that is a day of Viṣṇu,

6.s:
rātriśca tāvatītyevaṃ viṣṇurudraśatābhidhāḥ /
kramātsvasvaśatānteṣu naśyantyatrāṇḍalopataḥ // 146
6.d:
रात्रिश्च तावतीत्येवं विष्णुरुद्रशताभिधाः ।
क्रमात्स्वस्वशतान्तेषु नश्यन्त्यत्राण्डलोपतः ॥ 146
6.m: and the night is of equal length. In this manner, those named hundreds of Viṣṇus and Rudras / perish in succession at the end of their respective hundreds, through the dissolution of the Cosmic Egg.

6.s:
abādyavyaktatattvānteṣvitthaṃ varṣaśataṃ kramāt /
dinarātrivibhāgaḥ syāt svasvāyuḥśatamānataḥ // 147
6.d:
अबाद्यव्यक्ततत्त्वान्तेष्वित्थं वर्षशतं क्रमात् ।
दिनरात्रिविभागः स्यात् स्वस्वायुःशतमानतः ॥ 147
6.m: Thus, up to the end of the unmanifest tattva beginning with water, in succession, a century of years / constitutes the division of day and night according to the measure of a hundred of their own respective lifespans.

6.s:
brahmaṇaḥ pralayollāsasahasraistu rasāgnibhiḥ /
avyaktastheṣu rudreṣu dinaṃ rātriśca tāvatī // 148
6.d:
ब्रह्मणः प्रलयोल्लाससहस्रैस्तु रसाग्निभिः ।
अव्यक्तस्थेषु रुद्रेषु दिनं रात्रिश्च तावती ॥ 148
6.m: By thirty-six thousand dissolutions and manifestations of Brahmā, / there is a day for the Rudras residing in the unmanifest, and the night is of equal length.

6.s:
tadā śrīkaṇṭha eva syātsākṣātsaṃhārakṛtprabhuḥ /
sarve rudrāstathā mūle māyāgarbhādhikāriṇaḥ // 149
6.d:
तदा श्रीकण्ठ एव स्यात्साक्षात्संहारकृत्प्रभुः ।
सर्वे रुद्रास्तथा मूले मायागर्भाधिकारिणः ॥ 149
6.m: Then Śrīkaṇṭha alone is the sovereign who directly effects dissolution. / Likewise, all the Rudras at the root, who have jurisdiction within the womb of māyā,

6.s:
avyaktākhye hyāviriñcācchrīkaṇṭhena sahāsate /
nivṛttādhaḥsthakarmā hi brahmā tatrādhare dhiyaḥ // 150
6.d:
अव्यक्ताख्ये ह्याविरिञ्चाच्छ्रीकण्ठेन सहासते ।
निवृत्ताधःस्थकर्मा हि ब्रह्मा तत्राधरे धियः ॥ 150
6.m: dwell together with Śrīkaṇṭha in that which is called the unmanifest, up to the abode of Brahmā. / For Brahmā, whose work in the lower realms has ceased, remains there below with his mind,

6.s:
na bhoktā jño'dhikāre tu vṛtta eva śivībhavet /
sa eṣo'vāntaralayastatkṣaye sṛṣṭirucyate // 151
6.d:
न भोक्ता ज्ञोऽधिकारे तु वृत्त एव शिवीभवेत् ।
स एषोऽवान्तरलयस्तत्क्षये सृष्टिरुच्यते ॥ 151
6.m: not being an experiencer; when his tenure as an agent has elapsed, he becomes Śiva. / This is the intermediate dissolution; at its termination, creation is spoken of.

6.s:
sāṃkhyavedādisaṃsiddhāñchrīkaṇṭhastadaharmukhe /
sṛjatyeva punastena na samyaṅmuktirīdṛśī // 152
6.d:
सांख्यवेदादिसंसिद्धाञ्छ्रीकण्ठस्तदहर्मुखे ।
सृजत्येव पुनस्तेन न सम्यङ्मुक्तिरीदृशी ॥ 152
6.m: At the morning of that day, Śrīkaṇṭha certainly creates anew / those perfected in Sāṅkhya, Veda, and so forth; therefore, such is not complete liberation.

6.s:
pradhāne yadahorātraṃ tajjaṃ varṣaśataṃ vibhoḥ /
śrīkaṇṭhasyāyuretacca dinaṃ kañcukavāsinām // 153
6.d:
प्रधाने यदहोरात्रं तज्जं वर्षशतं विभोः ।
श्रीकण्ठस्यायुरेतच्च दिनं कञ्चुकवासिनाम् ॥ 153
6.m: What is a day and night in Pradhāna, a century of years arising from that / is the lifespan of the all-pervading Śrīkaṇṭha; and this is a day for the dwellers of the cuirass.

6.s:
tatkramānniyatiḥ kālo rāgo vidyā kaletyamī /
yāntyanyonyaṃ layaṃ teṣāmāyurgāhanikaṃ dinam // 154
6.d:
तत्क्रमान्नियतिः कालो रागो विद्या कलेत्यमी ।
यान्त्यन्योन्यं लयं तेषामायुर्गाहनिकं दिनम् ॥ 154
6.m: In that order, these—restriction, time, attachment, limited knowledge, and limited agency— / undergo dissolution mutually; their lifespan is a day of Gahaneśa.

6.s:
taddinaprakṣaye viśvaṃ māyāyāṃ pravilīyate /
kṣīṇāyāṃ niśi tāvatyāṃ gahaneśaḥ sṛjetpunaḥ // 155
6.d:
तद्दिनप्रक्षये विश्वं मायायां प्रविलीयते ।
क्षीणायां निशि तावत्यां गहनेशः सृजेत्पुनः ॥ 155
6.m: At the dissolution of that day, the universe dissolves into māyā. / When the night of equal length has expired, the Lord of Gahana creates anew.

6.s:
evamavyaktakālaṃ tu parārdhairdaśabhirjahi /
māyāhastāvatī rātrirbhavetpralaya eṣa saḥ // 156
6.d:
एवमव्यक्तकालं तु परार्धैर्दशभिर्जहि ।
मायाहस्तावती रात्रिर्भवेत्प्रलय एष सः ॥ 156
6.m: Thus, multiply the time of the unmanifest by ten parārdhas; / that is a day of māyā, and the night is of equal length: this is that dissolution.

6.s:
māyākālaṃ parārdhānāṃ guṇayitvā śatena tu /
aiśvaro divaso nādaḥ prāṇātmātra sṛjejjagat // 157
6.d:
मायाकालं परार्धानां गुणयित्वा शतेन तु ।
ऐश्वरो दिवसो नादः प्राणात्मात्र सृजेज्जगत् ॥ 157
6.m: Having multiplied the time of māyā by a hundred parārdhas, / there is a day of Īśvara; here the phonic resonance, identical with vital breath, creates the universe.

6.s:
tāvatī caiśvarī rātriryatra prāṇaḥ praśāmyati /
prāṇagarbhasthamapyatra viśvaṃ sauṣumnavartmanā // 158
6.d:
तावती चैश्वरी रात्रिर्यत्र प्राणः प्रशाम्यति ।
प्राणगर्भस्थमप्यत्र विश्वं सौषुम्नवर्त्मना ॥ 158
6.m: And of equal length is the night of Īśvara, in which the vital breath comes to rest. / Although situated in the womb of the vital breath, the universe here, through the path of the suṣumnā,

6.s:
prāṇe brahmavile śānte saṃvidyāpyavaśiṣyate /
aṃśāṃśikāto'pyetasyāḥ sūkṣmasūkṣmataro layaḥ // 159
6.d:
प्राणे ब्रह्मविले शान्ते संविद्याप्यवशिष्यते ।
अंशांशिकातोऽप्येतस्याः सूक्ष्मसूक्ष्मतरो लयः ॥ 159
6.m: when the vital breath has come to rest in the aperture of Brahmā, remains reposing in consciousness. / Even from this fractional state, there is an increasingly subtle dissolution.

6.s:
guṇayitvaiśvaraṃ kālaṃ parārdhānāṃ śatena tu /
sādāśivaṃ dinaṃ rātrirmahāpralaya eva ca // 160
6.d:
गुणयित्वैश्वरं कालं परार्धानां शतेन तु ।
सादाशिवं दिनं रात्रिर्महाप्रलय एव च ॥ 160
6.m: Having multiplied the time of Īśvara by a hundred parārdhas, / there is a day and night of Sadāśiva, and that is the great dissolution itself.

6.s:
sadāśivaḥ svakālānte bindvardhendunirodhikāḥ /
ākramya nāde līyeta gṛhītvā sacarācaram // 161
6.d:
सदाशिवः स्वकालान्ते बिन्द्वर्धेन्दुनिरोधिकाः ।
आक्रम्य नादे लीयेत गृहीत्वा सचराचरम् ॥ 161
6.m: At the end of his own time, having taken up the moving and the unmoving, / Sadāśiva, traversing the bindu, the crescent moon, and the nirodhikā, dissolves into the nāda.

6.s:
nādo nādāntavṛttyā tu bhittvā brahmabilaṃ haṭhāt /
śaktitattve layaṃ yāti nijakālaparikṣaye // 162
6.d:
नादो नादान्तवृत्त्या तु भित्त्वा ब्रह्मबिलं हठात् ।
शक्तितत्त्वे लयं याति निजकालपरिक्षये ॥ 162
6.m: The nāda, however, by operating as nādānta, violently piercing the aperture of Brahmā, / dissolves into the level of power at the exhaustion of its own time.

6.s:
etāvacchaktitattve tu vijñeyaṃ khalvaharniśam /
śaktiḥ svakālavilaye vyāpinyāṃ līyate punaḥ // 163
6.d:
एतावच्छक्तितत्त्वे तु विज्ञेयं खल्वहर्निशम् ।
शक्तिः स्वकालविलये व्यापिन्यां लीयते पुनः ॥ 163
6.m: Just this much is indeed to be known as day and night on the level of power. / Power, at the dissolution of its own time, dissolves in turn into Vyāpinī.

6.s:
vyāpinyā taddivārātraṃ līyate sāpyanāśrite /
parārdhakoṭyā hatvāpi śaktikālamanāśrite // 164
6.d:
व्यापिन्या तद्दिवारात्रं लीयते साप्यनाश्रिते ।
परार्धकोट्या हत्वापि शक्तिकालमनाश्रिते ॥ 164
6.m: That day and night belongs to Vyāpinī; she too dissolves into Anāśrita. / Even having multiplied the time of power by a crore of parārdhas,

6.s:
dinaṃ rātriśca tatkāle parārdhaguṇite'pi ca /
so'pi yāti layaṃ sāmyasaṃjñe sāmanase pade // 165
6.d:
दिनं रात्रिश्च तत्काले परार्धगुणितेऽपि च ।
सोऽपि याति लयं साम्यसंज्ञे सामनसे पदे ॥ 165
6.m: there is a day and a night in Anāśrita; and when that time is multiplied by a parārdha, / that too dissolves into the abode called Sameness, which is endowed with mind (sāmanasa).

6.s:
sa kālaḥ sāmyasaṃjñaḥ syānnityo'kalyaḥ kalātmakaḥ /
yattatsāmanasaṃ rūpaṃ tatsāmyaṃ brahma viśvagam // 166
6.d:
स कालः साम्यसंज्ञः स्यान्नित्योऽकल्यः कलात्मकः ।
यत्तत्सामनसं रूपं तत्साम्यं ब्रह्म विश्वगम् ॥ 166
6.m: That time, called Sameness, is eternal, free of parts, and composed of parts. / What is of that nature endowed with mind—that Sameness is the all-pervading Brahman.

6.s:
ataḥ sāmanasātkālānnimeṣonmeṣamātrataḥ /
tuṭyādikaṃ parārdhāntaṃ sūte saivātra niṣṭhitam // 167
6.d:
अतः सामनसात्कालान्निमेषोन्मेषमात्रतः ।
तुट्यादिकं परार्धान्तं सूते सैवात्र निष्ठितम् ॥ 167
6.m: Therefore, from that time endowed with mind, from a mere blinking and opening [of the eyes], / that very [power] brings forth what is fixed here, beginning with the tuṭi and ending with the parārdha:

6.s:
daśaśatasahasramayutaṃ lakṣaniyutakoṭi sārbudaṃ vṛndam /
kharvanikharve śaṃkhābjajaladhimadhyāntamatha parārdhaṃ ca // 168
6.d:
दशशतसहस्रमयुतं लक्षनियुतकोटि सार्बुदं वृन्दम् ।
खर्वनिखर्वे शंखाब्जजलधिमध्यान्तमथ परार्धं च ॥ 168
6.m: Ten, a hundred, a thousand, ten thousand (ayuta), a hundred thousand (lakṣa), a million (niyuta), ten million (koṭi), an arbuda, a vṛnda, / a kharva, a nikharva, a śaṅkha, a padma, a jaladhi, a madhya, an anta, and then a parārdha.

6.s:
ityekasmātprabhṛti hi daśadhā daśadhā krameṇa kalayitvā /
ekādiparārdhānteṣvaṣṭādaśasu sthitiṃ brūyāt // 169
6.d:
इत्येकस्मात्प्रभृति हि दशधा दशधा क्रमेण कलयित्वा ।
एकादिपरार्धान्तेष्वष्टादशसु स्थितिं ब्रूयात् ॥ 169
6.m: Having counted thus, tenfold by tenfold in succession from one, / one should state their persistence through the eighteen places, beginning with one and ending with a parārdha.

6.s:
catvāra ete pralayā mukhyāḥ sargāśca tatkalāḥ /
bhūmūlanaiśaśaktisthāstadevāṇḍacatuṣṭayam // 170
6.d:
चत्वार एते प्रलया मुख्याः सर्गाश्च तत्कलाः ।
भूमूलनैशशक्तिस्थास्तदेवाण्डचतुष्टयम् ॥ 170
6.m: These four are the principal dissolutions and emanations are their parts; / they reside in the earth, the root, the nocturnal (māyā), and power—that very [set] is the tetrad of cosmic eggs.

6.s:
kālāgnirbhuvi saṃhartā māyānte kālatattvarāṭ /
śrīkaṇṭho mūla ekatra sṛṣṭisaṃhārakārakaḥ // 171
6.d:
कालाग्निर्भुवि संहर्ता मायान्ते कालतत्त्वराट् ।
श्रीकण्ठो मूल एकत्र सृष्टिसंहारकारकः ॥ 171
6.m: Kālāgni is the destroyer on earth; at the end of māyā is the king of the principle of time; / in the root is Śrīkaṇṭha, operating as the single agent of emission and dissolution.

6.s:
tallayo vāntarastasmādekaḥ sṛṣṭilayeśitā /
śrīmānaghoraḥ śaktyante saṃhartā sṛṣṭikṛcca saḥ // 172
6.d:
तल्लयो वान्तरस्तस्मादेकः सृष्टिलयेशिता ।
श्रीमानघोरः शक्त्यन्ते संहर्ता सृष्टिकृच्च सः ॥ 172
6.m: His dissolution is intermediate; therefore, one is the lord of emission and dissolution: / the glorious Aghora at the end of power is the destroyer and the agent of emission.

6.s:
tatsṛṣṭau sṛṣṭisaṃhārā niḥsaṃkhyā jagatāṃ yataḥ /
antarbhūtāstataḥ śāktī mahāsṛṣṭirudāhṛtā // 173
6.d:
तत्सृष्टौ सृष्टिसंहारा निःसंख्या जगतां यतः ।
अन्तर्भूतास्ततः शाक्ती महासृष्टिरुदाहृता ॥ 173
6.m: Because within his emission innumerable emissions and dissolutions of worlds / are included, therefore the emission pertaining to power is declared the great emission.

6.s:
laye brahmā harī rudraśatānyaṣṭakapañcakam /
ityanyonyaṃ kramādyānti layaṃ māyāntake'dhvani // 174
6.d:
लये ब्रह्मा हरी रुद्रशतान्यष्टकपञ्चकम् ।
इत्यन्योन्यं क्रमाद्यान्ति लयं मायान्तकेऽध्वनि ॥ 174
6.m: In dissolution, Brahmā, Hari, the hundreds of Rudras, the forty [deities]— / these, in succession, dissolve into each other in the path that ends in māyā.

6.s:
māyātattvalaye tvete prayānti paramaṃ padam /
māyordhve ye sitādhvasthāsteṣāṃ paraśive layaḥ // 175
6.d:
मायातत्त्वलये त्वेते प्रयान्ति परमं पदम् ।
मायोर्ध्वे ये सिताध्वस्थास्तेषां परशिवे लयः ॥ 175
6.m: At the dissolution of the principle of māyā, however, these go to the supreme abode; / the dissolution of those who reside in the pure path above māyā occurs in Paraśiva.

6.s:
tatrāpyaupādhikādbhedāllaye bhedaṃ pare viduḥ /
evaṃ tāttveśvare varge līne sṛṣṭau punaḥ pare // 176
6.d:
तत्राप्यौपाधिकाद्भेदाल्लये भेदं परे विदुः ।
एवं तात्त्वेश्वरे वर्गे लीने सृष्टौ पुनः परे ॥ 176
6.m: Even there, because of extrinsic difference, the higher know a difference in dissolution. / In this way, when the group of lords of principles is dissolved, then, in the next emission,

6.s:
tatsādhakāḥ śiveṣṭā vā tatsthānamadhiśerate /
brāhmī nāma parasyaiva śaktistāṃ yatra pātayet // 177
6.d:
तत्साधकाः शिवेष्टा वा तत्स्थानमधिशेरते ।
ब्राह्मी नाम परस्यैव शक्तिस्तां यत्र पातयेत् ॥ 177
6.m: adepts dedicated to them or favored by Śiva occupy their places. / The power of the Supreme alone is named Brāhmī; wherever he casts it,

6.s:
sa brahmā viṣṇurudrādyā vaiṣṇavyāderataḥ kramāt /
śaktimantaṃ vihāyānyaṃ śaktiḥ kiṃ yāti nedṛśam // 178
6.d:
स ब्रह्मा विष्णुरुद्राद्या वैष्णव्यादेरतः क्रमात् ।
शक्तिमन्तं विहायान्यं शक्तिः किं याति नेदृशम् ॥ 178
6.m: he is Brahmā; similarly Viṣṇu, Rudra, and the rest from Vaiṣṇavī and the others in succession. / Does power, leaving aside the possessor of power, go to another? It is not so.

6.s:
chāditaprathitāśeṣa śaktirekaḥ śivastathā /
evaṃ visṛṣṭipralayāḥ prāṇa ekatra niṣṭhitāḥ // 179
6.d:
छादितप्रथिताशेष शक्तिरेकः शिवस्तथा ।
एवं विसृष्टिप्रलयाः प्राण एकत्र निष्ठिताः ॥ 179
6.m: Śiva is one, whose entire power is concealed and expanded. / Thus emission and dissolution are grounded in prāṇa as a single whole.

6.s:
so'pi saṃvidi saṃvicca cinmātre jñeyavarjite /
cinmātrameva devī ca sā parā parameśvarī // 180
6.d:
सोऽपि संविदि संविच्च चिन्मात्रे ज्ञेयवर्जिते ।
चिन्मात्रमेव देवी च सा परा परमेश्वरी ॥ 180
6.m: That [prāṇa] too is in consciousness, and consciousness is in pure consciousness devoid of objects of knowledge; / and pure consciousness alone is the Goddess, the supreme Parameśvarī.

6.s:
aṣṭātriṃśaṃ ca tattattvaṃ hṛdayaṃ tatparāparam /
tena saṃvittvamevaitatspandamānaṃ svabhāvataḥ // 181
6.d:
अष्टात्रिंशं च तत्तत्त्वं हृदयं तत्परापरम् ।
तेन संवित्त्वमेवैतत्स्पन्दमानं स्वभावतः ॥ 181
6.m: And that is the thirty-eighth principle, the Heart, both supreme and non-supreme. / Because of this, it is precisely consciousness that vibrates by its own nature.

6.s:
layodayā iti prāṇe ṣaṣṭyabdodayakīrtanam /
icchāmātrapratiṣṭheyaṃ kriyāvaicitryacarcanā // 182
6.d:
लयोदया इति प्राणे षष्ट्यब्दोदयकीर्तनम् ।
इच्छामात्रप्रतिष्ठेयं क्रियावैचित्र्यचर्चना ॥ 182
6.m: Thus the rising of dissolutions and emissions is the proclamation of the rising of sixty years within the prāṇa. / This examination of the manifold diversity of action is grounded in will alone.

6.s:
kālaśaktistato bāhye naitasyā niyataṃ vapuḥ /
svapnasvapne tathā svapne supte saṃkalpagocare // 183
6.d:
कालशक्तिस्ततो बाह्ये नैतस्या नियतं वपुः ।
स्वप्नस्वप्ने तथा स्वप्ने सुप्ते संकल्पगोचरे ॥ 183
6.m: The power of time is thus external; it has no fixed form: / in dream-within-dream, likewise in dream, in deep sleep, in the realm of mental conception,

6.s:
samādhau viśvasaṃhārasṛṣṭikramavivecane /
mito'pi kila kālāṃśo vitatatvena bhāsate // 184
6.d:
समाधौ विश्वसंहारसृष्टिक्रमविवेचने ।
मितोऽपि किल कालांशो विततत्वेन भासते ॥ 184
6.m: in meditative absorption, and in the discerning of the succession of the universe's dissolution and emission, / even a measured portion of time appears as extended.

6.s:
pramātrabhede bhede'tha citro vitatimāpyasau /
evaṃ prāṇe yathā kālaḥ kriyāvaicitryaśaktijaḥ // 185
6.d:
प्रमात्रभेदे भेदेऽथ चित्रो विततिमाप्यसौ ।
एवं प्राणे यथा कालः क्रियावैचित्र्यशक्तिजः ॥ 185
6.m: When there is a distinction of subjects or a distinction [of states], this [time] has a diverse extension. / Just as time in the prāṇa arises from the power of manifold action,

6.s:
tathāpāne'pi hṛdayānmūlapīṭhavisarpiṇi /
mūlābhidhamahāpīṭhasaṅkocapravikāsayoḥ // 186
6.d:
तथापानेऽपि हृदयान्मूलपीठविसर्पिणि ।
मूलाभिधमहापीठसङ्कोचप्रविकासयोः ॥ 186
6.m: so also in the apāna, extending from the heart to the root-seat; / in the contraction and expansion of the great seat called the root,

6.s:
brahmādyanāśritāntānāṃ cinute sṛṣṭisaṃhṛtī /
śaśvadyadyapyapāno'ya mitthaṃ vahati kiṃtvasau // 187
6.d:
ब्रह्माद्यनाश्रितान्तानां चिनुते सृष्टिसंहृती ।
शश्वद्यद्यप्यपानोऽय मित्थं वहति किंत्वसौ ॥ 187
6.m: it gathers the emissions and dissolutions of [the levels] from Brahmā to Anāśrita. / Even though this apāna flows incessantly in this manner, nevertheless,

6.s:
avedyayatno yatnena yogibhiḥ samupāsyate /
hṛtkandānandasaṃkocavikāsadvādaśāntagāḥ // 188
6.d:
अवेद्ययत्नो यत्नेन योगिभिः समुपास्यते ।
हृत्कन्दानन्दसंकोचविकासद्वादशान्तगाः ॥ 188
6.m: its effortless effort is meditated upon by yogins with exertion; / extending to the twelve ends of contraction and expansion of the heart-bulb's bliss,

6.s:
brahmādayo'nāśritāntāḥ sevyante'tra suyogibhiḥ /
ete ca parameśānaśaktitvādviśvavartinaḥ // 189
6.d:
ब्रह्मादयोऽनाश्रितान्ताः सेव्यन्तेऽत्र सुयोगिभिः ।
एते च परमेशानशक्तित्वाद्विश्ववर्तिनः ॥ 189
6.m: the levels from Brahmā to Anāśrita are served here by good yogins. / And these, being powers of the Supreme Lord, abide in the universe;

6.s:
dehamapyaśnuvānāstatkāraṇānīti kāmike /
bālyayauvanavṛddhatvanidhaneṣu punarbhave // 190
6.d:
देहमप्यश्नुवानास्तत्कारणानीति कामिके ।
बाल्ययौवनवृद्धत्वनिधनेषु पुनर्भवे ॥ 190
6.m: pervading the body as well, they are its primary causes, as stated in the Kāmika: / in childhood, youth, old age, death, rebirth,

6.s:
muktau ca dehe brahmādyāḥ ṣaḍadhiṣṭhānakāriṇaḥ /
tasyānte tu parā devī yatra yukto na jāyate // 191
6.d:
मुक्तौ च देहे ब्रह्माद्याः षडधिष्ठानकारिणः ।
तस्यान्ते तु परा देवी यत्र युक्तो न जायते ॥ 191
6.m: and liberation in the body, the six beginning with Brahmā exercise superintendence; / at its end is the supreme Goddess, joined to whom one is not reborn.

6.s:
anena jñātamātreṇa dīkṣānugrahakṛdbhavet /
samastakāraṇollāsapade suvidite yataḥ // 192
6.d:
अनेन ज्ञातमात्रेण दीक्षानुग्रहकृद्भवेत् ।
समस्तकारणोल्लासपदे सुविदिते यतः ॥ 192
6.m: By the mere knowledge of this, one becomes an agent of initiation and grace, / because when the abode of the flash of all primary causes is thoroughly known,

6.s:
akāraṇaṃ śivaṃ vindedyattadviśvasya kāraṇam /
adhovaktraṃ tvidaṃ dvaitakalaṅkaikāntaśātanam // 193
6.d:
अकारणं शिवं विन्देद्यत्तद्विश्वस्य कारणम् ।
अधोवक्त्रं त्विदं द्वैतकलङ्कैकान्तशातनम् ॥ 193
6.m: one finds causeless Śiva, who is the cause of the universe. / This downward-facing mouth, however, completely destroys the taint of duality,

6.s:
kṣīyate tadupāsāyāṃ yenordhvādharaḍambaraḥ /
atrāpānodaye prāgvatṣaṣṭyabdodayayojanām // 194
6.d:
क्षीयते तदुपासायां येनोर्ध्वाधरडम्बरः ।
अत्रापानोदये प्राग्वत्षष्ट्यब्दोदययोजनाम् ॥ 194
6.m: by which the pomp of upper and lower diminishes through its worship. / Here, in the rising of apāna, as before, one should perform the coordination

6.s:
yāvatkurvīta tuṭyāderyuktāṅgulavibhāgataḥ /
evaṃ samāne'pi vidhiḥ sa hi hārdīṣu nāḍiṣu // 195
6.d:
यावत्कुर्वीत तुट्यादेर्युक्ताङ्गुलविभागतः ।
एवं समानेऽपि विधिः स हि हार्दीषु नाडिषु ॥ 195
6.m: of the rising of the sixty years from the tuṭi onwards, according to the proper division of digits. / The same rule applies to the samāna: for moving in the channels of the heart,

6.s:
saṃcaransarvatodikkaṃ daśadhaiva vibhāvyate /
daśa mukhyā mahānāḍīḥ pūrayanneṣa tadgatāḥ // 196
6.d:
संचरन्सर्वतोदिक्कं दशधैव विभाव्यते ।
दश मुख्या महानाडीः पूरयन्नेष तद्गताः ॥ 196
6.m: it is conceived as ten-fold, going in every direction. / Filling the ten principal great channels, and traversing

6.s:
nāḍyantaraśritā nāḍīḥ krāmandehe samasthitiḥ /
aṣṭāsu digdaleṣveṣa krāmaṃstaddikpateḥ kramāt // 197
6.d:
नाड्यन्तरश्रिता नाडीः क्रामन्देहे समस्थितिः ।
अष्टासु दिग्दलेष्वेष क्रामंस्तद्दिक्पतेः क्रमात् ॥ 197
6.m: the subsidiary channels resting within them, it is situated equally in the body. / Moving through the eight petals of the directions, following the regent of each direction,

6.s:
ceṣṭitānyanukurvāṇo raudraḥ saumyaśca bhāsate /
sa eva nāḍītritaye vāmadakṣiṇamadhyage // 198
6.d:
चेष्टितान्यनुकुर्वाणो रौद्रः सौम्यश्च भासते ।
स एव नाडीत्रितये वामदक्षिणमध्यगे ॥ 198
6.m: imitating their activities, it shines forth as fierce and gentle. / That very [samāna], moving in the triad of channels—left, right, and middle—

6.s:
indvarkāgnimaye mukhye caraṃstiṣṭhatyaharniśam /
sārdhanālīdvayaṃ prāṇaśatāni nava yatsthitam // 199
6.d:
इन्द्वर्काग्निमये मुख्ये चरंस्तिष्ठत्यहर्निशम् ।
सार्धनालीद्वयं प्राणशतानि नव यत्स्थितम् ॥ 199
6.m: which are principal and composed of the moon, the sun, and fire, abides day and night. / That which abides for two and a half nālīs is nine hundred prāṇas;

6.s:
tāvadvahannahorātraṃ caturviṃśatidhā caret /
viṣuvadvāsare prātaḥ sāṃśāṃ nālīṃ sa madhyagaḥ // 200
6.d:
तावद्वहन्नहोरात्रं चतुर्विंशतिधा चरेत् ।
विषुवद्वासरे प्रातः सांशां नालीं स मध्यगः ॥ 200
6.m: flowing for that duration, it moves through day and night twenty-four times. / On the day of the equinox, in the morning, centered in the middle channel for a nālī with its fraction,

6.s:
vāmetarodaksavyānyairyāvatsaṃkrāntipañcakam /
evaṃ kṣīṇāsu pādonacaturdaśasu nāliṣu // 201
6.d:
वामेतरोदक्सव्यान्यैर्यावत्संक्रान्तिपञ्चकम् ।
एवं क्षीणासु पादोनचतुर्दशसु नालिषु ॥ 201
6.m: it moves through the five transitions by means of the left, right, northern, and southern [channels]. / When thirteen and three-quarter nālīs have thus passed,

6.s:
madhyāhne dakṣaviṣuvannavaprāṇaśatīṃ vahet /
dakṣodaganyodagdakṣaiḥ punaḥ saṃkrāntipañcakam // 202
6.d:
मध्याह्ने दक्षविषुवन्नवप्राणशतीं वहेत् ।
दक्षोदगन्योदग्दक्षैः पुनः संक्रान्तिपञ्चकम् ॥ 202
6.m: at midday the southern equinox bears nine hundred prāṇas. / Then through southern, northern, intermediate, northern, and southern, there are again five transitions,

6.s:
navāsuśatamekaikaṃ tato viṣuvaduttaram /
pañcake pañcake'tīte saṃkrānterviṣuvadbahiḥ // 203
6.d:
नवासुशतमेकैकं ततो विषुवदुत्तरम् ।
पञ्चके पञ्चकेऽतीते संक्रान्तेर्विषुवद्बहिः ॥ 203
6.m: each consisting of nine hundred breaths; from that arises the northern equinox. / When each group of five transitions has passed, an equinox occurs externally;

6.s:
yadvattathāntaḥ saṅkrāntirnavaprāṇaśatāni sā /
evaṃ rātrāvapītyevaṃ viṣuvaddivasātsamāt // 204
6.d:
यद्वत्तथान्तः सङ्क्रान्तिर्नवप्राणशतानि सा ।
एवं रात्रावपीत्येवं विषुवद्दिवसात्समात् ॥ 204
6.m: just as it is outside, so internally the transition consists of nine hundred prāṇas. / In this way it is at night also; thus, starting from the day of the equinox,

6.s:
ārabhyāharniśāvṛddhihrāsasaṅkrāntigo'pyasau /
rātryantadinapūrvāṃśau madhyāhno divasakṣayaḥ // 205
6.d:
आरभ्याहर्निशावृद्धिह्राससङ्क्रान्तिगोऽप्यसौ ।
रात्र्यन्तदिनपूर्वांशौ मध्याह्नो दिवसक्षयः ॥ 205
6.m: it undergoes the transitions of increase and decrease of day and night: / the end of the night and the early part of the day, midday, the decline of day,

6.s:
sa śarvaryudayo madhyamudakto viṣutedṛśī /
vyāptau viṣeryato vṛttiḥ sāmyaṃ ca vyāptirucyate // 206
6.d:
स शर्वर्युदयो मध्यमुदक्तो विषुतेदृशी ।
व्याप्तौ विषेर्यतो वृत्तिः साम्यं च व्याप्तिरुच्यते ॥ 206
6.m: the arrival of night, and its midpoint: the equinox is seen to be of such a nature. / For the root viṣ- denotes pervasion, and equality is said to be pervasion.

6.s:
tadarhati ca yaḥ kālo viṣuvattadihoditaḥ /
viṣuvatprabhṛti hrāsavṛddhī ye dinarātrige // 207
6.d:
तदर्हति च यः कालो विषुवत्तदिहोदितः ।
विषुवत्प्रभृति ह्रासवृद्धी ये दिनरात्रिगे ॥ 207
6.m: And the time corresponding to that is here called the equinox. / From the equinox onward, the decrease and increase occurring in day and night

6.s:
tatkrameṇaiva saṃkrāntihrāsavṛddhī divāniśoḥ /
itthaṃ samānamaruto varṣadvayavikalpanam // 208
6.d:
तत्क्रमेणैव संक्रान्तिह्रासवृद्धी दिवानिशोः ।
इत्थं समानमरुतो वर्षद्वयविकल्पनम् ॥ 208
6.m: occur by that very sequence of transition, decrease, and increase of day and night. / Thus is the conceptual differentiation of two years in the samāna breath.

6.s:
cāra ekatra nahyatra śvāsapraśvāsacarcanam /
samāne'pi tuṭeḥ pūrvaṃ yāvatṣaṣṭyabdagocaram // 209
6.d:
चार एकत्र नह्यत्र श्वासप्रश्वासचर्चनम् ।
समानेऽपि तुटेः पूर्वं यावत्षष्ट्यब्दगोचरम् ॥ 209
6.m: Its movement is in a single place; here there is indeed no consideration of inhalation and exhalation. / Even in the samāna, from before a tuṭi up to the scope of sixty years,

6.s:
kālasaṃkhyā susūkṣmaikacāragā gaṇyate budhaiḥ /
saṃdhyāpūrvāhṇamadhyāhnamadhyarātrādi yatkila // 210
6.d:
कालसंख्या सुसूक्ष्मैकचारगा गण्यते बुधैः ।
संध्यापूर्वाह्णमध्याह्नमध्यरात्रादि यत्किल ॥ 210
6.m: the reckoning of time traversing an extremely subtle single movement is computed by the wise. / The twilight, morning, noon, midnight, and so on that are known

6.s:
antaḥsaṃkrāntigaṃ grāhyaṃ tanmukhyaṃ tatphaloditeḥ /
uktaḥ samānagaḥ kāla udāne tu nirūpyate // 211
6.d:
अन्तःसंक्रान्तिगं ग्राह्यं तन्मुख्यं तत्फलोदितेः ।
उक्तः समानगः काल उदाने तु निरूप्यते ॥ 211
6.m: are to be understood as occurring in the internal transition; that is primary, because of the arising of its fruit. / The time occurring in the samāna has been described; but in the udāna it is now examined.

6.s:
prāṇavyāptau yaduktaṃ tadudāne'pyatra kevalam /
nāsāśaktyantayoḥ sthāne brahmarandhrordhvadhāmanī // 212
6.d:
प्राणव्याप्तौ यदुक्तं तदुदानेऽप्यत्र केवलम् ।
नासाशक्त्यन्तयोः स्थाने ब्रह्मरन्ध्रोर्ध्वधामनी ॥ 212
6.m: What was stated regarding the pervasion of prāṇa applies also to the udāna; only here, / in place of the nostril and the limit of power, are the opening of Brahmā and the upper abode.

6.s:
tenodāne'tra hṛdayānmūrdhanyadvādaśāntagam /
tuṭyādiṣaṣṭivarṣāntaṃ viśvaṃ kālaṃ vicārayet // 213
6.d:
तेनोदानेऽत्र हृदयान्मूर्धन्यद्वादशान्तगम् ।
तुट्यादिषष्टिवर्षान्तं विश्वं कालं विचारयेत् ॥ 213
