6.m: Therefore, in the udāna, from the heart up to the cranial limit of twelve fingers, / one should contemplate all time beginning with a tuṭi and ending with sixty years.

6.s:
vyāne tu viśvātmamaye vyāpake kramavarjite /
sūkṣmasūkṣmocchaladrūpamātraḥ kālo vyavasthitaḥ // 214
6.d:
व्याने तु विश्वात्ममये व्यापके क्रमवर्जिते ।
सूक्ष्मसूक्ष्मोच्छलद्रूपमात्रः कालो व्यवस्थितः ॥ 214
6.m: In the vyāna, however, which consists of the nature of all things, is pervasive, and devoid of sequence, / time is established merely as an extremely subtle emergent form.

6.s:
sṛṣṭiḥ pravilayaḥ sthemā saṃhāro'nugraho yataḥ /
kramātprāṇādike kāle taṃ taṃ tatrāśrayettataḥ // 215
6.d:
सृष्टिः प्रविलयः स्थेमा संहारोऽनुग्रहो यतः ।
क्रमात्प्राणादिके काले तं तं तत्राश्रयेत्ततः ॥ 215
6.m: Because emission, dissolution, stasis, reabsorption, and grace / occur sequentially in the time of prāṇa and the rest, therefore one should resort to each of them there.

6.s:
prāṇacāre'tra yo varṇapadamantrodayaḥ sthitaḥ /
yatnajo'yatnajaḥ sūkṣmaḥ paraḥ sthūlaḥ sa kathyate // 216
6.d:
प्राणचारेऽत्र यो वर्णपदमन्त्रोदयः स्थितः ।
यत्नजोऽयत्नजः सूक्ष्मः परः स्थूलः स कथ्यते ॥ 216
6.m: The arising of phonemes, words, and mantras that resides in this movement of prāṇa, / produced with effort, produced effortlessly, subtle, supreme, and gross, is now declared.

6.s:
eko nādātmako varṇaḥ sarvavarṇāvibhāgavān /
so'nastamitarūpatvādanāhata ihoditaḥ // 217
6.d:
एको नादात्मको वर्णः सर्ववर्णाविभागवान् ।
सोऽनस्तमितरूपत्वादनाहत इहोदितः ॥ 217
6.m: The single phoneme consisting of resonance, free of differentiation into all the [individual] phonemes, / is here called the unstruck because of its never-setting nature.

6.s:
sa tu bhairavasadbhāvo mātṛsadbhāva eṣa saḥ /
parā saikākṣarā devī yatra līnaṃ carācaram // 218
6.d:
स तु भैरवसद्भावो मातृसद्भाव एष सः ।
परा सैकाक्षरा देवी यत्र लीनं चराचरम् ॥ 218
6.m: That indeed is the reality of Bhairava; that is the reality of the Mother; / that is the supreme Goddess of a single phoneme in whom the moving and unmoving are dissolved.

6.s:
hrasvārṇatrayamekaikaṃ ravyaṅgulamathetarat /
praveśa iti ṣaḍvarṇāḥ sūryendupathagāḥ kramāt // 219
6.d:
ह्रस्वार्णत्रयमेकैकं रव्यङ्गुलमथेतरत् ।
प्रवेश इति षड्वर्णाः सूर्येन्दुपथगाः क्रमात् ॥ 219
6.m: The three short vowels, each one twelve fingers, then the other [three] / in the entry: thus are the six phonemes traversing the paths of the sun and moon in sequence.

6.s:
ikārokārayorādisandhau saṃdhyakṣaradvayam /
e+o iti praveśe tu ai+au iti dvayaṃ viduḥ // 220
6.d:
इकारोकारयोरादिसन्धौ संध्यक्षरद्वयम् ।
ए+ओ इति प्रवेशे तु ऐ+औ इति द्वयं विदुः ॥ 220
6.m: At the initial juncture of the vowels ‘i’ and ‘u’ are the two diphthongs / ‘e’ and ‘o’; but upon the entry they know the two as ‘ai’ and ‘au’.

6.s:
ṣaṇṭhārṇāni praveśe tu dvādaśāntalalāṭayoḥ /
gale hṛdi ca bindvarṇavisargau paritaḥsthitau // 221
6.d:
षण्ठार्णानि प्रवेशे तु द्वादशान्तललाटयोः ।
गले हृदि च बिन्द्वर्णविसर्गौ परितःस्थितौ ॥ 221
6.m: The neuter vowels are in the entry at the limit of twelve fingers and the forehead; / at the throat and in the heart, the anusvāra phoneme and the creative emission are situated round about.

6.s:
kādipañcakamādyasya varṇasyāntaḥ sadoditam /
evaṃ sasthānavarṇānāmantaḥ sā sārṇasantatiḥ // 222
6.d:
कादिपञ्चकमाद्यस्य वर्णस्यान्तः सदोदितम् ।
एवं सस्थानवर्णानामन्तः सा सार्णसन्ततिः ॥ 222
6.m: The group of five beginning with ‘ka’ is ever arisen within the first phoneme; / likewise, within the phonemes sharing the same place of articulation, is that succession of phonemes.

6.s:
hṛdyeṣa prāṇarūpastu sakāro jīvanātmakaḥ /
binduḥ prakāśo hārṇaśca pūraṇātmatayā sthitaḥ // 223
6.d:
हृद्येष प्राणरूपस्तु सकारो जीवनात्मकः ।
बिन्दुः प्रकाशो हार्णश्च पूरणात्मतया स्थितः ॥ 223
6.m: This ‘sa’-phoneme, which is the nature of the vital breath in the heart, consists of living; / the bindu is luminosity, and the ‘ha’-phoneme stands as consisting of repletion.

6.s:
uktaḥ paro'yamudayo varṇānāṃ sūkṣma ucyate /
praveśe ṣoḍaśaunmukhye ravayaḥ ṣaṇṭhavarjitāḥ // 224
6.d:
उक्तः परोऽयमुदयो वर्णानां सूक्ष्म उच्यते ।
प्रवेशे षोडशौन्मुख्ये रवयः षण्ठवर्जिताः ॥ 224
6.m: This supreme arising of phonemes has been taught; the subtle one is now stated: / in the entry there are sixteen, and in the directed outward state twelve, excluding the neuter vowels.

6.s:
tadevendvarkamatrānye varṇāḥ sūkṣmodayastvayam /
kālo'rdhamātraḥ kādīnāṃ trayastriṃśata ucyate // 225
6.d:
तदेवेन्द्वर्कमत्रान्ये वर्णाः सूक्ष्मोदयस्त्वयम् ।
कालोऽर्धमात्रः कादीनां त्रयस्त्रिंशत उच्यते ॥ 225
6.m: That alone is the moon and the sun here; the remaining phonemes are this subtle arising: / the time of the thirty-three phonemes beginning with ‘ka’ is stated to be half a mora.

6.s:
mātrā hrasvāḥ pañca dīrghāṣṭakaṃ dvistriḥ plutaṃ tu lṝ /
ekāśītimimāmardhamātrāṇāmāha no guruḥ // 226
6.d:
मात्रा ह्रस्वाः पञ्च दीर्घाष्टकं द्विस्त्रिः प्लुतं तु लॄ ।
एकाशीतिमिमामर्धमात्राणामाह नो गुरुः ॥ 226
6.m: The short vowels have one mora, the eight long have two, the prolated ‘lṝ’ has three: / our guru taught this eighty-one of half-moras,

6.s:
yadvaśādbhagavānekāśītikaṃ mantramabhyadhāt /
ekāśītipadā devī śaktiḥ proktā śivātmikā // 227
6.d:
यद्वशाद्भगवानेकाशीतिकं मन्त्रमभ्यधात् ।
एकाशीतिपदा देवी शक्तिः प्रोक्ता शिवात्मिका ॥ 227
6.m: by virtue of which the Lord declared the mantra of eighty-one [units]; / the divine śakti identical with Śiva is spoken of as having eighty-one words.

6.s:
śrīmātaṅge tathā dharmasaṃghātātmā śivo yataḥ /
tathā tathā parāmarśaśakticakreśvaraḥ prabhuḥ // 228
6.d:
श्रीमातङ्गे तथा धर्मसंघातात्मा शिवो यतः ।
तथा तथा परामर्शशक्तिचक्रेश्वरः प्रभुः ॥ 228
6.m: So too in the venerable Mātaṅga, since Śiva consists of the collection of qualities, / and in that very way the Lord is the sovereign of the wheel of the powers of apprehension,

6.s:
sthūlaikāśītipadajaparāmarśairvibhāvyate /
tata eva parāmarśo yāvatyekaḥ samāpyate // 229
6.d:
स्थूलैकाशीतिपदजपरामर्शैर्विभाव्यते ।
तत एव परामर्शो यावत्येकः समाप्यते ॥ 229
6.m: he is conceived through the gross apprehensions arising from the eighty-one words. / For that very reason, as far as a single apprehension extends to completion,

6.s:
tāvattatpadamuktaṃ no suptiṅniyamayāntritam /
ekāśītipadodāravimarśaktamabṛṃhitaḥ // 230
6.d:
तावत्तत्पदमुक्तं नो सुप्तिङ्नियमयान्त्रितम् ।
एकाशीतिपदोदारविमर्शक्तमबृंहितः ॥ 230
6.m: that much is said to be a ‘word’, not constrained by the rules of nominal and verbal endings; / expanded by the noble reflective awareness of eighty-one words,

6.s:
sthūlopāyaḥ paropāyastveṣa mātrākṛto layaḥ /
ardhamātrā nava nava syuścaturṣu caturṣu yat // 231
6.d:
स्थूलोपायः परोपायस्त्वेष मात्राकृतो लयः ।
अर्धमात्रा नव नव स्युश्चतुर्षु चतुर्षु यत् ॥ 231
6.m: this gross means is the supreme means, a dissolution effected through moras; / because nine half-moras each occur in every four

6.s:
aṅguleṣviti ṣaṭtriṃśatyekāśītipadodayaḥ /
aṅgule navabhāgena vibhakte navamāśakāḥ // 232
6.d:
अङ्गुलेष्विति षट्त्रिंशत्येकाशीतिपदोदयः ।
अङ्गुले नवभागेन विभक्ते नवमाशकाः ॥ 232
6.m: fingers: thus in thirty-six [fingers] is the arising of eighty-one words. / When a finger is divided into nine parts, the ninths

6.s:
vedā mātrārdhamanyattu dvicatuḥṣaṅguṇaṃ trayam /
evamaṅgularandhrāṃśacatuṣkadvayagaṃ laghu // 233
6.d:
वेदा मात्रार्धमन्यत्तु द्विचतुःषङ्गुणं त्रयम् ।
एवमङ्गुलरन्ध्रांशचतुष्कद्वयगं लघु ॥ 233
6.m: are four for half a mora; but the other three are two-, four-, and sixfold [that]. / Thus a short vowel occurs in twice four parts of a ninth of a finger;

6.s:
dīrghaṃ plutaṃ kramāddvitriguṇamardhaṃ tato'pi hal /
kṣakārastryardhamātrātmā mātrikaḥ satathāntarā // 234
6.d:
दीर्घं प्लुतं क्रमाद्द्वित्रिगुणमर्धं ततोऽपि हल् ।
क्षकारस्त्र्यर्धमात्रात्मा मात्रिकः सतथान्तरा ॥ 234
6.m: the long and prolated are respectively twice and thrice that, and a consonant is half of it; / the phoneme ‘kṣa’ consists of three half-moras, having a mora, and likewise between

6.s:
viśrāntāvardhamātrāsya tasmiṃstu kalite sati /
aṅgulārdhe'dribhāgena tvardhamātrā purā punaḥ // 235
6.d:
विश्रान्तावर्धमात्रास्य तस्मिंस्तु कलिते सति ।
अङ्गुलार्धेऽद्रिभागेन त्वर्धमात्रा पुरा पुनः ॥ 235
6.m: the rests there is its half-mora; but when that is calculated, / there is half a mora previously in the seventh part of half a finger, and again,

6.s:
kṣakāraḥ sarvasaṃyogagrahaṇātmā tu sarvagaḥ /
sarvavarṇodayādyantasandhiṣūdayabhāgvibhuḥ // 236
6.d:
क्षकारः सर्वसंयोगग्रहणात्मा तु सर्वगः ।
सर्ववर्णोदयाद्यन्तसन्धिषूदयभाग्विभुः ॥ 236
6.m: the phoneme ‘kṣa’, whose essence is the grasping of all conjuncts, is all-pervading; / that all-pervasive phoneme participates in arising at the initial and final junctions of the arising of all phonemes.

6.s:
itthaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśake cāre varṇānāmudayaḥ phale /
krūre saumye vilomena hādi yāvadapaścimam // 237
6.d:
इत्थं षट्त्रिंशके चारे वर्णानामुदयः फले ।
क्रूरे सौम्ये विलोमेन हादि यावदपश्चिमम् ॥ 237
6.m: Thus in a movement of thirty-six [fingers] is the arising of phonemes in fruit; / in the fierce and the gentle [movements] in reverse order from ‘ha’ down to the very first.

6.s:
hṛdyakāro dvādaśānte hakārastadidaṃ viduḥ /
ahamātmakamadvaitaṃ yaḥ prakāśātmaviśramaḥ // 238
6.d:
हृद्यकारो द्वादशान्ते हकारस्तदिदं विदुः ।
अहमात्मकमद्वैतं यः प्रकाशात्मविश्रमः ॥ 238
6.m: In the heart is the phoneme ‘a’, and at the limit of twelve fingers is the phoneme ‘ha’; thus they know this / non-duality whose nature is ‘I’ (aham), which is the rest consisting of luminosity.

6.s:
śivaśaktyavibhāgena mātraikāśītikā tviyam /
dvāsaptatāvaṅguleṣu dviguṇatvena saṃsaret // 239
6.d:
शिवशक्त्यविभागेन मात्रैकाशीतिका त्वियम् ।
द्वासप्ततावङ्गुलेषु द्विगुणत्वेन संसरेत् ॥ 239
6.m: Through the non-differentiation of Śiva and śakti, this eighty-one-mora [movement], / by being doubled, would circulate through seventy-two fingers.

6.s:
uktaḥ sūkṣmodayastraidhaṃ dvidhoktastu parodayaḥ /
atha sthūlodayo'rṇānāṃ bhaṇyate guruṇoditaḥ // 240
6.d:
उक्तः सूक्ष्मोदयस्त्रैधं द्विधोक्तस्तु परोदयः ।
अथ स्थूलोदयोऽर्णानां भण्यते गुरुणोदितः ॥ 240
6.m: The subtle arising has been spoken of as threefold, and the supreme arising has been taught as twofold; / now the gross arising of the phonemes, taught by the guru, is recited:

6.s:
ekaikamardhapraharaṃ dine vargāṣṭakodayaḥ /
rātrau ca hrāsavṛddhyatra kecidāhurna ke'pi tu // 241
6.d:
एकैकमर्धप्रहरं दिने वर्गाष्टकोदयः ।
रात्रौ च ह्रासवृद्ध्यत्र केचिदाहुर्न केऽपि तु ॥ 241
6.m: The arising of the eight classes occurs for half a watch each in the day, / and at night; here some speak of decrease and increase, but some do not.

6.s:
eṣa vargodayo rātrau divā cāpyardhayāmagaḥ /
prāṇatrayodaśaśatī pañcāśadadhikā ca sā // 242
6.d:
एष वर्गोदयो रात्रौ दिवा चाप्यर्धयामगः ।
प्राणत्रयोदशशती पञ्चाशदधिका च सा ॥ 242
6.m: This arising of classes at night and during the day occurs in half a watch: / that is thirteen hundred and fifty breaths.

6.s:
adhyardhā kila saṃkrāntirvarge varge divāniśoḥ /
tadaikye tūdayaścāraśatānāṃ saptaviṃśatiḥ // 243
6.d:
अध्यर्धा किल संक्रान्तिर्वर्गे वर्गे दिवानिशोः ।
तदैक्ये तूदयश्चारशतानां सप्तविंशतिः ॥ 243
6.m: In each class, day and night, there is indeed one and a half transitions; / in their union, the movement is the arising of twenty-seven hundred [breaths].

6.s:
nava vargāṃstu ye prāhusteṣāṃ prāṇaśatī svīn[viḥ] /
satribhāgaiva saṃkrāntirvarge pratyekamucyate // 244
6.d:
नव वर्गांस्तु ये प्राहुस्तेषां प्राणशती स्वीन्[विः] ।
सत्रिभागैव संक्रान्तिर्वर्गे प्रत्येकमुच्यते ॥ 244
6.m: For those who speak of nine classes, however, the breaths are twelve hundred; / in each class a transition with a third part is stated.

6.s:
aharniśaṃ tadaikye tu śatānāṃ śruticakṣuṣī /
sthūlo vargodayaḥ so'yamathārṇodaya ucyate // 245
6.d:
अहर्निशं तदैक्ये तु शतानां श्रुतिचक्षुषी ।
स्थूलो वर्गोदयः सोऽयमथार्णोदय उच्यते ॥ 245
6.m: In their union, day and night, there are twenty-four hundred [breaths]. / That is the gross arising of classes; now the arising of phonemes is stated:

6.s:
ekaikavarṇe prāṇānāṃ dviśataṃ ṣoḍaśādhikam /
bahiścaṣakaṣaṭtriṃśaddina itthaṃ tathāniśi // 246
6.d:
एकैकवर्णे प्राणानां द्विशतं षोडशाधिकम् ।
बहिश्चषकषट्त्रिंशद्दिन इत्थं तथानिशि ॥ 246
6.m: For each single phoneme there are two hundred and sixteen breaths / and thirty-six caṣakas externally; thus in the day and so at night.

6.s:
śatamaṣṭottaraṃ tatra raudraṃ śāktamathottaram /
yāmalasthitiyoge tu rudraśaktyavibhāgitā // 247
6.d:
शतमष्टोत्तरं तत्र रौद्रं शाक्तमथोत्तरम् ।
यामलस्थितियोगे तु रुद्रशक्त्यविभागिता ॥ 247
6.m: There, one hundred and eight are terrible, and the next belong to śakti; / but in the union of the state of the dyad, there is non-differentiation of Rudra and śakti.

6.s:
dinarātryavibhāge tu dṛgvahnyabdhyasucāraṇāḥ /
sapañcamāṃśā nāḍī ca bahirvarṇodayaḥ smṛtaḥ // 248
6.d:
दिनरात्र्यविभागे तु दृग्वह्न्यब्ध्यसुचारणाः ।
सपञ्चमांशा नाडी च बहिर्वर्णोदयः स्मृतः ॥ 248
6.m: In the non-differentiation of day and night, the movements of breath are four hundred and thirty-two, / and a nāḍī with a fifth part is remembered as the external arising of a phoneme.

6.s:
iti pañcāśikā seyaṃ varṇānāṃ paricarcitā /
ekonāṃ ye tu tāmāhustanmataṃ saṃpracakṣmahe // 249
6.d:
इति पञ्चाशिका सेयं वर्णानां परिचर्चिता ।
एकोनां ये तु तामाहुस्तन्मतं संप्रचक्ष्महे ॥ 249
6.m: Thus has this set of fifty phonemes been discussed; / as for those who speak of forty-nine, we now set forth their view:

6.s:
vedāścārāḥ pañcamāṃśanyūnaṃ cārārdhamekaśaḥ /
varṇe'dhikaṃ taddviguṇamavibhāge divāniśoḥ // 250
6.d:
वेदाश्चाराः पञ्चमांशन्यूनं चारार्धमेकशः ।
वर्णेऽधिकं तद्द्विगुणमविभागे दिवानिशोः ॥ 250
6.m: Four movements, plus half a movement minus one-fifth, individually / in addition for each phoneme; twice that in the non-differentiation of day and night.

6.s: sthūlo varṇodayaḥ so'yaṃ purā sūkṣmo nigadyate // 251
6.d: स्थूलो वर्णोदयः सोऽयं पुरा सूक्ष्मो निगद्यते ॥ 251
6.m: That is the gross arising of phonemes; the subtle one was stated earlier.

6.s: iti kālatattvamuditaṃ śāstramukhāgamanijānubhavasiddham // 252
6.d: इति कालतत्त्वमुदितं शास्त्रमुखागमनिजानुभवसिद्धम् ॥ 252
6.m: Thus the principle of time has been expounded, established from the mouth of the scriptures, the Agamas, and personal experience.
